companies.name: Intricately
companies.description: Intricately is a cloud and technology spend intelligence platform that tracks the adoption, usage, and spend of more than 15,000 cloud products across millions of companies worldwide, giving sales and marketing teams the signals they need to find accounts, spot active sales cycles, and predict churn. Founded in 2014 in San Francisco and backed by Bloomberg Beta, GitHub, Susa Ventures, and Singtel Innov8, Intricately was acquired by HG Insights in March 2022 and its data product is now delivered as the Cloud Dynamics API. The REST API (https://api.intricately.com/api/v2) authenticates with an X-API-KEY header and centers on asynchronous Bulk Jobs that enrich lists of domains with cloud adoption, product signatures, revenue, and digital-relationship data. API access is available on Enterprise plans.

companies.name: Nimble Storage
companies.description: Nimble Storage is an enterprise flash and adaptive-flash storage platform, acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise in 2017 and now part of the HPE Nimble Storage / HPE Alletra 6000 product line. Its NimbleOS software exposes a REST API for programmatic management of arrays, storage pools, volumes, snapshots, initiator groups, and data-protection policies. The API is served per-array at https://<array>:5392/v1/ using session-token (X-Auth-Token) authentication, and HPE publishes first-party Python, Go, and Ansible client libraries for it. Originally venture-backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was added to the API Evangelist network and enriched from its public developer surface.

companies.name: Shift Technology
companies.description: Shift Technology is an insurance-focused artificial intelligence company that builds purpose-built AI agents automating critical insurance workflows, including claims processing and automation, fraud and financial-crime detection, coverage assessment, subrogation, and payment integrity. Founded in Paris and now operating globally, Shift serves 120+ insurance customers across more than 30 countries and has analyzed billions of policies, claims, and supporting documents. Shift deploys as cloud SaaS and integrates with insurer core systems through its technology, data, and service partner programs. The company does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or self-service developer portal; integrations are delivered as enterprise engagements. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the artifacts here capture the company's public security, compliance, and domain posture rather than a public API.

companies.name: Zyte
companies.description: Zyte is a web data extraction platform providing APIs, smart proxy management, and AI-powered data extraction built on the Scrapy framework.

companies.name: City National Bank
companies.description: City National Bank is a national bank chartered in the United States and a wholly owned subsidiary of Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) since 2015, headquartered in Los Angeles, California and known historically as "the bank to the stars" for its deep roots in the entertainment industry. With roughly $98 billion in assets, it is an FDIC-insured, super-regional institution offering personal, business, and private banking, wealth management, treasury management, and capital markets services, with industry expertise across entertainment, healthcare, real estate, technology, and law. City National operates as CN Bank in Florida. It runs NO first-party public developer portal or documented public API: developer.cnb.com and developers.cnb.com do not resolve and api.cnb.com returns 404. Consistent with the voluntary, fragmented US open-finance model, consumer-permissioned account data is reached through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a direct City National API. As a covered depository institution it falls under the emerging CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule, but no City-National-specific 1033 or FDX participation posture is publicly documented. Its Canadian parent RBC runs a separate developer portal (developer.rbc.com) under a different charter that does not expose City National Bank APIs.

companies.name: Linte
companies.description: Linte is a Brazilian legal-technology company offering an AI-powered contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform for large enterprises. Its product family spans Linte CLM for document automation and contract lifecycle governance, Linte AI for contract review that summarizes versions and flags risk against a customer playbook, Linte BI for contract analytics dashboards, and Linte Intake for legal demand intake and triage. The platform integrates natively with digital signature providers including ClickSign, DocuSign and D4Sign, and is sold to enterprise legal, procurement and compliance teams primarily in Brazil. Linte publishes no public API program, developer portal or API reference; its only public developer-facing artifacts are npm-published embeddable "Linte Docs" form components.

companies.name: Sweep
companies.description: Sweep is the agentic layer for enterprise systems. By connecting to platforms like Salesforce, Snowflake, ServiceNow, and HubSpot, Sweep reads live metadata and gives AI agents the context they need to understand, plan, and govern changes safely across complex systems. It unifies discovery, design, and build into one continuous workflow — auto-generating living documentation of every flow, field, and rule; visualizing end-to-end business processes; running metadata agents that audit and optimize org configuration; and shipping Salesforce automations, lead routing, alerts, and deduplication without custom code. Sweep also publishes an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects Salesforce context to AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. Sweep is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Homebrew, and Insight Partners.

companies.name: Entytle
companies.description: Entytle, Inc. (founded 2014, Austin, Texas) provides an Installed Base Intelligence SaaS platform for equipment manufacturers (OEMs). It unifies fragmented data from ERP, CRM, FSM systems, and spreadsheets into a single "Source of Truth" for an OEM's installed base, then applies purpose-built AI and a Data Quality Engine to surface aftermarket revenue opportunities, predict parts/service/upgrade needs, and prevent customer churn. Products include Aftermarket IQ (IB 360, Customer Central, Customer Loyalty Manager, Predictive Opportunities, Wallet Share Assessment), an AI Quote Agent, Asset Lifecycle Management, IB HealthCheck, and a Data Quality Engine. Customers include Johnson Controls, Baker Hughes, Xylem, GEA, Dematic, Duravant, and Peerless Pump. Surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and enriched from Entytle's public surface; Entytle exposes an enterprise application (Entytle Insyghts) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK.

companies.name: EverBank
companies.description: EverBank, N.A. is a Jacksonville, Florida based national bank (Member FDIC) focused on high-yield consumer deposits, business and treasury banking, and commercial lending, serving customers nationwide online plus a small network of financial centers in Florida, California and New York. The bank operated as TIAA Bank from 2017 until 2023, when it was acquired by an investor group and reverted to the EverBank brand as an independent institution. Like most US banks, EverBank publishes NO first-party public developer API or developer portal; there is no documented open-banking, FDX, or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API exposed directly. Consumer-permissioned account data is reached only through third-party aggregators (e.g. Plaid, MX, Finicity), which is the honest, non-fabricated posture recorded here.

companies.name: Aizon
companies.description: Aizon is a B2B SaaS manufacturing-intelligence platform for GxP pharmaceutical manufacturers and CDMOs. It turns process data into AI-driven recommendations to increase yield, reduce deviations, and prevent batch loss without replacing existing MES, LIMS, ERP, or historian systems. The platform spans four connected products: Aizon Execute (intelligent electronic batch records), Aizon Unify (a GxP manufacturing data platform / lakehouse), Aizon Predict (operationalized ML for yield optimization, CPV, and predictive quality), and Aizon Agentic Studio (a natural-language application and dashboard builder). Aizon runs single-tenant on AWS with ALCOA++ data integrity, 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures, and a GxP model lifecycle, and exposes a RESTful API to customers. Offices in San Francisco, USA and Barcelona, Spain.

companies.name: CoStar Group
companies.description: CoStar Group is the dominant commercial and residential real estate data, analytics, and marketplace company. The portfolio spans the flagship CoStar commercial real estate intelligence platform, LoopNet (CRE marketplace), Apartments.com network (residential rentals, including ForRent.com and Westside Rentals), Homes.com and Homesnap (for-sale residential), Ten-X (online CRE auctions), BizBuySell (business-for-sale marketplace), STR (hotel data), Visual Lease (lease management), Matterport (3D spatial capture), and international properties including OnTheMarket (UK), Emporis (Germany), and a controlling stake in Domain Group (Australia). Distribution to partners is via enterprise data licensing, syndication feeds, and brand-specific marketplace tooling rather than a public self-serve developer portal.

companies.name: HData
companies.description: HData is the AI-native operating system for energy regulation. Founded in 2018 by Hudson Hollister, the platform turns disconnected federal and state regulatory filings, dockets, and proceedings from sources such as FERC, EIA, and state utility commissions into standardized, citable, machine-readable data. It combines centralized regulatory data, domain-specific AI trained on more than 20 million citable documents, and purpose-built tools — including HData Analytics, Regulatory Intelligence, Gateway for FERC data extraction, and Data Request Management — to help utilities, regulators, advocates, advisory firms, financial institutions, and large energy customers accelerate rate cases, resource planning, compliance reporting, and policy research.

companies.name: Nextdata
companies.description: Nextdata OS is a unified, automated data management platform for unstructured and structured data, designed for AI and analytics workloads. Founded by Zhamak Dehghani (creator of the data mesh paradigm), Nextdata enables organizations to build autonomous data products with embedded governance and discovery.

companies.name: Racing Data
companies.description: Racing Data is a developer-focused API providing real-time updates and historical statistics across racing series, including Formula One, IndyCar, and others. It is intended for building custom data sets and analytics experiences on top of motorsports data.

companies.name: Red Planet Labs
companies.description: Red Planet Labs builds Rama, a unified platform for constructing end-to-end scalable backends in as little as 1/100th the code of traditional stacks. Rama integrates durable indexed data storage (PStates), computation, and background processing into a single JVM programming model (Java and Clojure) with ACID semantics, automatic scaling, replication, and fine-grained reactivity — replacing the usual sprawl of databases, queues, caches, and workers. Rama ships a built-in REST API for non-JVM clients and is self-hosted, free for clusters up to two nodes. Backed by Initialized Capital.

companies.name: Harbr
companies.description: Harbr is a white-label external data-sharing, exchange, and marketplace platform that lets organizations reveal, build, and manage a data ecosystem for external collaboration and commercial data distribution. The platform provides data discovery and cataloging, subscription-based access governance, secure data delivery to external environments and AI systems, and audit trails for compliance. It deploys across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Databricks, and connects to Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Looker, and Power BI. Harbr exposes REST APIs and event-driven webhooks for automating data exchanges, though the technical API reference is published in an invite-only Operator Documentation portal. Harbr is backed by Seedcamp.

companies.name: Instrumental
companies.description: Instrumental is a platform for manufacturing intelligence that helps companies detect and prevent product failures during the manufacturing process. The Instrumental API enables programmatic access to retrieve unit and inspection test data and metadata from Instrumental projects.

companies.name: Scrapy
companies.description: Scrapy is an open-source Python web crawling framework for extracting structured data from websites using spiders and built-in data pipelines.

companies.name: Summation
companies.description: Summation is an enterprise AI analyst platform that automates recurring business work — financial reviews, forecasts, models, and executive-ready decks — by connecting to a company's data sources (ERPs, data warehouses, and spreadsheets) and producing verified, source-traced reports in the format teams already use. Its AI agent "Addison" runs playbooks across finance, operations, and sales, tracing every number back to its source so outputs are audit-ready and SOC 2 Type II compliant. Founded by Ian Wong (CEO) and Ramachandran "RC" Ramarathinam (CTO), formerly of Opendoor, Summation is backed by Battery Ventures. The company operates a customer application, product documentation, and a public Trust Center, but does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

companies.name: connectFirst Credit Union
companies.description: connectFirst Credit Union is a member-owned, cooperative (Schedule-equivalent provincial credit union) financial institution headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, formed on May 3, 2021 by amalgamating four Alberta credit unions (First Calgary Financial, Chinook Financial, Mountain View Financial, and Legacy Financial). At its peak it held over CAD $6 billion in assets under administration and served more than 128,000 members across 41 branches in Central and Southern Alberta, offering retail, commercial, agricultural, and dealer-services banking. Members voted in November 2023 to merge with Servus Credit Union; the legal amalgamation closed May 1, 2024 as "Connect First and Servus Credit Union Ltd." (~CAD $29.3B assets, 600,000+ members), and the unified brand realigned to Servus Credit Union in January 2025 — the connectfirstcu.com domain now 301-redirects to servus.ca. Its open-finance posture is honest and typical of a Canadian credit union: no first-party public developer portal or downloadable OpenAPI, digital banking delivered via the Celero Xpress platform (powered by ebankIT) with core/banking-tech through the Central 1 / Celero cooperative ecosystem, and third-party consumer data access available only through aggregators (Plaid coverage confirmed). Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / FCAC-overseen) is legislated but not yet operational, so no mandated open-banking API exists.

companies.name: Pachyderm
companies.description: Pachyderm is an open-source (Apache-2.0) platform for data-centric pipelines and data versioning, widely used for MLOps. It provides immutable, git-like data lineage through the Pachyderm File System (PFS) and data-driven, containerized pipelines that reprocess only changed data through the Pachyderm Pipeline System (PPS), all running on Kubernetes. The platform is driven by a gRPC/protobuf API with first-party Python, Go, Ruby and Rust clients and the pachctl command-line tool. Pachyderm was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise in January 2023; the standalone marketing, documentation and hosted (Pachyderm Hub) sites have since been retired, but the source, releases, SDKs and CLI remain actively published on GitHub and the language package registries (latest release v2.12.2, January 2025).

companies.name: Pantomath
companies.description: Pantomath is an AI-powered Data Operations Center that monitors, manages, and automatically resolves issues across an organization's entire data analytics ecosystem. The platform combines 24/7 automated data monitoring, cross-platform data lineage and impact analysis, AI-driven incident detection, and autonomous root-cause analysis and remediation to deliver full self-resolution of issues across the data stack. Pantomath integrates with 60+ platforms spanning data warehouses (Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery, Databricks), orchestration (Airflow, dbt, Astronomer), integration (Fivetran, Informatica, Matillion), BI/reporting (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Sigma), and notification channels (Slack, Teams, PagerDuty). It exposes a first-party API-key-authenticated ingestion API and a published JavaScript SDK for sending custom real-time job and dataset logs. Backed by General Catalyst (Series B, $30M) and Snowflake Ventures.

companies.name: Caya
companies.description: Caya (Caya GmbH, Berlin) is a German intelligent document processing (IDP) company whose Document Automation Suite digitizes, classifies, and routes business documents end to end. Its core capabilities are Post Scan (physical mail intake with OCR and automatic classification), Document Extractions (AI-powered structured data extraction), and Document Automations (rule-based routing and distribution into downstream systems). Caya connects to 100+ tools across accounting, ERP, HR, cloud storage, and e-signature, and hosts data in a high-security Frankfurt data center. It is certified and compliant against ISO 27001, GDPR/DSGVO, DORA, GoBD, and German HGB/AO retention rules, with a public Vanta-hosted trust center. Surfaced as an HV Capital portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Librato
companies.description: Librato was a hosted metrics, monitoring and analytics service for operational data — time-series measurements, tagged metrics, dashboards ("spaces"), charts, annotations, alerts and notification services — delivered as a developer-first SaaS with a JSON REST API at metrics-api.librato.com/v1. Backed by Cowboy Ventures among others, the San Francisco company was acquired by SolarWinds in 2015 for a reported $40 million, and its metrics platform was folded into SolarWinds AppOptics — released in November 2017 — which has itself since reached end of life. The librato.com domain and every product subdomain (metrics., status., www.) now 301-redirect to the SolarWinds AppOptics end-of-life notice, the metrics-api.librato.com API host no longer resolves in DNS, and the github.com/librato organization was archived on 2024-01-02. This profile is retained as a historical record of a well-regarded developer API: the API reference source, the first-party Ruby, Python, Java and Node client libraries and the collection agents remain publicly archived and are catalogued here. The successor product is SolarWinds Observability SaaS.

companies.name: Strawberry
companies.description: Strawberry is an agentic web browser for macOS with AI companions that work inside it: you describe an outcome and a companion operates the open web on your behalf — logged in as you, across many tabs — to research, extract data, fill forms, draft messages, and run multi-step work end to end ("Do hours of work in minutes"). Companions are persistent AI teammates you brief once; Routines run work on a schedule; Skills save a workflow to re-run in one line; Integrations let companions act across apps you are already signed into (Gmail, Google Sheets, Notion, Slack, Stripe, and more). It keeps a human in control, asking approval before consequential actions. Distributed as a desktop app, metered in credits. Backed by EQT Ventures and General Catalyst. Strawberry publishes no public REST/OpenAPI developer API as of this profiling; its surface is the consumer app plus web documentation, a security program, and machine-readable llms.txt and security.txt.

companies.name: REalyse
companies.description: REalyse is a UK residential property data platform that aggregates more than 100 data sources into geospatial analysis and market-intelligence tools for developers, lenders, investors, consultants, and funds. Its data spans five domains — Planning & Policy, Demographics, Market (rental and sales pricing, yields, days on market, comparables), Land & Ownership, and Amenities. REalyse offers a data API for institutions that require a constant feed of property data, alongside the REalyse Core geospatial platform, the REalyse Pulse consumer AI valuation product, and downloadable Market Intelligence reports. The company is based in London and is backed by Anthemis. API access is onboarded through the sales team rather than a self-service developer portal, so no public OpenAPI, base URL, or authentication reference is published.

companies.name: Urban SDK
companies.description: Urban SDK is a geospatial AI and data analytics company serving the public sector, delivering hourly road-speed and traffic data, analytics, and AI tools that help cities, counties, and transportation agencies prioritize issues, pinpoint trends, and act on traffic management, public safety, emergency response, and infrastructure planning. A Techstars portfolio company based in Jacksonville, Florida, Urban SDK delivers its data through a web platform and automated Workflows reports rather than a public API, and currently publishes no developer documentation or client SDKs.

companies.name: Canadian Tire Bank
companies.description: Canadian Tire Bank (operating as Canadian Tire Financial Services) is a federally regulated Schedule I bank, wholly owned by Canadian Tire Corporation, Limited and federally chartered in 2003. Headquartered in Oakville, Ontario with operations in St. Catharines and Welland, the bank is the financial-services arm of one of Canada's best-known retailers. It issues the Triangle Mastercard, Triangle World Mastercard, Triangle World Elite Mastercard, Gas Advantage and Cash Advantage Mastercards, and offers high-interest savings accounts and GICs, all tied to the Triangle Rewards loyalty program. On open finance, the bank exposes no first-party public developer API or banking API portal. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, overseen by the FCAC) is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer data access today is voluntary and aggregator-based — Canadian Tire Bank card and account data is reached through aggregators such as Finicity (by Mastercard), Flinks and Plaid rather than a first-party API. The cantire.com developer portal is run by the retail parent Canadian Tire Corporation, not the bank, is gated behind sign-in, and its TLS certificate expired in February 2026.

companies.name: Coast Capital Savings
companies.description: Coast Capital Savings is a member-owned financial co-operative headquartered in Surrey, British Columbia, serving over 600,000 members across roughly 45 branches. On November 1, 2018 it became Canada's first British Columbia-based federal credit union (regulated federally rather than provincially), and in May 2026 it completed a merger with Prospera Credit Union. With approximately $21.9 billion CAD in total assets it is one of Canada's largest credit unions. As a cooperative credit union rather than a Schedule I/II bank, Coast Capital operates within Canada's voluntary and still-fragmented open-finance landscape: the federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework legislated under Budget 2024 and the Fall Economic Statement 2024, with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) as overseer, is not yet operational. Coast Capital publishes NO public first-party developer portal or documented API; consumer financial-data access today is aggregator-mediated (e.g. Plaid) via screen-scraping/credential-based connections rather than a first-party API.

companies.name: ObjectBox
companies.description: ObjectBox is a high-performance, low-footprint, offline-first on-device database with built-in data synchronization and on-device vector search, designed for mobile, IoT, embedded, and edge computing applications. It is delivered as native language bindings (Java, Kotlin, C/C++, Go, Swift, Flutter/Dart, and Python) rather than a hosted REST API, giving apps ACID-compliant local persistence that works reliably offline and is described as up to 10x faster than SQLite. ObjectBox was the first on-device vector database on the market, targeting Edge AI use cases such as semantic search, recommendations, and retrieval-augmented generation, and offers optional bi-directional Data Sync between devices and the cloud, including a direct connector to MongoDB. Founded in Germany and backed by Techstars.

companies.name: sophiagenetics
companies.description: SOPHiA GENETICS (NASDAQ SOPH) is a healthcare technology company democratizing data-driven medicine through its cloud-based SOPHiA DDM Platform, which analyzes genomic, radiomic, and multimodal data to support clinicians and researchers across oncology, hereditary disorders, rare diseases, and precision medicine. The platform spans SOPHiA DDM for Genomics, Multimodal, and Radiomics, plus Alamut Visual Plus for variant interpretation and the OncoPortal knowledge base. The product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS platform; no public developer API or portal is currently published.

companies.name: UrbanFootprint
companies.description: UrbanFootprint is a resilient decision intelligence platform that delivers urban, climate, and community-resilience data and analytics, helping governments, utilities, financial institutions, and planners assess risk and make data-driven decisions. Its platform spans scenario analysis (Analyst), map-based data exploration (Explorer), and curated data subscriptions covering climate hazards, the built environment, and social vulnerability. UrbanFootprint is a closed SaaS platform sold via sales contact and publishes no public developer API; its application authenticates through Auth0 and consumes an internal platform API.

companies.name: Valerie Health
companies.description: Valerie Health is an AI-powered front office platform for independent healthcare provider groups, automating referral management, fax and document classification and data extraction, appointment scheduling, and growth analytics on top of existing EMR and practice management systems. Founded by Pete Shalek and Nitin Joshi and backed by General Catalyst and Redpoint Ventures with a $30M Series A, the company operates as a HIPAA Business Associate for its provider customers and publishes a Vanta-hosted trust center, but does not currently publish a developer portal or public API documentation.

companies.name: Wynd Network
companies.description: Wynd Network (now operating as Wynd Labs) is the company behind Grass, a decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) on Solana that rewards users for sharing their unused internet bandwidth. The Grass Network routes and verifies web traffic through a network of nodes, routers, and validators to collect and structure public web data for AI training and business intelligence. Grass ships consumer apps and a node network rather than a public developer API; its documentation covers network architecture, the GRASS token, staking, and points.

companies.name: Jellyfish
companies.description: Jellyfish is a software engineering intelligence (SEI) platform that turns data from developer tools — issue trackers (Jira, Linear, Azure Boards), source control and CI/CD (GitHub, Azure DevOps), and AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Amazon Q, Gemini Code Assist) — into productivity and business-impact insights for R&D leaders. The platform measures AI adoption, engineering allocation, and delivery across the software development lifecycle through a Data Hub, extensible dashboards, and AI-assisted custom queries. Jellyfish is an enterprise, demo-gated product with no public self-service API; data access is delivered through the product and its integrations rather than a documented developer API. Backed by Accel, Insight Partners, and Wing Venture Capital.

companies.name: Rhythmos
companies.description: Rhythmos (rhythmos.io) provides modern analytics for managing electric-vehicle charging and grid infrastructure. Its platform coordinates fleet charging needs against utility and wholesale market conditions to lower energy costs and defer costly grid infrastructure investment, serving EV fleet owners, utilities, municipalities, and market aggregators through Fleet, Grid, and Market applications. Rhythmos maintains a SOC 2 Type II report and is GDPR compliant. The company is now part of Electron (electron.net). No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity, website properties, and security/compliance posture.

companies.name: Von
companies.description: Von (vonlabs.ai) is an AI RevOps agent from Rattle Software, the Insight Partners and Sequoia backed team behind gorattle.com, positioned as an AI data scientist for revenue teams. Von connects to CRMs, data warehouses, call recorders, and sales engagement tools - Salesforce, HubSpot, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Gong, Outreach, Salesloft, and more, plus 100+ integrations consumed via MCP - to automate pipeline forecasting, win/loss analysis, churn detection, sales coaching, and Salesforce administration. Von publishes no public API or developer program; its security posture is documented at trust.vonlabs.ai (SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001, CASA Tier 2).

companies.name: Aviso
companies.description: Aviso is an end-to-end AI revenue platform that combines agentic AI, revenue forecasting, conversation intelligence, relationship intelligence, pipeline inspection, and unified RevOps capabilities to help go-to-market teams predict, guide, and simplify every revenue action. It offers role-specific AI agents, a no-code GTM Agent Studio, sales engagement and coaching, and a mobile revenue command center, with vertical solutions for Pharma and Life Sciences, Financial Services, and Technology. Aviso is SOC 2 Type II audited and GDPR compliant, and is backed by Bloomberg Beta and Cowboy Ventures.

companies.name: Bigfinite
companies.description: Bigfinite (now Aizon) is a B2B SaaS provider of AI-powered manufacturing intelligence for pharmaceutical manufacturers and CDMOs. The platform turns GxP manufacturing process data into ML-driven recommendations to improve yield, reduce deviations, and prevent batch loss without replacing existing MES, LIMS, or historian systems. Its product stack spans Aizon Execute (intelligent electronic batch records), Aizon Unify (a GxP manufacturing data platform with ALCOA++ integrity), Aizon Predict (operationalized ML for yield optimization, CPV, and predictive quality), and Aizon Agentic Studio (a natural-language application builder). Aizon runs single-tenant on AWS and maintains ISO 27001, ISO 27017, SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, and EU GMP Annex 11 compliance. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from public web surfaces; the company publishes no public API.

companies.name: Netezza
companies.description: IBM Netezza Performance Server is a cloud-native data warehouse and analytics appliance for running large-scale SQL analytics and in-database machine learning on structured data. Originally a standalone data-warehouse appliance vendor acquired by IBM, Netezza is now delivered as Netezza Performance Server on IBM Cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure and as part of IBM Cloud Pak for Data. It is consumed primarily through SQL over standard database connectivity — the pure-Python nzpy DB-API 2.0 driver, JDBC (nzjdbc) and ODBC drivers, and the nzpyida in-database analytics library — rather than as a public REST API, with a REST interface for backup/restore administration and a web console for monitoring and administration.

companies.name: Aleph
companies.description: Aleph is an AI-native financial planning & analysis (FP&A) platform for finance teams that want live data, spreadsheet-native workflows, automated reporting, and AI-assisted analysis in one system. It consolidates data from ERP, HRIS, CRM, billing, and databases through 200+ no-code connectors, offers bi-directional Excel and Google Sheets add-ins, web dashboards, and an AI layer (Aleph Intelligence, Aleph Agent, AI Variance Analysis, AI Mappings). Aleph also ships an Aleph Agent MCP integration that brings governed financial data to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible tools. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures; SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certified.

companies.name: Concourse
companies.description: Concourse builds AI agents for corporate finance teams. Its platform lets finance, accounting, and data teams query financial data in natural language, generate board and investor reporting with commentary, and run forecasts and scenarios against real-time data. Concourse connects natively to financial and operational systems including QuickBooks, NetSuite, Ramp, Snowflake, Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe, Brex, Rippling, Gusto, BigQuery, and Databricks, and says it cuts manual finance work by over 75%. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and backed by CRV, raising a $12M Series A alongside general availability. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Cyberwrite
companies.description: Cyberwrite is an AI-powered cyber insurance intelligence platform, founded in 2017, that turns raw data into explainable, defensible financial decisions for the cyber insurance market. Its proprietary 4SEEN AI engine assesses cyber risk, forecasts breaches, simulates financial impact, and recommends mitigation, giving brokers, carriers, reinsurers, MGAs, ILS investors, and corporates access to cyber risk analytics, catastrophe modeling, and risk quantification on more than 100 million companies worldwide in seconds and in eight languages. Cyberwrite delivers its scoring and analytics through an enterprise API for real-time aggregated risk management; the platform is a Gartner Cool Vendor and DIA Top 100 InsurTech, and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company.

The company is ISO 27001 certified and GDPR compliant. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: OPGG
companies.description: OP.GG is the world's leading League of Legends statistics and performance tracking platform. Founded in Seoul, South Korea and launched in 2013, it grew from a LoL stats search engine into a global gaming platform serving tens of millions of monthly active users across games including League of Legends, Valorant, Teamfight Tactics, Overwatch 2, and PUBG. OP.GG surfaces summoner ranks, win rates, champion mastery, builds, tier lists, match history, and live meta trends. Its programmatic surface centers on an official, hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives AI agents access to LoL, TFT, and Valorant game data, plus first-party AI-readable ai.json summoner/match snapshot endpoints advertised in its published llms.txt. OP.GG is backed by 500 Global, SBVA, DS Asset Management, Dunamu & Partners, and others.

companies.description: Queensland Government Data is a open data portal open-data portal for Australia running CKAN. companies.name: Channel99
companies.description: Channel99 is a B2B marketing performance and attribution platform founded by Demandbase creator Chris Golec. It uses AI and first-party account identification to unify cross-channel marketing results, verify B2B ad delivery, reveal the "dark funnel" and view-through traffic, and benchmark vendor and channel performance against the industry, then recommend budget and campaign changes that grow pipeline while reducing wasted spend. Marketing and RevOps teams export unified performance data into data warehouses (Snowflake), CDPs, and BI tools, and activate intent-based audiences. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Jackson Square Ventures, Industry Ventures, Ridge Ventures, Geek Ventures, and Marin-Sonoma Impact Ventures.

companies.name: Azure Notebooks
companies.description: Azure Notebooks was a free hosted service to develop and run Jupyter notebooks in the cloud with no installation required. The service was retired on October 9, 2020. Users are recommended to migrate to Azure Machine Learning, Visual Studio Code with Jupyter extension, or GitHub Codespaces for equivalent functionality.

companies.name: Evertune
companies.description: Evertune is a Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and AI brand-intelligence platform that helps brands, marketers, and agencies understand, measure, and influence how they appear in AI-driven recommendations. As discovery shifts from traditional search engines to conversational answer engines like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity, Evertune tracks brand visibility and sentiment across 10+ AI models, analyzes how large language models describe a brand versus its competitors, and delivers prescriptive message and content briefs to improve that positioning. The platform combines large-scale prompt testing (100,000+ prompt responses per report via direct base-model API access), the EverPanel consumer panel, daily consumer-app data, an AI Brand Index and AI Brand Score, content activation, and AI advertising. Founded in 2024 by operators who helped scale The Trade Desk, Evertune is backed by Felicis and serves customers including Roku, WPP, athenahealth, and HexClad. Evertune is a data consumer of the major model APIs; it does not currently publish a first-party developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI.

companies.name: 7 Chord
companies.description: 7 Chord is a New York-based financial technology company providing AI-driven, real-time pricing and analytics for fixed income (corporate bond) markets. Its flagship engine, BondDroid, ingests 100 million-plus data points per day - firm and indicative quotes, post-trade prints, and macro and country risk factors - and distills them into risk-neutral bid, ask, and mid prices, yields, and option-adjusted spreads, including for thinly traded bonds. Founded in 2017, 7 Chord delivers BondDroid pricing in streaming, delayed, and historical bulk formats, and can run behind a client's firewall so proprietary data never leaves their environment. Its pricing powers platforms including Broadridge's LTX, TS Imagine, and PortfolioBI, and is distributed through partners such as Bonds.com and Dewey Data.

companies.name: Aris Machina
companies.description: Aris Machina builds AI-powered industrial software for advanced manufacturing, describing its mission as delivering "industrial superintelligence" that unifies design, production, and operations through AI agents and a shared semantic knowledge model. Its products include Protos, an AI co-engineer for R&D teams that accelerates design validation and simulation; Gemba, shopfloor operational agents that provide real-time equipment diagnostics; and the Ontology Toolkit, a knowledge-integration layer that bridges data across MES, ERP, and PLM systems. Aris Machina serves batteries, biopharma, robotics, defense, and aerospace, and is backed by Earlybird. The company operates from Stockholm, Bangalore, and California. This profile was surfaced as an Earlybird portfolio company and enriched from public web sources; Aris Machina does not currently publish a public developer API surface, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

companies.name: Databand
companies.description: DBND (Databand) is an open-source Python framework — a library, a set of APIs, and a CLI — for building, tracking, and observing data pipelines across data ingestion, preparation, ETL/ELT, and machine-learning workflows. It collects pipeline metadata (runs, metrics, dataframes, schemas) to give data-engineering teams a system of record for runs and to detect pipeline failures and data quality issues before they hit downstream consumers. The DBND SDK integrates with Apache Airflow, Apache Spark, Databricks, dbt, and IBM DataStage. Databand was acquired by IBM in 2022 and is now IBM Databand, part of IBM's data observability offering; the open-source DBND SDK remains published on PyPI and GitHub under the databand-ai organization.

companies.name: DataPeople
companies.description: Datapeople is an AI-powered job description management platform (acquired by PayScale) that helps talent and recruiting teams centralize, standardize, and optimize their job content across the hiring workflow. Its products include a Smart Editor for job-content management, a First Draft writing AI, Insights performance and compliance analytics, Guidance and Compliance AI for review and recommendations, and Datapeople Anywhere, which surfaces its guidance inside existing ATS and HRIS systems. Datapeople integrates with applicant tracking systems including Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Greenhouse, SmartRecruiters, iCIMS, Lever, and Gr8People. The company publishes no public developer API, portal, or OpenAPI; its integration surface is delivered through native ATS/HRIS connectors rather than a self-serve API.

companies.name: Directus
companies.description: Open-source data platform that wraps any SQL database with a REST and GraphQL API, auto-generated from the schema, plus a no-code admin app for data management. Directus turns any new or existing SQL database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MS SQL, OracleDB, CockroachDB) into an instant REST and GraphQL API with a visual Data Studio for non-technical users. The platform includes policy-based access control, an automation engine (Flows), a built-in AI assistant, digital asset management, real-time WebSockets, and an MCP server for AI agent integration. Deployable as a self-hosted open-source project or as Directus Cloud.

companies.name: Metamarkets Group
companies.description: Metamarkets was a real-time analytics platform for programmatic advertising, giving ad exchanges, SSPs, DSPs, and ad networks interactive dashboards over billions of daily bid, impression, click, and spend events. Its Real-time Data Ingestion (RDI) API accepted continuous streams of OpenRTB-based JSON event records over authenticated HTTPS POST, surfacing them in the Metamarkets dashboard within seconds. Founded in 2010 and the birthplace of the Druid analytics database (now Apache Druid), Metamarkets was acquired by Snap Inc. in 2017; its successor products live on as Rill Data. This profile enriches the dcvc portfolio lead from the surviving public documentation at docs.metamarkets.com.

companies.name: One Model
companies.description: One Model is an HR and people-analytics software platform that unifies fragmented workforce data from HRIS, ATS, payroll, engagement, performance, and finance systems into a governed data mesh, then applies AI to turn it into insights for HR leaders and executives. Its products include Data Mesh (unify, govern, and activate data across sources), Data Stories (dashboards and reporting), One AI (a transparent predictive-modeling pipeline plus a natural-language assistant), and enterprise AI connections — including an MCP Server Access option — that let governed people data feed tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot, and Claude with role-based access controls. One Model is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 Type II attested, and adheres to GDPR data-processor requirements.

companies.name: TRDATA
companies.description: TRDATA (TRDATA Technology Limited) is a real-time financial information and communication platform for professional traders, aggregating over-the-counter (OTC) quotes, prices, news, and analytics from market makers across fragmented fixed-income and emerging-market instruments. It covers Ukrainian, CEEMEA, and global bonds, currencies, commodities, and derivatives from local and international data providers, and bundles analytics tools such as a Bond Calculator, Bond Calendar, Swap Curves, real-time asset charts, and a TRDATA Excel add-in. More than 800 institutions -- including Societe Generale, UniCredit, Raiffeisen, BNP Paribas, Barclays, Deutsche Bank, and Commerzbank -- use the platform to read and exchange market information. TRDATA is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; access is via registration and the hosted platform.

companies.name: ABILITY Network (Inovalon)
companies.description: ABILITY Network is a healthcare SaaS business acquired by Inovalon in 2018 and now delivered as part of the cloud-based Inovalon ONE Platform. It provides US healthcare providers with software for medical billing and claims management, eligibility verification, revenue cycle management, clinical quality reporting, patient access, and workforce/staffing and care coordination. Inovalon pairs these provider-facing applications with large national datasets and analytics to support data-driven healthcare across payers, providers, pharmacies, and life-sciences organizations. Developer access to Inovalon ONE APIs is offered through the authenticated Inovalon developer portal at developer.inovalonone.com, which exposes sandbox, staging, and live environments.

It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 150 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

companies.name: Upsolver
companies.description: Upsolver is a cloud data ingestion and lakehouse pipeline company whose SQLake platform lets teams build and deploy high-scale streaming data pipelines using familiar SQL, with automatic schema evolution and Apache Iceberg optimization. Upsolver was acquired by Qlik and the product now continues as Qlik Open Lakehouse; the standalone Upsolver (SQLake) product is legacy, with documentation maintained under Qlik's help site and first-party Python SDK, CLI, and dbt tooling still published on PyPI.

companies.name: US Small Business Administration Open Data
companies.description: US Small Business Administration Open Data is a federal government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 41 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

companies.name: Virginia Open Data
companies.description: Virginia Open Data is a state government open-data portal for United States running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 33,247 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

companies.name: Western Australia Data Catalogue
companies.description: Western Australia Data Catalogue is a state government open-data portal for Australia running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 2,909 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

companies.name: Yokohama City Open Data
companies.description: Yokohama City Open Data is a municipal government open-data portal for Japan running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 657 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

companies.name: PredictionIO
companies.description: Apache PredictionIO is an open source machine learning server that lets developers and data scientists build, deploy, and serve predictive engines as web services. Originally the commercial product prediction.io from TappingStone, it was acquired by Salesforce in 2016, donated to the Apache Software Foundation, and graduated as a top-level Apache project before being retired to the Apache Attic. It exposes a REST-based Event Server for collecting event data and an Engine Query API for real-time predictions, built on Apache Spark, MLlib, HBase, Elasticsearch, and Akka HTTP, with official SDKs for Python, Ruby, PHP, and Scala/Java. This profile enriches the original portfolio-lead stub.

companies.name: Raymond James Bank
companies.description: Raymond James Bank is a Florida-chartered state member bank headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida, and a wholly owned subsidiary of Raymond James Financial, Inc. (NYSE: RJF), a diversified financial services holding company founded in 1962. Supervised by the Federal Reserve and the Florida Office of Financial Regulation, the bank provides securities-based lending, residential mortgages, commercial and industrial and commercial real estate loans, tax-exempt loans, and deposit products (including its Enhanced Savings Program) primarily to Raymond James wealth-management and institutional clients. On open finance, the bank runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable API specifications; consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party aggregators such as Plaid. No FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented for this institution as of this record.

companies.name: Summer 2
companies.description: SummerOS (formerly reached at gosummer.com, which now 308-redirects to summeros.com) is an AI-driven asset-intelligence platform for short-term rental operators, owners, investors, and property managers. It provides professional-grade revenue forecasting, competitive market intelligence, and portfolio-wide performance analytics, plus an AI assistant (Sunny AI), so short-term rental teams can make data-driven pricing and investment decisions instead of relying on spreadsheets. It connects to property-management systems (Guesty, Hospitable, Streamline, Track) rather than exposing a public developer API. Surfaced as a QED Investors portfolio lead and enriched from its live public surface.

companies.name: 42 Technologies
companies.description: 42 Technologies is a retail business-intelligence and reporting platform, founded in 2013, that consolidates omnichannel retail data — point-of-sale, ecommerce, wholesale, and online-marketplace sources — into a single unified dashboard. It provides merchandisers, buyers, and retail executives with more than 100 purpose-built retail metrics, NRF retail-calendar-aware analytics, multi-currency support, and automated reporting, integrating with 100+ systems including Shopify, NetSuite, Amazon, Walmart, Magento, and WooCommerce. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; 42 does not publish a public developer API at this time.

companies.name: Clarisights
companies.description: Clarisights is an enterprise marketing analytics platform that unifies marketing data from channels, web analytics, attribution platforms, and the data warehouse into a single self-service system. Marketing teams explore data, build custom dashboards, and generate trustworthy insights without SQL or data-engineering support, accelerating reporting cycles and reducing manual spreadsheet work. Clarisights also ships a Marketing Data MCP server that connects governed marketing data to AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Gemini, exposing discovery, query, and report-navigation tools scoped by the same workspace access controls as the UI. The platform advertises 50+ connectors, ISO 27001 certification, and SOC 2 Type 2 attestation.

companies.name: Desjardins Group
companies.description: Desjardins Group (Mouvement Desjardins) is the largest cooperative financial group in North America, founded in 1900 in Lévis, Quebec by Alphonse Desjardins. It is a federation of caisses populaires (member-owned credit unions) rather than a share-capital chartered bank, comprising the Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec and its subsidiaries, the caisses in Quebec and the Caisse Desjardins Ontario Credit Union, regulated in Quebec by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). It holds roughly CAD $470 billion in assets and serves more than 7.8 million members and clients with personal, business, wealth-management and insurance products. On open finance, Desjardins publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification; developer.desjardins.com and other API-portal subdomains do not resolve, and consumer financial-data access is delivered today through third-party aggregators (Flinks, Plaid, Finicity, Tink) via screen-scraping/aggregator connectivity rather than a documented Desjardins API. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework is legislated (Budget 2024/2025, overseen by the FCAC) but not yet operational; as a cooperative outside the Big Six, Desjardins may opt in to Phase 1 rather than being mandated.

companies.name: Employee Cycle
companies.description: Employee Cycle is an HR analytics and reporting platform that bills itself as "the first Employee Data Platform." It connects a company's HRIS, ATS, payroll, performance, and engagement systems into one place and turns that data into automated, real-time dashboards and reports covering headcount, turnover, tenure, DEI, and other people metrics. The no-code dashboard and report builder lets non-technical HR teams run multi-dimensional workforce analysis without manual spreadsheets, with a claimed one-day implementation. Employee Cycle integrates with 20+ HR systems (ADP, BambooHR, Greenhouse, Lattice, Rippling, UKG, and more) and is aimed at enterprise HR teams, typically at organizations with 500+ employees. The company is SOC 2 compliant (audited by Sensiba San Filippo, monitored by Drata), GDPR and CCPA aligned, and built on the NIST Cybersecurity Framework. It is backed by the Techstars accelerator and venture funding. Employee Cycle offers pre-built data integrations rather than a public developer REST API; this profile tracks the company's identity and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Ensighten
companies.description: Ensighten is an enterprise tag management, data governance, and client-side website security platform. It gives digital, marketing, and privacy teams centralized control over the third-party tags, scripts, and vendor code that run on their web and mobile properties, enforcing consent and privacy rules (GDPR, CCPA) at the point of data collection. The platform combines server- and client-side tag management, malicious-script and data-leakage detection (client-side security), and consent management. Ensighten was acquired by CHEQ (CHEQ AI Technologies Ltd.) and is now delivered as part of CHEQ's Control & Compliance / Go-to-Market Security suite; the ensighten.com domain 301-redirects to cheq.ai. This company profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline. Ensighten publishes no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; it is a hosted SaaS console (manage.ensighten.com) with a Zendesk-based help center, so most spec-derived artifacts are not applicable.

companies.name: Panorama Education
companies.description: Panorama Education is a K-12 education technology company whose student success platform is used by thousands of school districts to turn student data into action across academics and behavior (MTSS/RTI), universal screening, social- emotional learning (SEL) and survey instruments, attendance, graduation planning, and family and staff engagement. The platform ingests data nightly from 24+ student information systems, learning management systems, and 100+ benchmark and state assessments using the OneRoster standard and secure file transfer. Panorama does not publish a public self-service developer API; integrations are delivered as managed B2B data synchronization. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 attested, 1EdTech Data Privacy certified, ESSA Level II/IV rated, and a Student Privacy Pledge signatory (FERPA/COPPA/PPRA/CCPA aligned).

companies.name: Govini
companies.description: Govini (rebranded to Air, air.ai, in 2026) is a defense-technology and decision-analytics company whose Ark platform combines proprietary defense acquisition data with AI-enabled applications to close the national-security "Readiness Gap" across supply chain, science and technology, production, sustainment, logistics, and modernization missions. Ark holds FedRAMP High authorization and a DISA Impact Level 5 (IL5) Provisional Authorization plus service-level IL5 ATOs, making it a closed, government-authorized SaaS platform rather than a public developer API. Led by CEO Tara Murphy Dougherty and backed by investors including Accel and Bain Capital. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and has been enriched with the provider's real public identity, security posture, and published compliance authorizations.

companies.name: SafeGraph
companies.description: SafeGraph is a geospatial data company that builds and maintains high-quality Point of Interest (POI), building geometry, and geocoded address datasets used for location intelligence, site selection, competitive analysis, and machine-learning models. Its core products are Places (millions of POIs with base, rich, and premium attributes), Geometry (building-footprint polygons), Address (structured geocoded addresses across 25+ countries), and Spend (transaction data). Rather than a hosted REST API, SafeGraph delivers data as bulk parquet files via S3, Snowflake, AWS Data Exchange, CARTO, Databricks, and ArcGIS. Surfaced originally as a Sapphire Ventures portfolio company and enriched here from SafeGraph's public documentation, changelog, and packages.

companies.name: Listings API
companies.description: REST API and agent-native platform for managing business listings, citations, reviews, Google Business Profile posts, and local analytics across major publisher directories (Google, Facebook, Bing, Yelp, TripAdvisor). A facade over Synup's federated GraphQL backend, with first-party Python and Node SDKs, a hosted MCP server, and llms.txt.

companies.name: Biobot
companies.description: Biobot Analytics is a wastewater epidemiology company that operates a wastewater intelligence platform, analyzing sewage samples to detect and track more than 50 human health indicators — including pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, influenza, RSV, measles, norovirus), substances (fentanyl, cocaine, methamphetamine, buprenorphine), and public-health threats (HIV, mpox, poliovirus, Candida auris) — before they surface in conventional reporting. Founded from MIT research and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Biobot serves federal, state, and local government agencies, pharmaceutical and life-sciences companies, and healthcare systems through dashboards, CSV exports, map visualizations, and enterprise data integrations. Biobot does not publish a public self-serve developer API; data access is arranged directly with the company.

companies.name: Civitas Learning
companies.description: Civitas Learning is a higher education technology company whose Student Impact Platform unifies student data, predictive analytics, and coordinated workflows to help colleges and universities improve enrollment, persistence, and completion outcomes. The platform consolidates data from SIS, LMS, CRM, and event systems into a data lakehouse, layers institution-specific predictive models (CivIQ) on top, and surfaces real-time, actionable insights to advisors, faculty, and administrators through products such as Explore, Inspire, Impact, Illume, College Scheduler, Degree Map, and Academic Planning. Civitas Learning serves institutions of all sizes and pairs its software with strategic advisory services. It does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public operational, security, and compliance surface.

companies.name: Veritas Software
companies.description: Veritas Technologies (originally Veritas Software) is an enterprise data management and protection vendor whose products — NetBackup, Alta, Backup Exec, and InfoScale — expose RESTful APIs for automating backup, recovery, storage provisioning, and data governance. NetBackup ships Swagger/OpenAPI-documented REST APIs served from the master server, with first-party code samples published under the VeritasOS GitHub organization. The company runs a public trust and compliance program covering SOC 2, FedRAMP, HIPAA, FIPS 140, GDPR, and CCPA. Accel is among its historical investors.

companies.name: BevSpot
companies.description: BevSpot is a Boston-based food and beverage inventory management platform for restaurants, bars, and hospitality groups. The web application streamlines back-of-house operations including inventory counting, ordering, invoice management, recipe and menu costing, and sales-driven analytics. BevSpot ingests point-of-sale data through integrations with more than a dozen POS systems (Toast, Square, Clover, Lightspeed, SpotOn, NCR Aloha, Upserve, Brink, Lavu, and others), plus accounting and vendor connections (QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics GP, Ottimate, Fintech, US Foods, Sysco). It is a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures. BevSpot does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, commercial, and security surface.

companies.name: Finaloop
companies.description: Finaloop is a real-time, ecommerce-native bookkeeping and accounting platform for direct-to-consumer (DTC) and multichannel brands. It replaces QuickBooks/Xero, human bookkeepers, and integration tooling with automation plus a team of ecommerce accounting experts, delivering always-current financials. Finaloop continuously syncs sales, returns, fees, reimbursements, inventory movements, COGS, and banking across 60+ ecommerce, marketplace, payment, banking, lending, and 3PL integrations (Shopify, Amazon, TikTok Shop, Walmart, PayPal, Stripe, Chase, ShipBob, and more) to produce real-time P&L, balance sheet, and cash-flow statements, inventory analytics, and tax services. Finaloop exposes no public developer API; its APIs are internal connectors to source platforms, so this profile is identity- and posture-focused rather than spec-bearing.

companies.name: Firstory
companies.description: Firstory is a podcast hosting and monetization platform for creators, holding the leading share of the Mandarin-language podcast market and a growing presence across the Asia-Pacific region with over 14,000 shows. Creators upload an episode once and distribute it to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, KKBOX, YouTube, Amazon Music, Pocket Casts, and more than ten other players, then use AI Studio to auto-generate transcripts, summaries, highlights, and newsletter drafts. Firstory layers on second-by-second analytics, dynamic ad insertion, membership subscriptions, listener donations, cross-promotion, a personal website builder, the Flink universal link, and embeddable players. It does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public surface and infrastructure signals.

companies.name: Verint Systems
companies.description: Verint Systems is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Verint Systems API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Watershed
companies.description: Watershed is an enterprise sustainability platform used by large companies to measure their carbon footprint, report against regulatory and voluntary frameworks, and act on decarbonization opportunities. The platform combines a library of 500,000+ emissions factors, pre-verified methodologies, and AI agents for data cleaning, analysis, and report drafting. Watershed exposes an API for automated data ingestion and reporting, alongside guided uploads, and publishes integrations for common enterprise data sources. API keys are provisioned to customers via the Watershed dashboard at dashboard.watershedclimate.com. Public developer documentation is limited; most API access is delivered through customer onboarding and partner enablement.

companies.name: Commerce Bank
companies.description: Commerce Bank is the principal banking subsidiary of Commerce Bancshares, Inc. (NASDAQ CBSH), a Missouri-based regional bank holding company with roughly $32 billion in assets and dual headquarters in Kansas City and St. Louis. Commerce Bank is a Missouri state-chartered bank and Federal Reserve member, founded in 1865, offering personal, business, commercial, and wealth-management services across the U.S. Midwest. Its API posture is corporate/embedded-banking oriented rather than a fully open public program: it runs a registration-gated external developer portal (developers.commercebank.com) and a CommercePayments developer platform, and delivers ERP-embedded banking via Commerce Connections Direct. Consumer-permissioned data sharing is largely intermediated through aggregators such as Plaid and platforms like Modern Treasury rather than a documented first-party, self-serve open-banking API. No public FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented, and no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger is publicly available.

companies.name: ChannelMeter
companies.description: ChannelMeter is a creator management and payments platform for multi-channel networks, agencies, and brands. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, it provides an all-in-one suite for creator discovery, onboarding, contract management, analytics, and automated global payouts. Its Creator Pay product moves money to creators across 21+ currencies and 50+ countries, and Creator Cash offers cash advances to creators. ChannelMeter reports having processed over $1B in payments to more than one million creators, working with Stripe and Fifth Third Bank for financial services. The company is backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: Humio
companies.description: Humio is a log management and observability platform built for ingesting, storing, and searching machine data in real time at scale. Backed by Accel and acquired by CrowdStrike in 2021, Humio is now delivered as CrowdStrike Falcon LogScale. It provides high-throughput streaming ingest (including Splunk HEC and Elastic bulk compatible endpoints), a live query language for dashboards and alerts, and index-free retention. Developers integrate through a REST API for ingest and search plus a GraphQL API for administration (repositories, parsers, users, ingest tokens), with official client libraries for Python, Node.js, Go, and JavaScript and the humioctl command-line client.

companies.name: LevelTen Energy
companies.description: LevelTen Energy operates a two-sided digital marketplace and transaction platform for carbon-free energy, describing itself as the transaction infrastructure for the energy transition. Clean energy buyers, advisors, project developers, utilities and financiers use the LevelTen Energy Marketplace to compare thousands of power purchase agreement (PPA) offers, run NPV and settlement cashflow analysis, evaluate risk scenarios and track a Development Maturity Score across projects in North America and Europe. The platform also covers granular certificates, hybrid and storage PPAs, and performance monitoring, alongside market intelligence products including MarketPulse, the LevelTen PPA Price Index and Market Transparency Reports. The marketplace is served by an authenticated API at api.levelten.energy, which is gated behind marketplace login and publishes no public developer documentation, SDKs or machine-readable specification at this time.

companies.name: OpenGamma
companies.description: OpenGamma is a derivatives and margin analytics company whose technology helps trading, risk, treasury and operations teams forecast, stress test, simulate and reduce the collateral and margin costs of trading cleared and bilateral derivatives. Its capabilities span Forecast, Stress Test, Simulate, Reduce, Allocate, Process, Explain, Validate and Comply. OpenGamma's public developer surface is Strata, its award-winning open-source (Apache 2.0) analytics and market-risk library for pricing and risk of OTC and exchange-traded derivatives, which also powers OpenGamma's commercial SaaS Analytics platform. Strata is a Java library published to Maven Central under com.opengamma.strata, with a bundled command-line tool, Javadoc reference and community forum; OpenGamma does not expose a public REST API. OpenGamma is backed by Accel and was acquired by Trading Technologies.

companies.name: TigerBeetle
companies.description: TigerBeetle is an open-source (Apache 2.0) distributed financial accounting and transactions database, purpose-built for high-throughput, mission-critical double-entry bookkeeping and online transaction processing (OLTP). It is NOT an HTTP/REST API and ships no OpenAPI - the database is accessed over a custom binary wire protocol on TCP (default port 3000) via official client libraries for .NET, Go, Java, Node.js, Python, Ruby, and Rust. The "API" is the set of client operations - create_accounts, create_transfers, lookup_accounts, lookup_transfers, get_account_transfers, get_account_balances, query_accounts, and query_transfers - that use fixed-size, cache-line-aligned structs for zero-deserialization performance. TigerBeetle is self-hostable; a fully managed service is also offered to select enterprise partners via sales@tigerbeetle.com.

companies.name: Chorus.ai
companies.description: Chorus.ai is a conversation intelligence platform (acquired by ZoomInfo) that records, transcribes, and analyzes customer-facing calls and meetings to surface deal insights and coach reps.

companies.name: Datacore
companies.description: DataCore Software is a software-defined storage and data management vendor serving approximately 15,000 customers worldwide, from Fortune 500 enterprises to small and medium businesses. Its portfolio includes SANsymphony (SAN and HCI storage virtualization), Swarm (scalable S3-compatible object storage for archives and backups), Nexus (a high-performance parallel file system for HPC and AI workloads), Puls8 (container-native persistent storage for Kubernetes), and StarWind hyperconverged infrastructure for edge, ROBO, and SMB deployments. DataCore does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI-described REST API; programmatic access is delivered through product-embedded interfaces and open-source integration plugins (CSI, Docker Volume Plugin, OpenStack Cinder) maintained on its GitHub organization.

companies.name: Polars
companies.description: Polars is a blazingly fast, open-source DataFrame library and query engine written in Rust, with first-party bindings for Python, Rust, Node.js, and R. It provides lazy and eager execution, streaming for larger-than-memory datasets, automatic query optimization, multi-threading, and the Apache Arrow columnar memory format. Polars Cloud extends the same DataFrame API to managed and on-premise distributed compute with zero code changes. The project is developed by pola-rs and backed by Accel and Bain Capital Ventures.

companies.name: SolveBio
companies.description: SolveBio is a platform for biomedical and genomic datasets that lets developers query, harmonize, and automate bioinformatics workflows over curated reference data through a REST API and first-party client libraries (Python, JavaScript, Ruby, and R). SolveBio has been rebranded to QuartzBio, a Precision for Medicine company: the solvebio.com website now redirects to quartz.bio, the legacy API is served as the QuartzBio EDP REST API on per-customer instance hosts, and the SolveBio SDKs are being deprecated in favor of the quartzbio packages (Python client end of maintenance 2026-03-31). Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched from its public GitHub organization and package registries.

companies.name: BECU
companies.description: BECU (Boeing Employees' Credit Union) is a member-owned, not-for-profit state-chartered credit union founded in 1935 and headquartered in Tukwila, Washington (NMLS ID 490518). Originally serving Boeing employees, it is today one of the largest credit unions in the United States, offering consumer and business deposit accounts, lending, mortgages, and investment services across the Pacific Northwest and nationally through digital channels. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, BECU exposes no public first-party developer API or developer portal; its digital banking runs on established core and fintech vendors (FIS, LPL/Client Point, ICE/Ellie Mae for mortgage), and consumer-permissioned data access for third-party fintech apps is intermediated through data aggregators rather than a documented, self-serve BECU API. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and no mandated open-banking API contract applies here; the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule is the emerging framework that will shape BECU's future data-access posture.

companies.name: EDITED
companies.description: EDITED is an AI-powered retail intelligence platform that helps retailers, buyers, merchandisers, planners, designers, and eCommerce teams make data-driven decisions across assortment, pricing, and promotions. Its Market API (the EDITED Data product) exposes a large normalized retail market data set — SKUs, brands, categories, pricing, and assortment signals across thousands of retailers and many countries — so organizations can benchmark against competitors in real time, spot emerging trends early, and integrate competitive intelligence into their own systems. The company is a Seedcamp portfolio company; access to the Market API is sales-gated (demo / contact sales) with no public developer portal or OpenAPI at this time.

companies.name: Enable
companies.description: Enable Medicine is a healthcare and life-sciences data company that licenses an integrated, AI-ready index of clinical, spatial, cellular, and molecular data. Its research platform helps biopharma companies, academic institutions, and healthcare providers run spatial-biology analysis — spatial proteomics, cell phenotyping, tumor-microenvironment characterization, immune profiling, and biomarker identification — across 20+ disease areas over harmonized datasets spanning 10M+ patients and 125M+ cells. The platform is delivered through a login-gated web application at app.enablemedicine.com; no public developer API is currently documented. Backed by initialized-capital, insight-partners, lightspeed-venture-partners, menlo-ventures, norwest-venture-partners, and sierra-ventures.

companies.name: First Hawaiian Bank
companies.description: First Hawaiian Bank is Hawaii's oldest and largest financial institution, founded in 1858 and headquartered at First Hawaiian Center in Honolulu. It is a Hawaii state-chartered commercial bank and member FDIC, operating as the principal subsidiary of First Hawaiian, Inc. (NASDAQ ticker FHB), a publicly traded bank holding company. The bank serves consumer and commercial customers through roughly 57 branches in Hawaii plus locations in Guam and Saipan, offering deposit accounts, lending, wealth management, treasury/cash management, and merchant services. On the open-finance front, First Hawaiian operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; probes of developer.fhb.com, api.fhb.com, and fhb.com/en/developers returned no host or HTTP 404. Consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), not a direct bank API. No documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participation or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture was found as of this record. Its commercial online banking product (FHB Commercial Online, formerly OBC) is a traditional web application rather than a developer-facing API surface.

companies.name: Nexus One
companies.description: NexusOne, by Nexus Cognitive, is a composable open data architecture that lays horizontally across an entire enterprise data estate — connecting on-prem, cloud, hybrid, and legacy systems through one universal identity, governance, and operational control plane. Built on 85+ deeply integrated open-source tools (Iceberg, Trino, Spark, Ranger, Keycloak, DataHub, Gravitino, Airflow, and more), it positions itself as "The Data Layer for AI," making every system operate as a single coherent, agent-callable system without data migration or vendor lock-in. Founded in 2022, headquartered in Atlanta, GA, and backed by Insight Partners.

companies.name: Om1
companies.description: OM1 is an AI-powered healthcare analytics and real-world data company that generates real-world evidence from clinical, EMR, and claims data. Its PhenOM foundation model is trained on billions of patient-years to identify patient phenotypes, accelerate diagnosis, and predict future medical events, risks, and responses to treatment. OM1 delivers clinical registries, automated observational studies, patient-finding and outcomes-prediction solutions, and curated real-world datasets covering hundreds of millions of patients to life sciences, biopharma, payer, and provider organizations. OM1 does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation surface.

companies.name: Tangerine
companies.description: Tangerine is a Canadian direct (branchless) bank headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and a federally regulated Schedule I bank chartered as Tangerine Bank (institution number 614). Founded in 1997 as ING Direct Canada, it was acquired by Scotiabank in 2012 and rebranded as Tangerine in 2014; it remains a separate legal entity operating as Scotiabank's digital-banking arm, serving roughly two million clients with no-fee chequing and savings accounts, GICs, mortgages, mutual funds, and a cash-back Mastercard delivered entirely through mobile and web. On API and open-finance posture, Tangerine publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; Canada has no operational consumer-driven-banking mandate yet (the federal framework is legislated but not live), so third-party access to Tangerine account and transaction data today is aggregator-based via Plaid and Finicity (Mastercard) rather than through a documented first-party API.

companies.name: VetSource
companies.description: VetSource is a veterinary technology and pharmacy company founded in 2008 that delivers a suite of pharmacy, technology, and business services for the pet health industry.
