Its offerings span home-delivery prescription management (an online pharmacy and prescription workflow that lets veterinary practices prescribe and fulfill medications with compliance and revenue tools), the Vet2Pet client-engagement platform (a custom-branded app connecting practices with pet owners for communication, reminders, loyalty, and telehealth), and data/analytics services that provide industry benchmarking and practice performance insights. VetSource serves veterinary practices and pet owners across North America. No public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation is published; this profile captures the company identity and probed domain-security posture.

companies.name: Major League Baseball
companies.description: Major League Baseball (MLB) is the professional baseball organization of the United States and Canada, operating the National League and American League with 30 teams. MLB Advanced Media (now part of MLB) provides public stats and game data through the MLB Stats API and the legacy MLB Data (lookup service) API, used by teams, broadcasters, analysts, and a wide community of developers building stats sites, fantasy applications, and analytical tools. MLB also exposes Statcast data through Baseball Savant. There is no general-purpose self-service developer portal with terms or signup; the APIs are widely consumed but are formally intended for partner use.

companies.name: Bloom Institute of Technology
companies.description: Bloom Institute of Technology (formerly Lambda School) is an online coding bootcamp founded in 2017 that trains learners for AI-driven tech careers through part-time and full-time programs in Full Stack Web Development, Backend Development, and Data Science, plus corporate "AI for Developer Productivity" training. It is known for its income-share and deferred-tuition model ($0 upfront with a job-contingent payment plan) and a tuition-refund guarantee. The company reports 4,000+ graduates since 2017. It is a venture-backed consumer education company (backed by GV) and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

companies.name: Flarion
companies.description: Flarion is a data-processing acceleration company that speeds up distributed compute engines — Apache Spark, Hadoop, and Ray — without code or infrastructure changes. It ships an Arrow-native, DataFusion/Polars-based execution engine written in Rust that installs as a plugin in about six minutes, plus intelligent workload caching (query, data-block, and buffer caching) and a performance-monitoring platform for job metrics, resource tracking, anomaly detection, and failure prevention. Flarion runs on-premises or on Databricks, AWS EMR, GCP Dataproc, Azure HDInsight, and Anyscale, with an agentless architecture that requires no access to customer data, delivering roughly 3x performance and 60% cost savings. Flarion is a portfolio company of Sierra Ventures. The company exposes a product console and a legal/SLA surface but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Flarion Technologies
companies.description: Flarion is a data-processing acceleration company that speeds up distributed data engines without code changes or infrastructure migration. Its plug-and-play engine replaces row-by-row JVM execution with a native, vectorized runtime built in Rust on Apache Arrow and DataFusion, delivering roughly 3x performance and up to 60% cost savings. Flarion ships three capabilities across Apache Spark, Hadoop, and Ray: a Data Processing Accelerator, Workload Caching that eliminates redundant recomputation, and a Performance Monitoring platform with anomaly detection and failure prevention. It integrates with managed services including Databricks, AWS EMR, GCP Dataproc, and Azure HDInsight via simple Spark configuration (dropping in a JAR), with usage-based pricing billed per accelerated CPU-hour. Flarion is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. As of this profile the company exposes a product console and marketing/legal surface but no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation portal.

companies.name: hobbyDB
companies.description: hobbyDB is a database and marketplace for collectibles — a platform that lets anyone catalog, offer, buy, and sell just about any collectible (Funko Pops, action figures, trading cards, die-cast, and more) at any time, from anywhere, in auction-style or fixed-price formats. It pairs a community-curated reference database of collectible items and variants with personal collection-management tools (lists, condition and grading tracking, pre-orders, trades, and import/export) and a peer-to-peer marketplace for transactions between collectors. hobbyDB is a Techstars-backed company.

companies.name: Plixi
companies.description: Plixi is an AI-powered Instagram growth platform that helps influencers, businesses, e-commerce brands, and content creators gain authentic followers through organic automation rather than bots or fake accounts. The service combines paid advertising, micro-interactions, and niche audience-data clustering with a machine-learning targeting feature (AI-Match) that lets users train the algorithm by rating accounts. It provides a real-time analytics dashboard, optional expert account management (Plixi Experts), and a subscription model across Basic, Pro, and Experts tiers. Plixi is a consumer SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Pomo
companies.description: Pomo is an AI marketing platform that runs an always-on AI marketing team, turning continuous market, competitor, brand, and trend intelligence into strategy, creative direction, ad-placement planning, and launch-ready campaign workflows for lean growth, brand, and performance teams. It monitors signals daily, surfaces opportunity and whitespace, drafts approval-ready campaigns, briefs, and creatives, and supports AEO/GEO AI-search visibility and Marketing Mix Modeling. Pomo is also offered as a managed service where in-house marketing experts operate the platform on a customer's behalf. Founded in 2025 and based in Palo Alto, California, Pomo raised a $4.5M seed round led by Kindred Ventures with Databricks Ventures, SV Angel, and angel investors. There is no public developer API; the site publishes a real /llms.txt AI-discovery document but no OpenAPI, docs, or developer surface.

companies.name: Shopventory
companies.description: Thrive by Shopventory is inventory management, catalog control, and reporting software for small and medium-sized retail, restaurant, and hospitality businesses. Founded in 2012 out of a San Diego boutique and a graduate of the Techstars Boulder accelerator, Shopventory syncs stock, sales, and cost-of-goods data across multiple locations and sales channels, and integrates with Square, Shopify, Clover, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, and QuickBooks Online. The platform offers barcode scanning, purchase-order automation, demand forecasting, bundles and component-level tracking, price-tag printing, and advanced custom reporting. The company operates as Thrive by Shopventory (thrivemetrics.com). Its former public developer API (apidocs.shopventory.com) is no longer resolvable, so this profile captures the company's live web, support, and integration surface plus probed domain-security posture rather than a public API specification.

companies.name: Spate
companies.description: Spate is an AI-powered consumer trend forecasting and market intelligence platform for beauty, wellness, and food and beverage brands. It analyzes hundreds of billions of search signals and hundreds of millions of social posts across TikTok, Instagram, Reddit, and Google to predict emerging trends, benchmark competitors, surface whitespace opportunities, and track viral content and sentiment. Used by 200+ brands including Sephora, L'Oreal, P&G, Unilever, and e.l.f. Beauty across marketing, R&D, sales, and retail teams. Spate is a consumer-facing SaaS analytics product and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Track Titan
companies.description: Track Titan is a sim racing analytics and coaching platform that records in-game telemetry from simulators including iRacing, Assetto Corsa and ACC, the F1 series, Automobilista 2, Forza Motorsport, and Le Mans Ultimate, turning laps into time-loss analysis, AI coaching feedback, auto-installed esports car setups, and structured Academy learning content for a community of over 295,000 sim racers on PC and console. Founded by former professional sim racer and Porsche coach Max Teichert and backed by investors including Partech, Track Titan is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of July 2026 (api.tracktitan.io serves only an internal backend service).

companies.name: TransferRoom
companies.description: TransferRoom is football's real-time transfer marketplace, connecting clubs, agents and players to buy, sell and loan players and to recruit head coaches. Its API delivers verified, real-time market intelligence — Expected Transfer Value (xTV) benchmarks, player availability and deal-viability signals, contract-expiry and estimated-salary data, agent and coach representation, and head-coach ratings — returned as JSON for clubs to integrate directly into their own systems (SQL databases, BI dashboards, spreadsheets and code notebooks). Trusted by 800+ clubs across 130 leagues and 500+ agencies, covering 130,000+ players and 7,000+ head coaches, and powering 7,500+ transfer deals. The API is sales-gated: technical reference (endpoints, authentication, base URL) is provided to clubs on engagement and is not published publicly.

companies.name: Whatifi
companies.description: Whatifi is a visual financial modeling and scenario planning platform for small and medium businesses, letting founders, fractional CFOs, VFX and gaming studios, and startups model, forecast, and share runway, staffing, capacity, and profit scenarios without spreadsheets or formulas. The product uses an event-based canvas of 30+ pre-built business logic "Events" to build and compare "what if" forecasts in real time, and connects to accounting and banking data through integrations with Excel, Google Sheets, Xero, QuickBooks, Plaid, Railz, and OpenAI. Whatifi is backed by a16z. As of this enrichment pass Whatifi publishes a marketing site, a Notion-hosted help center, and a web application, but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface.

companies.name: 3PAR (HPE 3PAR StoreServ)
companies.description: 3PAR is an enterprise storage platform, now part of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE acquired 3PAR in 2010), that powers mission-critical applications with HPE 3PAR StoreServ and Primera arrays. For developers and automation engineers, 3PAR exposes the HPE 3PAR Web Services API (WSAPI) — a REST interface that manages storage provisioning, virtual volumes, hosts, ports, CPGs, snapshots, and remote copy on 3PAR/Primera/Alletra arrays, offering a more flexible and programmable alternative to the 3PAR Command Line Interface. HPE publishes first-party client libraries (Python, Ruby, PowerShell) plus Ansible, Puppet, Chef, OpenStack Cinder, and Docker volume integrations against WSAPI. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead (Mayfield, Menlo Ventures backed the original 3PAR before its IPO and HP acquisition) and enriched from HPE's public developer surface.

companies.name: Kayrros
companies.description: Kayrros is an environmental-intelligence and geospatial-AI company that independently tracks human activity and its physical footprint worldwide by combining satellite imagery, alternative data, and machine learning. Its products span energy markets — crude oil and jet fuel intelligence, LNG, renewables, solar and battery-storage construction monitoring, industrial and on-road energy demand, and stockpiles — and environmental risk — methane emissions via Methane Watch, wildfire risk, forest-carbon and deforestation monitoring, and carbon accounting. Kayrros delivers asset-level data feeds, APIs, and dashboards to traders, operators, financial institutions, regulators, insurers, and the public sector. The company was acquired by Energy Aspects in May 2026.

companies.name: Premier Inc
companies.description: Premier Inc is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Premier Inc API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Securiti
companies.description: Securiti is a San Jose, California data security, privacy, and AI governance company that markets the Data Command Center, a unified hybrid multicloud platform for sensitive data discovery, classification, security posture management, privacy operations, and AI governance. The platform is built on the Data Command Graph, a knowledge-graph layer that correlates data assets, identities, regulations, and AI systems across 1,000+ pre-built connectors spanning AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Snowflake, Databricks, and major SaaS applications. Securiti's product surface includes Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), Sensitive Data Intelligence, Data Access Intelligence, Data Flow Governance, Data Minimization, Breach Impact Analysis, Data Subject Request (DSR) Automation, Universal Consent Management, Mobile App Consent SDKs, Assessment Automation, Data Mapping, Privacy Center, the People Data Graph, Data Catalog, Data Lineage, Data Quality, Compliance Management, AI Security and Governance, Agent Commander for AI risk detection, Security for AI Agents and Copilots, and the Gencore AI suite for safe enterprise AI copilots, vector-database synchronization, unstructured data curation, and context-aware LLM firewalls. The platform exposes REST-based APIs, a turnkey JavaScript consent library, standards-based webhook interfaces, no-code/low-code workflow integrations, and native mobile SDKs for iOS and Android consent capture. The API reference, SDKs, consent banner generators, and connector catalog are all reached through the Securiti app and Privacy Center; full API documentation requires an authenticated tenant. Securiti was founded in 2018 by Rehan Jalil and has been recognized as a Gartner Customers' Choice and an IDC Worldwide Leader in data privacy and data security. The company's revenue model is enterprise SaaS subscription with usage-based connector and module pricing; no public free tier or self-serve API key issuance is currently offered.

companies.name: USADATA, Inc.
companies.description: USADATA is a data and marketing intelligence company founded in 1998 and headquartered in New York City, backed by Insight Partners. It maintains a database of 260+ million US consumer records, 15+ million businesses, and 190 million households, updated monthly, and provides audience intelligence, data enrichment, hygiene, and omnichannel campaign activation. Products include the SL360 self-serve audience platform, Hailey AI conversational audience builder, a white-label Leads Portal with an embeddable Leads Module, and RESTful APIs for real-time and batch enrichment, audience building, hygiene (address standardization, NCOA, dedup, deceased suppression), and matchback attribution, with integrations into Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, and other CRM and marketing platforms. API access is sales-gated with no public developer portal or published reference documentation.

companies.name: Alinea Health
companies.description: Alinea Health is an AI-powered clinical trial recruitment intelligence platform that analyzes global trial registry data (ClinicalTrials.gov, ISRCTN, EU CTR) alongside patient availability to detect enrollment risk before it causes delays and to match eligible patients to appropriate studies for sponsors, CROs, sites, and healthcare providers. The platform surfaces at-risk trials, benchmarks sites, and visualizes enrollment pipelines, positioning delay prevention as protecting $1.1M-$1.7M per month in trial spend. The company advertises enterprise-grade RESTful APIs and custom data pipelines with end-to-end encryption and SOC 2 compliance, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; access is gated behind a partner platform and an early-access program. Backed by General Catalyst, with offices in Toronto and Barcelona.

companies.name: Brightfield
companies.description: Brightfield is an extended-workforce intelligence company whose TDX (Talent Data Exchange) and TDX AI platform give enterprises data, automation, and precision over contingent-labor and statement-of-work (SOW) spending across 100+ countries. Products include Rate Intelligence, Rate Card Manager, SOW Rate Insights, SOW Quality and Risk Analytics, Supplier Scorecard, and an ROI Dashboard, built on transaction-level data from 700+ companies and $500B+ of global spend. Founded and led by CEO Jason Ezratty and headquartered in Washington, DC, Brightfield is backed by Sapphire Ventures. The product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS application; no public developer API or documentation surface is published at this time.

companies.name: Cadence Bank
companies.description: Cadence Bank is a regional U.S. commercial bank headquartered in Tupelo, Mississippi and Houston, Texas, formed in October 2021 when legacy Cadence Bancorporation merged into BancorpSouth Bank (the surviving entity, subsequently renamed Cadence Bank; NYSE ticker CADE). It is a Mississippi state-chartered bank operating roughly 400+ branches across the U.S. South, Midwest, and Texas with about $48-50 billion in assets, offering consumer banking, mortgages, home equity, credit cards, small business and commercial banking, treasury management, and wealth/insurance services. On open finance, Cadence Bank exposes no first-party public developer API or developer portal; consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), which is the honest, prevailing posture for most U.S. regional banks. No documented direct FDX (Financial Data Exchange) membership or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access API was found as of this profile.

companies.name: Duco
companies.description: Duco is an AI-powered operational data automation platform for financial services. It helps banks, asset managers, brokers, asset servicers and market infrastructure firms normalize, validate and reconcile any data in the cloud — cutting the time spent on manual data work, reducing operational risk and accelerating front-, middle- and back-office processes. The no-code platform ingests data from any source (including unstructured documents via Adaptive Intelligent Document Processing), then transforms, matches, reconciles and publishes it with full audit and control. Duco's Agentic Workspace layers agentic AI over these operations so agents can handle repetitive extraction, matching and exception-labelling work under human oversight. Use cases span securities and derivatives reconciliation, ETD clearing, OTC confirmations, custody, cash accounts, crypto holdings and transaction/regulatory reporting (EMIR, CFTC, MiFID II, ASIC, MAS, T+1). Customers include HSBC, Deutsche Bank, ING, Santander, Northern Trust and Fidelity Digital Assets. Duco is backed by Insight Partners.

companies.name: Naboo
companies.description: Naboo is Reasoning Layer infrastructure for enterprise AI agents, built on a Decision Graph that models how a company actually decides, ships, and unblocks - who decided what, what triggered each decision, what blocks it, and what depends on it - across code, tickets, pull requests, docs, Slack, runtime, and internal services. Any AI agent in the organization queries the graph in GraphQL, or through an MCP server that turns plain intent into a structured query, and gets a structured answer instead of a list of search results. Naboo deploys on-premise or in a customer VPC with zero data egress, integrates with any LLM (OpenAI, Anthropic, Llama, Mistral) and agentic framework (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI), and enforces existing role-based access controls at retrieval time. Founded in 2023 by Gilad Salinger (CEO) and Dror Wolmer (CTO), with production customers Global-E (NASDAQ: GLBE) and Melio.

companies.name: Odaseva
companies.description: Odaseva is an enterprise data security, backup, and governance platform purpose-built for large, complex Salesforce environments. It provides data backup and recovery, archiving, seeding and anonymization/masking, encryption and key management, privacy and data-residency controls, and data governance for regulated enterprises. Odaseva holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, HITRUST, HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, TISAX, IRAP, MLPS 2.0, and CSA STAR Level 2, with independent audits by Ernst & Young. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network; Odaseva sells to enterprises and does not publish a public developer API portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs at this time.

companies.name: LeapYear
companies.description: LeapYear Technologies built an enterprise platform for differentially private analytics and machine learning, letting organizations run statistics, SQL-style queries, feature engineering, and supervised and unsupervised model training against their most sensitive data while a mathematically provable privacy guarantee bounds what any single record can leak. The product shipped as a self-hosted server, LeapYear Core, driven by a first-party Python client library that exposes databases, tables, views, users, groups, permissions, privacy profiles, and per-database privacy budgets as programmable resources. Snowflake announced its intent to acquire LeapYear in February 2023 and closed the acquisition for $62.0 million in cash, folding the differential privacy technology and team into the Snowflake Data Cloud clean-room capabilities. The standalone company surface is now retired: leapyear.io no longer answers on HTTPS. The surviving public developer surface is the hosted LeapYear Python client reference for version 4.1.1.

companies.name: Change Healthcare
companies.description: Change Healthcare is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Change Healthcare API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Jala
companies.description: JALA is an Indonesian aquaculture technology company providing end-to-end solutions for the shrimp farming industry, describing itself as a fully connected system powered by data farmers can trust. It connects farmers, processors, and buyers through the JALA App for real-time pond monitoring and data analytics, the Baruni technology platform, farming supplies (post-larvae, feed, technical assistance), harvest and cold-chain logistics services, and traceable certified supply chains for processors and buyers. Backed by 500 Global, JALA operates a consumer/operator SaaS platform (app.jala.tech) rather than a public developer API program. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline.

companies.name: Montenegro Open Data
companies.description: Montenegro Open Data is a national government open-data portal for Montenegro running CKAN. It exposes the CKAN catalog API, a standardized machine-readable interface over approximately 894 datasets, supporting programmatic dataset search, metadata retrieval, and resource access. Because it runs CKAN, it shares a consistent API surface with every other CKAN portal, making it uniformly harvestable and integrable.

companies.name: Sunairio
companies.description: Sunairio is a grid forecasting company that provides integrated weather, climate, and energy insights for power markets. Its flagship platform, Sunairio ONE, generates 1,000-member ensemble forecasts across horizons from hourly to decadal, capturing extreme-weather and grid-stress scenarios that traditional forecasts miss. The company also publishes SHED (Sunairio High-resolution Earth Data), a proprietary historical weather dataset for the Continental US from 1950 to present at roughly 100x the resolution of ERA5, with asset-level wind and solar variability. Customers such as energy traders, grid operators, utility-scale asset developers, and demand-response aggregators access forecasts and data through a web UI, an API, and (on higher tiers) direct Snowflake data delivery. Founded in 2020 by Rob Cirincione, the company has been recognized by the National Science Foundation, American Clean Power, and EPRI.

companies.name: Zorus
companies.description: Zorus is a cybersecurity company that provides DNS web protection and filtering built for managed service providers (MSPs), managed security service providers (MSSPs), and IT teams. Its Archon agent delivers DNS filtering without requiring per-router DNS changes, layered with CyberSight behavioral user analytics, geo-IP and network filtering, zero-trust device isolation, and SaaS inventory and usage visibility. Zorus is delivered as a multi-tenant SaaS platform administered through a partner portal (portal.zorustech.com), positioned as an alternative to Cisco Umbrella, WebRoot DNS, and WebTitan. Zorus does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation; its API surface (api.zorustech.com) sits behind the authenticated product portal. This profile captures the company's public web properties and probed security posture.

companies.name: Aily Labs
companies.description: Aily Labs is a Munich-based enterprise AI company that builds an AI Decision Intelligence Suite — a platform that connects siloed internal and external data to deliver real-time, explainable predictions and recommendations across Finance, R&D, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, Go-To-Market, Procurement, and People functions. The suite ships with 300+ validated predictive models and an iOS app, and is deployed across Healthcare & Life Sciences, Consumer Goods, Luxury & Fashion, Media & Tech, Retail, and Services (clients include Sanofi). Aily Labs is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's corporate, security, and compliance surface.

companies.name: Citus Data
companies.description: Citus Data is the company behind Citus, an open source extension that turns PostgreSQL into a distributed database. Rather than forking Postgres, Citus adds sharding, distributed tables, reference tables, and a distributed query planner so applications can scale out across many nodes while keeping full SQL, ACID transactions, and the entire Postgres ecosystem. It is used for multi-tenant SaaS applications, real-time analytics dashboards, and microservices architectures. Founded in San Francisco and acquired by Microsoft in 2019, Citus is developed in the open on GitHub and is also offered as a managed cloud service (Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL); its reference documentation is hosted on Microsoft Learn. Citus is consumed over the standard PostgreSQL wire protocol and SQL, so it exposes no REST/HTTP API, no OAuth surface, and no language SDKs of its own.

companies.name: Curve Health
companies.description: Curve Health is a New York City-based digital health technology company, founded in 2020, that delivers a virtual care and telemedicine platform purpose-built for skilled nursing facilities (SNFs) and senior care. The platform unifies telemedicine, a health information exchange, predictive analytics, and smart billing into a single system so nurses, physicians, behavioral health providers, and facility operators can deliver care in place and reduce avoidable hospital transfers. Curve Health reports enabling 150,000+ remote care visits and an 80% reduction in hospitalizations for partner facilities, and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Morningside. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web and product-documentation surface; Curve Health does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition.

companies.name: dv01
companies.description: dv01 is an "InvestorTech" data and analytics platform for the structured finance and consumer-lending markets, part of Fitch Group. It aggregates, standardizes, and validates loan-level data across asset classes (RMBS, auto, student loans, personal loans, buy-now-pay-later) and delivers it, along with reporting and surveillance tooling, to issuers, lenders, and investors. Products include Data Direct, Data Management, DealStudio, Securitizations, Tape Cracker, and portfolio/market surveillance. dv01 publishes no public developer REST API or OpenAPI; data is delivered into client environments via Snowflake Data Share, BigQuery, SFTP, and S3. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Ribbit Capital and enriched with verified public identity, compliance, and domain-security signals.

companies.name: ExlService Holdings
companies.description: ExlService Holdings is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The ExlService Holdings API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Lica
companies.description: Lica is an AI research company building a substrate to train and evaluate AI models to be capable design partners across expressions of taste and consumption. Its research spans spatial reasoning and composition, layout generation and editing, vector-graphics (SVG) understanding, personalization and brand identity, and animation generation. Lica publishes the LICA dataset of layered graphic-design compositions and GDB (Graphic Design Benchmark), a real-world benchmark that scores frontier models on designer workflows across layout, typography, infographics, template semantics and animation. The company is backed by Accel, South Park Commons and Village Global. As of July 2026 Lica ships no public API, developer portal or API reference; product access is an email waitlist and its public developer surface is the lica-world GitHub organization, including the first-party DesignMCP MCP server.

companies.name: Mobagel
companies.description: MoBagel is an AI and automated machine learning (AutoML) company founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Jose, California, with offices across seven global locations. Its flagship Decanter AI platform lets business users build machine learning models and generate predictions without a data science background, spanning AutoML, automated time-series forecasting (AutoTSF), MLOps, DataOps, and a generative-BI suite (Generative BI, Generative ETL, Generative Expert) now surfaced through the 8ndpoint product and a family of vertical AI agents for marketing, supply chain, finance, and manufacturing. MoBagel exposes Decanter AI programmatically through an official first-party Python SDK (decanter-ai-sdk) that authenticates with an API key and drives data upload, model training, and prediction. Backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: Rapidminer
companies.description: RapidMiner (now Altair RapidMiner / Altair AI) is a data science and machine learning platform that unites data preparation, machine learning, and predictive model deployment in a visual, low-code environment. The developer surface is centered on the official `rapidminer` Python package for interacting with Altair AI Studio and Altair AI Hub — reading and writing data, running and scheduling processes, managing git-based versioned projects and connections, and calling deployed Web API and Scoring endpoints — plus a Java/Python extension SDK for building custom operators. AI Hub authenticates via OAuth (offline token against a Keycloak-style authentication server). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Earlybird; RapidMiner was acquired by Altair, now part of Siemens.

companies.name: Waters Corporation
companies.description: Waters Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Waters Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: WNS Holdings
companies.description: WNS Holdings is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The WNS Holdings API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Zenline AI
companies.description: Zenline AI (Zenline GmbH / Zenline AG) is a Swiss assortment-intelligence platform for retail category teams. It blends public market data with a retailer's own product data to recommend pricing, product consolidation, and new-product launches, surfacing market white spots, sell-out trends, substitutes and variants so category managers can improve margin and portfolio performance across omni-channel retail. Backed by Seedcamp and used by European retailers including Otto Group, Conrad Electronic, Lapeyre and Fressnapf/Das Futterhaus. ISO 27001 certified. As of this enrichment pass Zenline publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or MCP server.

companies.name: SkyFoundry
companies.description: SkyFoundry, founded in 2009 and headquartered in Glen Allen, Virginia, develops SkySpark, an analytics and informatics platform that connects, stores, analyzes, and visualizes data from smart devices, automation and control systems, meters, and sensors to "find what matters" in large equipment and facility datasets. SkySpark automatically detects issues, patterns, deviations, faults, and cost-reduction opportunities across intelligent buildings, industrial, agriculture, energy, government, and healthcare facilities, and has been applied to over 15,000 buildings spanning more than a billion square feet. SkySpark is a native Project Haystack server: external applications integrate through the Haystack HTTP REST API (ops such as read, hisRead, hisWrite, pointWrite, watchSub/watchPoll, eval, commit, and nav) with Zinc, JSON, Trio, and CSV data formats, and authenticate using the Haystack SCRAM (SHA-256) handshake with bearer authTokens. The company sells through a network of 140+ OEM, systems-integrator, and value-added-distributor channel partners rather than a self-service public SaaS.

companies.name: Albertinvent
companies.description: Albert Invent builds Albert OS, an AI operating system for chemists and R&D teams that unifies electronic lab notebooks, structured molecular-level experimental data, chemical drawing, and safety/compliance data (safety data sheets for roughly 400,000 substances) with chemistry-trained AI models built on a foundation of 15 million molecular structures. The platform helps materials, formulation, and specialty-chemical teams capture proprietary experimental data and accelerate discovery, training custom predictive models on each customer's own chemistry. Albert Invent is a scientific R&D / developer-tools SaaS company backed by Homebrew; its APIs and developer surface are not publicly documented (product documentation at docs.albertinvent.com is access-gated).

companies.name: Preql
companies.description: Preql (preql.ai) is an enterprise data platform that automates data cleaning, reconciliation, and semantic modeling to deliver the trustworthy context layer that AI agents and business analytics depend on. Its agentic platform combines Agentic Semantic Modeling, Data Cleaning Agents, and AI-Powered Reporting to automatically resolve data mismatches, schema drift, and anomalies across ERP, CRM, HR, and expense systems without manual intervention, serving finance, operations, revenue, and executive decision-making at large enterprises. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Felicis, and added to the API Evangelist network. Preql does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API reference; this profile captures its public company identity, help center, and web properties.

companies.name: Spredfast
companies.description: Spredfast was an Austin-based social media marketing and management platform providing social publishing, engagement, listening, and analytics for enterprise brands and agencies. Backed by Battery Ventures, Spredfast merged with Lithium Technologies in 2018; the combined company rebranded as Khoros in 2019, and the Spredfast product line is now delivered as Khoros Marketing. Its developer API surface — the Conversations API, Publishing API, Analytics Reporting API, Notification API, and CRM API — is documented today under the Khoros developer center at developer.khoros.com, secured with OAuth 2.0. The legacy api.spredfast.com host still resolves, while the original devcenter.spredfast.com developer portal is no longer maintained.

companies.name: Zenysis
companies.description: Zenysis is a health intelligence infrastructure company that helps governments and organizations across low- and middle-income countries turn fragmented, messy health data into actionable insight. Its flagship Harmony Analytics Platform is open source (AGPL-3.0) and transforms, cleans, enriches, and integrates data from many disparate sources for analysis, visualization, and decision support. Zenysis powers national health information systems, disease surveillance, and program monitoring. There is no public hosted API product; Harmony is self-hosted and exposes its own REST (Flask-Potion) and GraphQL interfaces on a per-deployment basis. This repo was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched from the company's public web and GitHub presence.

companies.name: Affinity Credit Union
companies.description: Affinity Credit Union is a member-owned financial cooperative headquartered in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada. Formed in 2005 through the amalgamation of several Saskatchewan credit unions, it is the largest credit union in Saskatchewan and among the ten largest in Canada, with roughly CAD 9.6 billion in managed assets and a province-wide branch and advice-centre network serving personal and business members. As a provincially regulated cooperative under its "Banking on Values" mandate, members democratically own and govern the institution. Affinity exposes NO first-party public developer API or developer portal; digital and core banking are delivered through banking-technology providers (the credit-union system's Central 1 rails), and third-party consumer data access today is aggregator/screen-scraping based. Affinity is a stated supporter of the credit-union-system "Open Banking Solution" delivered by Caspian One under the Large Credit Union Coalition, positioning it for Canada's legislated-but-not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework (FCAC).

companies.name: Agentic Data Intelligence
companies.description: Agentic Data Intelligence SA (ADI) is a Swiss-headquartered startup building the control plane for AI data analytics: a thin semantics-and-control layer that sits between AI agents and data. ADI automatically generates machine-readable semantics and an enforceable contract (rules) that governs how copilots and agents conduct data analysis, improving governance, accuracy, and consistency while lowering inference cost. It never sees the underlying data, generating the contract from schema and context and running analysis locally. The Starter Edition targets coding agents and IDEs (Claude Code, Cursor, Manus) delivered via SKILL.md files, plugins, and MCP Servers; the Enterprise Edition extends cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, Databricks, dbt). Backed by Electric Capital and supporting the Open Semantic Interchange (OSI) initiative. Currently in limited alpha, accepting first partners via a waitlist.

companies.name: Appriss Inc.
companies.description: Appriss Inc. was a Louisville, Kentucky data and analytics holding company whose business units were broken up in 2021: Appriss Insights was sold to Equifax in a $1.825 billion deal, and Appriss Health was rebranded as the independent company Bamboo Health. The surviving Appriss Retail business (apprissretail.com) is an AI-powered retail loss-prevention platform that helps retailers combat total retail loss across in-store and online channels through returns-fraud prevention, shrink and exception analytics, and case and audit management. Its products include Appriss Engage (returns and claims management), Appriss Secure (shrink and exception analytics), Appriss Incident (case and audit management), and the Sidekick AI collaborator. Appriss Retail publishes no public developer API program — its APIS Online portal is an authenticated Asset Protection Information System (customer login), not a developer API surface.

companies.name: Associated Bank
companies.description: Associated Bank, N.A. is the primary banking subsidiary of Associated Banc-Corp (NYSE ASB), a nationally chartered commercial bank and the largest bank holding company headquartered in Wisconsin, based in Green Bay. With roughly $50 billion in total assets following the April 2026 acquisition of American National Corporation, Associated operates a full-service Midwest banking franchise of more than 200 locations across Wisconsin, Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri and Nebraska, offering consumer, business, commercial and wealth-management services. Associated does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. Its digital banking runs on a core-provider stack (Jack Henry), and consumer-permissioned data access is delivered through third-party aggregators (Plaid, Tink/TrueLayer) rather than a direct first-party API. Its commercial treasury customers use the login-gated Associated Connect platform. No FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is publicly documented as of this review.

companies.name: Bank of Hawaii
companies.description: Bank of Hawaii is a state-chartered commercial bank organized under the laws of the State of Hawaii in 1897, a member of the Federal Reserve System and FDIC-insured. It is the principal banking subsidiary of Bank of Hawaii Corporation (NYSE: BOH), a Honolulu-headquartered regional financial services company serving Hawaii, Guam, and other Pacific islands with consumer, commercial, and wealth-management banking. As a regional US institution, Bank of Hawaii publishes no first-party public developer portal and exposes no documented public API surface; probes of developer.boh.com and developers.boh.com do not resolve. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and consumer-permissioned data access to Bank of Hawaii accounts is available in practice only through third-party aggregators (for example Plaid), not through a direct bank-operated API. No Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership and no published CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture were found at the time of this record.

companies.name: Briya
companies.description: Briya builds AIRE (AI Research Environment), a privacy-first AI platform for healthcare and clinical research that lets researchers analyze real-world medical data without writing code. AIRE trains AI models on real-world data and provides domain-specific agents for literature review, hypothesis testing, population and cohort analysis, study design, and manuscript-ready output with built-in validation. Data is accessed across multiple sources without centralizing it into a warehouse, with a compliance posture aimed at HIPAA, GDPR, and FDA/EMA regulatory standards. Briya serves emerging biotech, life sciences organizations, academic institutions, and healthcare systems, with offices in New York, Nashville, and Tel Aviv. The company is backed by Insight Partners. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass on a portfolio lead; Briya publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

companies.name: Conexus Credit Union
companies.description: Conexus Credit Union is Saskatchewan's largest credit union, a member-owned cooperative financial institution headquartered in Regina with over $10 billion in consolidated assets under management, more than 140,000 members, roughly 30 branches, and over 800 employees across the province. As a provincially regulated Saskatchewan credit union it operates under a cooperative charter, with member deposits guaranteed by the Credit Union Deposit Guarantee Corporation (CUDGC). In November 2024 Conexus announced its intent to explore a merger with Cornerstone and Synergy credit unions. Conexus does not publish a first-party public developer API or a developer portal; developer.conexus.ca does not resolve, and /developer and /api on the corporate site return 404. Consumer financial-data access is provided through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid in Canada) via screen-scraping and connection-based data sharing rather than a first-party API. Digital and online banking are delivered through core-banking and fintech partners (banking.online.conexus.ca), and investing runs through the credit-union system's Aviso Wealth / Qtrade and Thrive Wealth partners. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework, overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC), is legislated but not yet operational, so Conexus's open-finance access remains voluntary and aggregator-mediated today.

companies.name: Equitable Bank
companies.description: Equitable Bank is Canada's seventh largest independent Schedule I bank by assets and a wholly owned subsidiary of EQB Inc. (TSX: EQB), a Toronto-based Canadian financial services company with over CAD $144 billion in combined assets under management and administration. Federally chartered and Canadian owned, Equitable Bank markets itself as "Canada's Challenger Bank" and, in 2016, launched EQ Bank, its digital-only banking platform offering high interest savings accounts, GICs, and payments alongside the parent bank's single-family residential and commercial lending. Equitable Bank and Equitable Trust are members of the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC). On the open-finance front, Equitable Bank does not operate a public first-party developer portal or publish downloadable API specifications; consumer permissioned data sharing is delivered through the Canadian aggregator Flinks (Flinks Outbound) rather than a first-party API. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated in Budget 2024 with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada as overseer) is not yet operational, so the bank's data-access posture today is voluntary and aggregator-mediated.

companies.name: Frost Bank
companies.description: Frost Bank is the banking subsidiary of Cullen/Frost Bankers, Inc. (NYSE: CFR), a San Antonio, Texas-based financial holding company and one of the largest Texas-headquartered banks. Founded in 1868, Frost operates as a Texas state-chartered commercial bank (regulated by the Texas Department of Banking and the Federal Reserve after converting from a national charter to a state charter in 2012), serving consumer, commercial, wealth-management, and insurance customers through financial centers across Texas. On open finance, Frost runs NO first-party public developer portal or documented public API: the host developer.frostbank.com does not resolve and no developers/API page exists on frostbank.com. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is made available only through third-party aggregators — Frost's own digital banking uses Plaid for account aggregation — rather than a direct API. Frost publishes no FDX (Financial Data Exchange) participation and no stated CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture. This is an honest identity-only record for a regional US bank whose external data access is aggregator-mediated.

companies.name: Kompyte
companies.description: Kompyte is a competitive intelligence and sales enablement platform, part of Semrush, that automates the tracking of competitors across their websites, pricing pages, product releases, content, ads, social channels and review sites. Captured changes are scored and summarized into AI-generated daily digests and continuously updated sales battlecards, so revenue teams can see what rivals changed and how to respond in live deals. Kompyte also supports win/loss capture and delivers intelligence into the tools sellers already use through CRM, chat, sales-enablement and file-storage integrations including Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Highspot, Showpad, Trello, Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive. Kompyte publishes no public developer API, developer portal or API documentation as of this profile.

companies.name: Laurentian Bank of Canada
companies.description: Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada) is a Montreal-headquartered Schedule I chartered bank, founded in 1846 as the Montreal City and District Savings Bank and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange as LB. With roughly CA$47 billion in assets, about 3,000 employees, and approximately 1.5 million clients, it serves personal, commercial, and capital-markets customers - concentrated in Quebec with commercial offices across Canada - through subsidiaries including B2B Bank, Laurentian Bank Securities, and LBC Capital. The bank operates no public developer portal and exposes no first-party or FDX-style data-access API; consumer data access is aggregator-mediated today (screen-scraping via providers such as Flinks and Plaid), and Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework remains legislated but not yet operational, so participation is voluntary. In December 2025 the bank announced a proposed sale to Fairstone Bank of Canada, with National Bank of Canada acquiring its retail operations.

companies.name: PC Financial
companies.description: PC Financial (President's Choice Financial) is the financial-services brand of Canadian grocery giant Loblaw Companies Limited. Its personal banking and Mastercard credit-card products are issued by President's Choice Bank, a federally chartered Schedule I bank and CDIC member, while insurance is offered through PC Financial Insurance. The digital-first, branchless brand centers on the no-fee PC Money Account (a Mastercard-network everyday spending account launched September 2020), a line of PC Financial and PC World Elite Mastercard credit cards, and deep integration with the PC Optimum loyalty program across Loblaw's grocery, pharmacy, and retail banners. Consumer banking (chequing, savings, mortgages) was transferred to CIBC's Simplii Financial in 2017, so PC Financial today is a rewards-linked digital banking arm rather than a full-service bank. In December 2025 Equitable Bank (EQB) agreed to acquire PC Financial from Loblaw for roughly $800 million. On open finance, PC Financial runs NO public first-party developer portal or API; Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking framework is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer account access today is aggregator/screen-scraping-based via providers such as Plaid and Finicity (Mastercard). The bank supports Interac e-Transfer on the PC Money Account as shared payments-rail participation.

companies.name: Prized
companies.description: Prized is an AI-powered platform that lets non-technical operations, support, and finance teams build, deploy, and share secure internal tools without engineering. Users describe a workflow in natural language (or bring their own coding agent such as Claude Code) and Prized builds real software on company data that is pre-connected and scoped, with least-privilege database access per tool, credential isolation, outbound-traffic proxying, and an audit trail on every access. Tools deploy behind corporate authentication and connect to 20+ services including Salesforce, Postgres, Slack, Stripe, and Notion. Prized is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company founded by Hudson Griffith and Marinos Eliades, both formerly of Gander (YC F24, acquired by Archer Aviation). Added to the API Evangelist network via the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from the company's public web surface.

companies.name: Samu
companies.description: Samu (samu.ai) is an AI-powered conversation-intelligence and sales-analytics platform built for sales managers and revenue leaders across Latin America. It automatically records and transcribes customer interactions across WhatsApp, phone calls, video calls, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet, then analyzes them to surface actionable coaching insights. Features include an AI "Samu Score" that evaluates call quality against customizable criteria, custom data extractors (e.g. competitor mentions or company size), analysis using SPICED, BANT, and SANDLER sales frameworks, and auto-generated CRM notes, tasks, and meeting summaries. Samu integrates bidirectionally with HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, and other CRMs, and emphasizes high-accuracy Spanish-language transcription. Programmatic inbound/outbound API access is available on the Enterprise plan, though no public developer documentation is published. Samu is backed by 500 Global.

companies.name: Simplii Financial
companies.description: Simplii Financial is the no-fee direct banking brand of the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC), one of Canada's Big Six Schedule I domestic banks. Launched November 1, 2017, Simplii succeeded CIBC's two-decade President's Choice Financial (PC Financial) co-venture with Loblaws, migrating roughly two million accounts to the new brand. Simplii is not a separately chartered bank; it operates as a division and trade name of CIBC under CIBC's Schedule I federal charter, offering no-fee daily chequing and savings, mortgages, personal loans, lines of credit, GICs, mutual funds, and USD accounts through online, mobile, and telephone channels only (no branches), with CDIC deposit insurance provided through CIBC. On open finance, Simplii exposes no first-party public developer API or developer portal; consumer financial-data access today is aggregator- and screen-scraping-based via Plaid, Finicity, and MX (CIBC signed a data-access agreement with MX), consistent with Canada's voluntary, pre-mandate posture while the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / FES 2024, overseen by the FCAC) is legislated but not yet operational.

companies.name: Webster Bank
companies.description: Webster Bank, N.A. is a nationally chartered commercial bank (National Association) and the principal banking subsidiary of Webster Financial Corporation (NYSE: WBS), a Delaware-incorporated bank and financial holding company headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut. A values-based super-regional institution with roughly $84 billion in assets, Webster serves businesses, individuals, and families across the Northeast from the New York City metro area through Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts, and operates the HSA Bank division, a leading national provider of health savings accounts and consumer-directed benefit administration in all 50 states. Webster does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications. Its open-finance posture is consumer- and commercial-permissioned data sharing delivered through aggregators rather than a direct API: in June 2026 Webster went live on Prolific Banking's FI-Streams Connector using Plaid's FDX-aligned Core Exchange specification to give commercial clients secure, tokenized connectivity to the Plaid network, and consumer account data is also reachable via Plaid and Finicity. There is no publicly documented first-party REST API, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, or self-serve developer program.

companies.name: Xfactor.io
companies.description: Xfactor.io is an AI-powered revenue operations platform founded by Mike Carpenter and backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its Growth AI engine, together with the Xfactor Central, OpenInsights, and Simulation products, builds a live digital twin of a company's go-to-market operations — connecting CRM, pipeline, usage, and financial data so revenue teams can test decisions through simulation before rolling them out. The platform is delivered as a closed B2B SaaS application (app.xfactor.io) and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or client SDKs; security posture is documented on a Secureframe trust center with a SOC 2 Type II attestation.

companies.name: Abacum
companies.description: Abacum is an AI-native financial planning and analysis (FP&A) platform built for CFOs and finance teams to connect financial data, automate planning and reporting, and align cross-functional teams. It unifies budgeting and forecasting, headcount and revenue planning, scenario modeling, investor and board reporting, and P&L / balance-sheet / cash-flow roll-ups, with 700+ prebuilt integrations across ERP and accounting systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, Xero, Dynamics 365), HRIS and payroll (Workday, Rippling, BambooHR, Gusto, Deel), CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), billing (Stripe, Chargebee, Maxio), and data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks). An Excel connector and embedded workflows keep planning models and actuals in sync. Abacum surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Creandum and Scale Venture Partners.

companies.name: Deluxe Corporation
companies.description: Deluxe Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Deluxe Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

companies.name: Serve First
companies.description: Serve First is a UK-based AI-driven customer experience (CX) platform that unifies reviews, surveys, receipts, in-location feedback terminals, operational audits, and mystery shopping into a single dashboard. It turns real-time customer feedback into role-based, actionable insight, with sentiment analysis and unified reporting across retail, hospitality, facilities management, health & wellness, and franchise businesses. Serve First also provides Client Connect journey/workflow automation and Martyn's Law public-protection compliance management. Serve First does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; this profile captures company identity plus verified security and compliance posture (SOC 2 and ISO 27001 via a Sprinto-hosted trust center).

companies.name: Vodafone
companies.description: Vodafone Group plc is a UK-headquartered (Newbury, England) multinational telecommunications company and one of the world's largest mobile and fixed network operators, with operations in 15 country markets and partner-market agreements covering 40+ additional countries across Europe and Africa. The group serves 279 million mobile customers, 5 million business customers, and manages 215+ million IoT connections through its Vodafone IoT platform. Beyond mobile and broadband connectivity, Vodafone operates one of the largest IoT/M2M businesses in the industry, invests in 70+ subsea cables, and runs financial services like M-PESA (Africa) and Vodapay. Through Vodafone Business it sells connectivity, cloud, security, and managed-mobility services to enterprises, and through the GSMA Open Gateway and CAMARA initiative it exposes a growing portfolio of standardised network APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Match, MVNO Discovery, and more) via the Vodafone Developer Marketplace (developer.vodafone.com), which publishes 27+ commercial and CAMARA APIs across Identity, Mobile, Analytics, Boost/QoS, and Partner categories. The Marketplace exposes sandbox and live endpoints under api-sandbox.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com and api.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com, with OAuth2 (Consumer Key / Consumer Secret) authentication and Postman collections for every product. Vodafone is a premier member of the CAMARA alliance hosted at the Linux Foundation, a founding participant in the GSMA Open Gateway, and one of the principal telco operators driving network-as-an-API adoption globally.

companies.name: CIBC
companies.description: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) is a Schedule I domestic chartered bank and one of Canada's Big Six, formed in 1961 through the merger of the Canadian Bank of Commerce and the Imperial Bank of Canada and headquartered in Toronto, Ontario. Serving roughly eleven million personal, business, commercial, wealth, and capital-markets clients across Personal & Business Banking, Wealth Management, and Capital Markets, CIBC is a participant in the shared Canadian rails, including Interac e-Transfer and Payments Canada settlement systems. Canada has no operational open-banking mandate today: the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework legislated in Budget 2024 and the 2024 Fall Economic Statement, overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC), is not yet live, so access remains voluntary and fragmented. CIBC runs no first-party public developer portal (developer.cibc.com does not resolve) and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger specifications. Consumer-permissioned data access is aggregator-mediated: CIBC signed a tokenized data-access agreement with U.S. aggregator MX (announced August 2022, MX's first in Canada) to let clients share financial data with third-party apps without exposing banking credentials, and its accounts are also reachable through Plaid (Assets, Auth, Balance). Corporate connectivity is offered through CIBC SWIFT Corporate Access (SCA) file exchange rather than a public REST API, so CIBC's honest public API surface today is aggregator-mediated only, pending the coming Consumer-Driven Banking regime.

companies.name: Collibra
companies.description: Collibra is a data intelligence company providing a cloud-based platform for data governance, cataloging, quality, lineage, and AI governance. The Collibra Data Intelligence Platform helps enterprises discover, understand, govern, and trust their data assets through automated lineage tracking, policy management, data observability, and collaborative stewardship. The Collibra developer ecosystem includes REST APIs, GraphQL Knowledge Graph API, workflow automation, and a broad library of source connectors.

companies.name: First Tech Federal Credit Union
companies.description: First Tech Federal Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in San Jose, California, and one of the largest credit unions in the United States. It was founded to serve employees of the technology industry and their families, and its membership is drawn heavily from workers at major technology employers. As an NCUA-insured credit union, First Tech offers consumer and business deposit accounts, lending, mortgages, credit cards, and wealth services delivered primarily through its website and mobile apps. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, First Tech publishes no first-party public developer portal or documented open API; consumer-permissioned financial data sharing is handled through third-party data aggregators (such as Plaid, MX, Finicity, and Akoya) rather than a directly documented first-party API surface. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented — the Financial Data Exchange (FDX) standard and the CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule are still emerging — and no first-party FDX-conformant data-access API or published Section 1033 posture was found for First Tech during this review.

companies.name: Quantum Metric
companies.description: Quantum Metric is a continuous product design and digital experience intelligence platform that captures and quantifies every user session across web and mobile, replaying interactions and surfacing friction, errors, and conversion opportunities in real time so that product, engineering, and customer-experience teams can prioritize work by quantified business impact. The platform exposes data-export and integration APIs to customers within their authenticated instance; during enrichment no public, unauthenticated developer portal or OpenAPI definition was discoverable (developer.quantummetric.com and docs.quantummetric.com redirect to the marketing site and the help center returns a maintenance page).

companies.name: America First Credit Union
companies.description: America First Credit Union is a federally chartered, NCUA-insured credit union headquartered in Riverdale, Utah, founded in 1939. With roughly $19 billion in assets, more than one million members, and about 124 branches across seven western states (Utah, Idaho, Oregon, New Mexico, Arizona, Nevada, and California), it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, America First operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. It provides no self-serve, publicly documented API surface; consumer-permissioned account data access is handled through third-party data aggregators and its core banking provider rather than a direct first-party API. No public FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented on its public website as of this bootstrap. This record is an honest identity profile with no fabricated API surface.

companies.name: Atlantic Union Bank
companies.description: Atlantic Union Bank is a Virginia state-chartered commercial bank with roots going back to 1902, and the principal banking subsidiary of Atlantic Union Bankshares Corporation (NYSE: AUB), a Richmond, Virginia bank holding company regulated under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956. It is the largest regional bank headquartered in Virginia, with roughly $37 billion in assets and a branch network across Virginia, Maryland, and North Carolina, offering consumer and business checking, savings, lending, mortgages, credit cards, and wealth management. Like most US regional banks, Atlantic Union Bank operates under the voluntary, fragmented US open-finance landscape rather than a mandated open-banking regime: it publishes no first-party public developer portal or documented public API. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached indirectly through third-party data aggregators (Plaid, Finicity by Mastercard, MX, Teller) as surfaced by aggregator coverage directories, and no direct FDX-conformant data-access endpoint, Akoya participation, or published CFPB Section 1033 posture was found. This is an identity-only, aggregator-only record with no first-party API surface.

companies.name: Inovalon
companies.description: Inovalon is a healthcare technology company providing cloud-based data analytics and data-enabled intervention platforms for the healthcare industry. Its Inovalon ONE Platform pairs national-scale primary-source datasets with analytics, workflow, and SaaS applications used by health plans, providers, pharmacies, life-sciences, and specialty organizations for risk adjustment, quality measurement, care-gap closure, and revenue-cycle and claims management (including the ABILITY provider workflow products). Inovalon was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Its developer surface is enterprise and auth-gated: the corporate site is WAF-protected and the API host api.inovalon.com requires authentication (HTTP 401); security and compliance posture is published on the public Inovalon Trust Center.

companies.name: Servus Credit Union
companies.description: Servus Credit Union Ltd. is a member-owned cooperative financial institution headquartered in Edmonton, Alberta, founded in 1938. It is Alberta's largest credit union and, following its 2023 member-approved merger with connectFirst Credit Union, became Canada's largest credit union by total assets (roughly $30 billion CAD), serving more than 500,000 members through about 100 branches and distributing profits back to members via its Profit Share program rather than to outside shareholders. As a provincially regulated Alberta credit union, Servus operates within a cooperative charter and offers retail and business banking, mortgages, loans, investments, and digital/mobile banking. On the open-finance front its posture is aggregator-only and honest: Servus runs no public first-party developer portal or documented public API. External data access to member accounts today is provided through third-party financial-data aggregators (Mastercard Open Banking / Finicity and Plaid) via consumer-permissioned connections, consistent with Canada's voluntary, not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC).

companies.name: F.N.B. Corporation
companies.description: F.N.B. Corporation (NYSE: FNB) is a diversified financial services holding company headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and the parent of First National Bank of Pennsylvania, an FDIC-insured, state-chartered commercial bank. With roughly $50 billion in total assets at year-end 2025, FNB is a regional super-community bank operating around 350 branches across seven states and Washington, D.C. (Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, West Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia), offering commercial banking, consumer banking and wealth management through its eStore digital platform. On open finance, FNB exposes NO first-party public developer portal or documented API: the developer/api subdomains of fnb-online.com redirect to the marketing homepage and no developer documentation is published. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), not a first-party FNB API. No direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership or public CFPB Section 1033 posture is documented by the institution as of this profile.

companies.name: Marcus by Goldman Sachs
companies.description: Marcus by Goldman Sachs is the U.S. consumer banking brand of The Goldman Sachs Group, launched in 2016 to offer no-fee high-yield Online Savings Accounts and Certificates of Deposit (CDs) directly to retail customers online. Deposits are held at Goldman Sachs Bank USA, a New York State-chartered bank and member of the Federal Reserve System, insured by the FDIC. After Goldman's broad retreat from consumer lending, Marcus no longer originates personal loans and now centers on digital deposit products. Marcus operates NO public first-party consumer developer API and runs no self-serve developer portal for its retail banking products; the Goldman Sachs Developer platform (developer.gs.com) serves institutional Transaction Banking and Marquee offerings, not Marcus consumer banking. Consumer-permissioned account data (balances, transactions, account/holder info) is reachable only through third-party open-finance aggregators such as Plaid, Flinks, and MX, not a documented Marcus API. As a bank chartered in the U.S., Goldman Sachs Bank USA is subject to the emerging CFPB Section 1033 personal financial data rights framework, but no first-party FDX-conformant Marcus developer interface is publicly documented as of this record.

companies.name: Praxis AI (Vortexify)
companies.description: Praxis AI is a Y Combinator (Fall 2024) company that now operates as Vortexify (vortexify.ai). Vortexify is an AI-native platform that generates operational software directly from a company's data: teams connect data sources through 20+ prebuilt connectors (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, BigQuery, Redshift, Snowflake, NetSuite, Oracle, S3, Azure Blob, Google Sheets/Drive, SharePoint and more), describe requirements in plain English, and AI agents plan, code, test and deploy backend logic plus custom frontends with no infrastructure to manage. The platform emphasizes building complete apps on operational data rather than just dashboards, with built-in scheduling, serverless compute execution, role-based access control, audit logs, sandboxed environments, token-based authentication, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. Praxis AI was founded by Aditya Tewari (ex-Palantir) and Ransika Liyanage (ex-Tesla, GM, Deloitte), originally focused on manufacturing-specific AI agents for predicting and preventing machine failures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator. Vortexify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification.

companies.name: Duetto Research
companies.description: Duetto Research is a hospitality technology company whose cloud platform, marketed as Duetto, delivers a Revenue & Profit Operating System (RP-OS) for hotels, casinos, and resorts. The platform pairs real-time dynamic pricing, demand forecasting, group and block business management, and profitability benchmarking so revenue teams can optimize rates and total property profit across more than 20,000 properties in over 100 countries. Its marquee products include GameChanger (dynamic pricing and rate optimization), ScoreBoard (forecasting and reporting), BlockBuster (group business), Advance (AI-driven rate recommendations), GameTime (select-service revenue management), and HotStats (profitability benchmarking). Duetto connects with the property management systems, booking engines, and channel managers hotels already use through a large partner-integration ecosystem rather than a self-serve public developer API. Backed by Battery Ventures; surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

companies.name: EcoMap Technologies
companies.description: EcoMap Technologies is an ecosystem intelligence software company (Baltimore, MD) that helps economic development organizations, chambers of commerce, universities, arts agencies, bioscience associations, and state and local governments map, connect, and measure their entrepreneurial ecosystems. Its platform turns scattered regional resource directories, referrals, and stakeholder relationships into a measurable, reportable network. Products span EcoMap Discover (resource hub and navigation), the Ecosystem Relationship Manager, an AI-powered Ecosystem ChatBot, the Economic Intelligence Monitor for regional benchmarking, and a Nonprofit Intelligence Dashboard. EcoMap reports 250,000+ resources mapped across 100+ ecosystems nationwide.

companies.name: Greenplaces
companies.description: Greenplaces is a sustainability and ESG reporting platform that pairs software with expert consulting to help companies — especially suppliers responding to enterprise requirements — measure their carbon footprint under the GHG Protocol and complete sustainability framework submissions including CDP, EcoVadis, SBTi, GRI, SASB/ISSB and GRESB. The managed-service platform also supports B Corp certification, CSRD readiness, SOC 2 and AI-governance compliance, and tracking of regulations such as California SB 253 and SB 261. Greenplaces is venture-backed by Felicis and Redpoint Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC portfolio data; the company publishes a managed product (app.greenplaces.com) but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: MidFirst Bank
companies.description: MidFirst Bank is a federally chartered savings association (thrift) headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, and owned by Midland Financial Co. Founded in 1982 with roots in Midland Mortgage from the early 1950s, it is the largest privately owned bank in the United States, with roughly $42 billion in assets and retail banking, private banking, commercial real estate lending, and nationwide mortgage servicing operations across Oklahoma, Arizona, California, Colorado, Nevada, Texas, and Utah. MidFirst does not operate a first-party public developer portal or publish downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications. Its open-finance posture is aggregator-mediated: through its "Open Access" program, MidFirst adds direct API connections between its Business Online Banking platforms and consumer-permissioned data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Stripe, Intuit, Mastercard/Finicity, Envestnet Yodlee, and Morningstar), replacing screen scraping. There is no publicly documented first-party API surface, and no FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is published on its site as of this review.

companies.name: Neo Financial
companies.description: Neo Financial is a Calgary- and Winnipeg-based Canadian fintech (neobank) founded in 2019 by the founders of SkipTheDishes, offering credit cards, savings, money, investing, and mortgage products to consumers. Neo is not a chartered bank and holds no Canadian banking licence; it delivers CDIC-eligible deposits and card issuance through regulated partner institutions — Peoples Bank of Canada for everyday accounts, ATB Financial as Mastercard credit-card issuer, and formerly Concentra Bank (now part of Equitable Bank) for savings. Neo operates a consumer mobile and web platform only and publishes no first-party public developer API or developer portal; third-party access to Neo accounts today is available solely through data aggregators such as Flinks (a National Bank-owned Canadian aggregator) and Plaid via credential/screen-scraping access, not a documented first-party API. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking (open banking) framework, legislated in Budget 2024 and overseen by the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, is not yet operational, so no first-party FDX or CDB data API exists. Neo maintains a public GitHub organization of internal engineering tooling and an engineering blog, but ships no public API products.

companies.name: Old National Bank
companies.description: Old National Bank is a nationally chartered, FDIC-insured regional commercial bank and the primary subsidiary of Old National Bancorp (NASDAQ: ONB), headquartered in Evansville, Indiana and Chicago, Illinois. With roughly $73 billion in assets and nearly 200 retail branches across Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Michigan, Minnesota, Tennessee, and Wisconsin, it is one of the largest commercial banks headquartered in the U.S. Midwest, offering consumer, small business, commercial, treasury management, and wealth banking. Old National does not operate a first-party public developer portal or publish any downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; probes of developer., api., and apis.oldnational.com do not resolve and /developers returns HTTP 404. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is instead reached through third-party financial data aggregators (Finicity by Mastercard is documented), which is the honest, aggregator-only open-finance posture typical of U.S. regional banks. No documented first-party FDX-conformant data-access API or published CFPB Section 1033 developer surface was found at review time.

companies.name: PortF
companies.description: PortF is an AI-powered portfolio monitoring platform for private equity, venture capital, and institutional investors. It automates investment data collection and reporting by extracting qualitative and quantitative data from emails, documents, and 25+ connected systems (Excel, OneDrive, SharePoint, SSO, Salesforce, FIS Global, Xero, QuickBooks, Sage, and NetSuite), then consolidates financial, ESG, and impact data into a single source of truth with real-time analytics, IRR benchmarking, and agentic reporting workflows. Founded by Alex Lu and headquartered in London, PortF is backed by Techstars.

companies.name: Valley National Bank
