companies.description: Valley National Bank is a nationally chartered commercial bank (OCC-regulated) and the principal banking subsidiary of Valley National Bancorp (NASDAQ: VLY), a regional financial holding company founded in 1927 with roughly $64 billion in assets and more than 200 offices serving consumers, families, and businesses across New Jersey, New York, Florida, Alabama, California, and Illinois. Its business spans consumer banking, commercial banking, and treasury services. As of this profile Valley National Bank operates no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable API specifications; consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached only through third-party open-finance aggregators (Finicity by Mastercard is documented, alongside general Plaid/Tink connectivity) rather than a directly exposed FDX-conformant or first-party API.

companies.name: Qognitive
companies.description: Qognitive, Inc. is an AI company that develops QCML (Quantum Cognition Machine Learning), an analytical AI architecture positioned as an alternative to classical statistical modeling. Its product, Hone, targets high-dimensional, multi-modal, and noisy structured data — claiming near-linear scaling with feature count and accuracy improvements over industry-standard models, with peer-reviewed backing in Nature Scientific Reports and Risk.net. Hone is distributed as first-party Python packages (hone-io community edition and hone-io-enterprise) exposing scikit-learn-compatible regression and classification wrappers. The company was surfaced as a Ribbit Capital portfolio company. There is no public REST/HTTP API surface; integration is via the Python SDK.

companies.name: AirPR
companies.description: AirPR is a public relations analytics and media measurement company whose software helped communications teams quantify the business impact of earned media, tie coverage to web traffic and conversions, and benchmark share of voice against competitors. AirPR is now part of Onclusive, the media intelligence platform that monitors and enriches conversations across 3M+ online sources, 70K+ print outlets, 6K+ broadcast channels, and 25+ social platforms for PR, communications, and marketing professionals. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: DecisionLink
companies.description: DecisionLink pioneered enterprise Customer Value Management (CVM), giving B2B sales, marketing, and customer-success teams a platform to quantify, present, and defend the economic value their products deliver to buyers. The company has since rebranded and relaunched as Xfactor.io, a revenue-operations AI platform that builds a "digital twin" of a company's go-to-market system: it unifies CRM, pipeline, usage, and finance signals into Xfactor Central, surfaces cross-source risk through Xfactor OpenInsights with plain-English alerts, and lets teams simulate growth scenarios before committing with Xfactor Simulation and Growth AI. Backed by Accel, the company sells to revenue and go-to-market leaders. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; security posture is published via a SecureFrame trust center (SOC 2 Type II).

companies.name: Snapsheet
companies.description: Snapsheet is a cloud-based property & casualty (P&C) claims management platform for insurance carriers, MGAs, and TPAs. It runs the full claims lifecycle with no-code workflow configuration, intelligent automation, document management, virtual vehicle appraisals, total-loss settlement, integrated claims payments, and analytics. Snapsheet reports serving 170+ customers, including 16 of the top 20 P&C carriers, and processing more than 400 million API calls per month. It exposes open APIs and webhooks to customers and partners for connecting policy, billing, underwriting, and vendor systems, though API access is arranged through its sales and partner channel rather than a public self-serve developer portal.

companies.name: State Employees' Credit Union
companies.description: State Employees' Credit Union (SECU / NCSECU) is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina. Founded in 1937 with 17 members and $437 in deposits, it is a state-chartered credit union regulated by the Credit Union Division of the North Carolina Department of Commerce and federally insured by the NCUA (NMLS #430055). SECU is the second-largest natural-person credit union in the United States by both assets and membership, serving nearly 2.9 million member-owners with roughly $56 billion in assets across 275 branches in all 100 North Carolina counties. Membership is primarily limited to North Carolina state employees and their families. On the open-finance front, SECU operates no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; its consumer digital banking (Member Access) supports connecting external accounts for aggregation, and outbound consumer-permissioned data sharing is handled through data aggregators rather than a documented first-party API. No public FDX-conformant data-access endpoint or CFPB Section 1033 data-rights posture is published as of July 2026.

companies.name: Syndio
companies.description: Syndio is an enterprise workplace-equity and compensation-governance software company. Its AI-assisted platform helps large organizations make defensible, compliant pay decisions at scale, spanning offers, promotions, merit cycles, and pay-equity/pay-transparency compliance (including EU Pay Transparency Directive requirements). The platform is organized into Essentials (foundations for aligned, compliant pay decisions), Decisions (real-time guidance during pay decision-making), and Predict (forward-looking workforce intelligence), all powered by the domain-specific Syndi AI. Syndio reports governing more than $1T in pay decisions for 350+ global enterprises. It is delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS accessed via the app with OAuth 2 / SSO; there is no public self-serve developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition. First-party developer-facing surfaces are limited to the syndioctl command-line tool and a public GitHub organization. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

companies.name: Dragonfly
companies.description: Dragonfly is a modern in-memory datastore built for performance and scalability, designed as a drop-in replacement for Redis and Memcached with improved efficiency and throughput. Dragonfly uses a multi-threaded, shared-nothing architecture to deliver significantly higher throughput with lower latency than Redis. It is fully compatible with Redis and Memcached APIs, requiring no code changes to migrate existing workloads.

companies.name: Hilbert's AI
companies.description: Hilbert's AI is an AI-native growth infrastructure platform for B2C companies, backed by a16z. It unifies fragmented product, marketing, and finance data into a single source of truth and layers agentic automation on top through four intelligence stages: Detect (anomalies, churn signals, and behavioral shifts), Reason (ML/deep-learning root-cause analysis and forecasting), Act (autonomous growth interventions such as churn plays and channel adjustments), and Optimize (continuous budget and strategy tuning). A natural-language interface lets growth, product, and finance teams collapse months-long decision cycles into minutes without writing code or navigating dashboards. Hilbert connects to existing data and paid-media stacks via prebuilt integrations (Meta, Google, Pinterest, Snapchat, Reddit, Google Analytics 4, Triple Whale, Klaviyo, Braze) and is SOC 2 certified. The product is delivered as a hosted application; there is no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

companies.name: Komprise
companies.description: Komprise is an unstructured data management company whose Intelligent Data Management platform analyzes, tiers, migrates and governs file and object data across NAS, cloud and object storage. The platform spans Komprise Analysis, Elastic Data Migration, Transparent Move Technology, Smart Data Workflows, the Global Metadatabase Service, KAPPA Data Services and Transparent File Tables, giving enterprises a single metadata layer for discovery, classification, sensitive-data detection, ransomware-attack-surface reduction, intelligent tiering and AI data preparation. Komprise publishes an llms.txt bot-access and content policy at www.komprise.com/llms.txt, but its product documentation portal at docs.komprise.com is authentication-gated and no public REST API reference, OpenAPI description, SDK or package was found on any public registry as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Ovation
companies.description: Ovation is an AI-first guest experience and feedback platform for restaurants, founded by Zack Oates and voted the #1 guest feedback platform in a RestaurantOwner.com survey. It uses a frictionless, SMS-based two-question survey to capture real-time guest sentiment on- and off-premise, then applies AI to categorize feedback across 35+ restaurant-specific topics, surface operational insights, generate guest-recovery responses, manage online reviews, and run text marketing campaigns. Ovation connects to 50+ POS, online ordering, and loyalty systems, including Olo, to source guest interactions. These are pre-built partner integrations; Ovation does not publish a public, self-service developer API or API reference. Where integration is technical it is inbound and partner-driven: for example, Ovation receives Olo webhook events (OrderPlaced, OrderClosed, OrderCancelled, GuestOptIn, UserOptOut, and similar) authenticated with a shared secret, and the connection is configured directly through the partner's customer success and developer teams rather than via a self-serve Ovation API. Integration access is arranged directly with the company.

companies.name: Uplevel
companies.description: Uplevel is an engineering intelligence platform for enterprises — an operating system for engineering transformation that helps leaders see team performance clearly, solve root causes, and sustain improvement in the AI era. The platform pulls data from existing tools and uses machine learning to produce engineering metrics and actionable insights: DORA metrics, time allocation and ML issue classification, deep-work and interruption measurement, developer-experience metrics, and AI-impact analysis, framed by the company's WAVE framework of engineering KPIs. Founded in 2018 and led by CEO Joe Levy, Uplevel is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Madrona Ventures, and Voyager Capital. Uplevel serves enterprise customers such as Xactly, Accolade, Braze, Avalara, and Qualtrics; it operates an internal API behind the product (api.uplevelteam.com, AWS API Gateway) but publishes no public developer API surface.

companies.name: Bank OZK
companies.description: Bank OZK is a regional bank headquartered in Little Rock, Arkansas, tracing its charter to 1903 and today operating roughly 265 offices across Arkansas, Georgia, Florida, North Carolina, Texas, and New York. It is a state-chartered commercial bank and the wholly owned subsidiary of Bank OZK holding company, publicly traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol OZK, with about $40.8 billion in total assets as of year-end 2025 and a national reputation in commercial real estate lending. Bank OZK runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; it is not a documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participant and has not published a specific CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture. Consumer-permissioned account data is reached only indirectly through third-party aggregators, with Plaid documented as the supporting aggregator. This is an honest identity-only profile with no public API surface.

companies.name: Barclays US
companies.description: Barclays US is the United States consumer banking arm of Barclays PLC, operated through Barclays Bank Delaware, a Delaware state-chartered bank headquartered in Wilmington. Doing business as Barclays US (barclaysus.com redirects to cards.barclaycardus.com), it is one of the largest co-branded credit card issuers in the country, running highly customized card programs for major travel, airline, retail, and affinity partners (JetBlue, American Airlines, Wyndham, AARP, Gap, and others), alongside small-business cards, installment loans, point-of-sale financing, and a direct-to-consumer online savings and CD franchise. Unlike Barclays UK — which operates a mandated PSD2 Open Banking API Exchange at developer.barclays.com — the US consumer entity publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, so consumer- permissioned account and card data from Barclays US is reached in practice through third-party data aggregators rather than a documented first-party API. No FDX-conformant data-access endpoint or formally stated CFPB Section 1033 posture is published on the US site as of this profile.

companies.name: DCU (Digital Federal Credit Union)
companies.description: Digital Federal Credit Union (DCU) is a not-for-profit, member-owned federal credit union headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts and regulated by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA), with roughly 1.18 million members, 23 branches across Massachusetts and New Hampshire, and nationwide access via the Co-Op shared-branch and surcharge-free ATM networks. It offers consumer and business banking, lending, mortgages, credit cards, and investment services, and has recently merged with First Technology Federal Credit Union. Like most US credit unions, DCU publishes NO public first-party developer API, developer portal, or downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specifications; consumer-permissioned account data is reached only indirectly through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) and its core banking provider, and there is no publicly documented FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access program. This is an honest identity-only record: no public API surface exists to catalog.

companies.name: Expert Intelligence
companies.description: Expert Intelligence is an AI company building analytical automation for pharmaceutical drug-development laboratories. Its platform turns raw instrument data into signed, regulatory-grade results and surfaces lab-wide trends across instruments, methods, and sites. Two integrated products anchor the offering: EI Flow automates batch analysis by converting instrument output into SOP-aware, signed, explainable results that reach LIMS systems in minutes so analysts review only exceptions, and EI Signal unifies historical data across instruments, methods, and sites to surface drift and anomalies before release. The company promotes exception-based review for higher accuracy, a Limited Sample Model (LSM) approach that needs only 30-50 expert examples, and instrument-agnostic deployment across cloud, on-premises, or hybrid environments. Backed by Sierra Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio and enriched from the company's public website; no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs were found at enrichment time.

companies.name: Fintary
companies.description: Fintary is an AI-powered commission management and revenue operations platform for insurance distribution — serving brokerages, carriers, and wealth firms. It automates compensation calculation and reporting across complex hierarchies, splits, overrides, and bonuses; reconciles carrier statement data; monitors chargebacks; surfaces real-time revenue and profitability analytics; and provides a white-label producer portal for 24/7 commission visibility. Fintary integrates with agency and distribution systems such as Applied Epic, Agency Integrator, SmartOffice, OneHQ, and BenefitPoint, and states it supports API connections to accounting, document management, and custom databases. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Fintary does not currently publish a public developer portal or API specification.

companies.name: First Nations Bank of Canada
companies.description: First Nations Bank of Canada (FNBC) is a Schedule I federally regulated chartered bank under the Bank Act, chartered on 19 November 1996 and headquartered in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan. It is the first Canadian chartered bank to be independently controlled by Indigenous shareholders — roughly 88% Indigenous owned and controlled by 78 Indigenous shareholder groups from Nunavut, Northwest Territories, Yukon, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Alberta and Quebec — and focuses on serving the Indigenous marketplace, with over 90% of its loans going directly to Indigenous communities, many of its branches on reserve, and CDIC-insured deposits. On the open-finance and API front, FNBC runs no first-party developer portal and publishes no public API: probes of developer.fnbc.ca, api.fnbc.ca and developers.fnbc.ca all fail to resolve, and the fnbc.ca site exposes only retail online-banking and a mobile app, not a documented API surface. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated via Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, with FCAC as overseer) is not yet operational, so third-party access to FNBC account data today is voluntary and effectively aggregator-mediated (Flinks, Plaid and similar), not a first-party open-banking API.

companies.name: Markt Pilot (aka MP)
companies.description: MARKT-PILOT GmbH is a German software company (registered in Beilstein, business address Stuttgart, with a US office in Chicago) that provides a unified pricing performance platform for industrial manufacturers. Its flagship product, MP ONE, combines an Intelligence Engine (real-time competitor and market data with AI-powered cross-reference part matching), a Decision Engine (cost-plus, market-based, and attribute-based pricing workflows), and a Performance Engine (portfolio, revenue, and margin analysis with executive dashboards). MARKT-PILOT serves 200+ manufacturers across agriculture, construction and mining, machine tooling, packaging, and industrial equipment, helping them move from static annual spare-parts pricing to dynamic, data-driven pricing. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners. The company operates a marketing site, blog, and a hosted (Better Stack) status page, but publishes no public developer/API surface: no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, well-known discovery endpoints, or client SDKs were found during enrichment.

companies.name: MedeAnalytics (JLL Partners)
companies.description: MedeAnalytics is a healthcare data and analytics company serving health insurance payers and risk-bearing provider organizations, positioning itself as a healthcare performance improvement company that turns claims, clinical, and operational data into actionable insight and measurable financial and quality results. Its platform spans Health Fabric, an AI-powered healthcare data fabric; AI Studio for ready-to-use and custom predictive models; Managed Action for workflow automation; and Integrated Analytics modules with embedded ROI tracking. Solution areas include MLR optimization, HEDIS/Stars quality performance, utilization and network management, value-based care, revenue cycle, population health, and social determinants of health (SDOH). The company was surfaced from a VC portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

companies.name: Medical Informatics
companies.description: Medical Informatics Corp. (MIC) is a Houston, Texas healthcare technology company behind the FDA-cleared Sickbay platform for virtual and remote patient monitoring. Founded in 2010 by Emma Fauss and Craig Rusin, Sickbay archives, aggregates, and transforms otherwise unrecorded high-resolution physiological waveform data across disparate, vendor-neutral biomedical devices to enable anytime, anywhere remote monitoring, TeleICUs, alarm management, workflow automation, and patient-centered predictive analytics and AI across the continuum of care. The company is backed by DCVC, Intel Capital, Catalio Capital, and the Texas Medical Center. Sickbay is a clinical SaaS platform with no public developer API surface; integration is delivered through the vendor as HL7/device connectivity.

companies.name: PDI Technologies (fka PDI Software)
companies.description: PDI Technologies (formerly PDI Software) is a global provider of software and data solutions for the convenience retail and wholesale petroleum industries, serving 200,000+ customers across 60+ countries. Its portfolio spans PDIQ (an AI foundation for convenience and fuel operations), PDI Enterprise wholesale petroleum software, ERP and back-office systems, POS and store systems, logistics, loyalty marketing, fuel and mobility payments, an offer network, insights and analytics, cybersecurity (PDI Security and Network Solutions, formerly Echosat), and the consumer app GasBuddy. PDI is backed by Insight Partners and has grown through acquisitions including P97 Networks. The company exposes no public self-serve developer/API portal; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

companies.name: Pedestal Health (formerly Target RWE)
companies.description: Pedestal Health, formerly Target RWE (and NoviSci), is a Durham, North Carolina real-world evidence and health-data company serving life sciences organizations and health systems. It generates regulatory-grade real-world evidence from large-scale observational data and longitudinal patient cohorts across hepatology, dermatology, and gastroenterology (including the TARGET-NASH, TARGET-Derm, and TARGET-Gastro registries), supporting clinical development, regulatory strategy, and care delivery. The company operates as a data, research, and services provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched from the company's public website (targetrwe.com now redirects to pedestalhealth.com).

companies.name: Protege
companies.description: Protege (Protege Health Inc.) is a two-sided data platform that connects AI model builders with high-quality, real-world proprietary datasets for pre-training, post-training, fine-tuning, and evaluation. It curates data from hundreds of sources across healthcare, video, audio and speech, motion capture, architecture/engineering/construction, manufacturing, energy, finance, and agriculture, handling licensing and rights protection while fairly compensating data rights holders. Protege also operates DataLab, a research team focused on data-for-AI challenges. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, CRV, Bloomberg Beta, Footwork, Flex Capital, SV Angel, Liquid, and Shaper Capital. As of this enrichment pass Protege publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and web properties.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

companies.name: Bluefish AI
companies.description: Bluefish AI is an enterprise AI marketing platform built for Fortune 500 brands to gain visibility and control over how they are represented across AI channels. The platform spans AI monitoring of brand reputation in AI-native experiences, generative engine optimization (GEO) to improve performance across AI search, GEO measurement frameworks, and agentic commerce tooling for AI-driven buying journeys. It serves search, content, brand, and PR teams. Founded by martech veterans whose prior advertising technologies are now owned by Microsoft and Meta, and backed by enterprise and AI investors including Bloomberg Beta and Threshold Ventures. Bluefish does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Datafy
companies.description: Datafy is a location-analytics and advertising platform, founded in 2018 and headquartered in Ogden, Utah, that helps destinations and communities turn visitation, spending, and behavioral signals into marketing decisions. It serves travel and tourism boards, attractions, downtowns, retail partners, and civic organizations with three core offerings — data analytics, targeted advertising, and real-world attribution — alongside Tally, an attendance-measurement product. The company reports 500+ clients and states that it maintains SOC 2 compliance. Datafy operates a client portal at portal.datafyhq.com; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Datumate
companies.description: Datumate is a construction technology company whose cloud-native SaaS platform, DatuBIM, turns drone imagery, laser-scanning, and site data into real-time progress tracking, deviation detection, automated reporting, and actionable analytics for heavy civil infrastructure projects. It serves asset owners, general contractors, and engineering and consulting firms across roads, highways, rail, bridges, and earthworks, giving multi-site visibility from design validation through construction to final inspection. The company reports 125+ active customers, thousands of managed sites, and tens of thousands of processed drone flights. Datumate has Israeli engineering roots (Technion) with leadership based in Miami, Florida, and is backed by Battery Ventures.

companies.name: Enurgen
companies.description: Enurgen is a solar energy software company whose DUET platform uses 3D physics-based modeling to optimize photovoltaic assets across their entire lifecycle. The platform spans three products - Design, Construction, and Operations - helping large-scale solar developers, independent power producers, EPC engineers, and asset managers improve energy yield estimates, validate construction against expected performance, and monitor plants in production to close the gap between forecasted (P50) and actual field output. Enurgen is a Techstars-backed company; customers include Scatec, Potentia, Lightsource, Eni, and Kiewit. The company operates a customer web application at app.enurgen.com but does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile is an enrichment pass that captures the company's public web properties and domain security posture.

companies.name: Foresight
companies.description: Foresight is a predictive project-delivery platform for complex construction and infrastructure megaprojects, with a particular focus on data centers, government, and critical infrastructure. Founded by Dr. Atif Ansar and Igor Shifrin (Oxford) and headquartered in London, it layers on top of existing scheduling tools such as Microsoft Project and Excel to turn raw schedule data into forecasts, risk assessment, delay prediction, and portfolio-wide project assurance. The company reports managing $100B+ in mission-critical projects and is backed by Creandum and Macquarie Capital. Foresight is delivered as a SaaS web application and does not publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Georama
companies.description: Georama is now QualSights (qualsights.com), a consumer-insights research technology company that helps brands understand human behavior across the product lifecycle. The platform combines Smart Sensors that passively capture product consumption and usage in real time, a participant app that collects video, photo, and survey feedback, and an AI-powered analytics layer that turns that data into actionable insights. Marquee offerings include UseSights (Physical AI for product usage), VoiceSights (AI-moderated conversations), and the moment-based XMOT feedback method, spanning opportunity identification, concept optimization, product development, pre-launch validation, market launch, and acceleration. Georama entered the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead; QualSights publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time.

companies.name: Gravel AI
companies.description: Gravel AI is a beauty and personal care market intelligence platform that turns alternative data into early trend, ingredient, brand, and product signals for the global cosmetics industry. It offers a suite of analysis tools — application and ingredient trends, brand and market deep dives, consumer review analysis, new brand and product launch monitoring, ingredient supplier and OEM mapping, and product analyzers — alongside curated datasets, market reports, and an enterprise data/API service that delivers licensed beauty data into customer pipelines (API, Snowflake, S3). Backed by Techstars, Gravel AI serves beauty brands, ingredient and contract manufacturers, and enterprise insights, R&D, procurement, and data teams. Its flagship Gravel Early Trends product positions against incumbents such as Euromonitor, Mintel, NielsenIQ, Circana, WGSN, and Spate.

companies.name: Greyparrot
companies.description: Greyparrot is a London-based AI waste analytics company that turns materials recovery facilities (MRFs) into data-driven operations. Its Greyparrot Analyzer uses computer-vision cameras mounted over waste conveyor belts to identify, count, and measure the composition of waste streams in real time, giving recyclers continuous visibility into what flows through their plant. The Greyparrot Sync product routes that analytics stream into existing operational control systems, ERP platforms, Power BI dashboards, and OEM sortation hardware (robotic arms, air-jet systems, balers, belt control), while Deepnest turns real-world recovery data into design feedback for packaging brands. Backed by Speedinvest, Greyparrot serves recyclers, equipment manufacturers, and consumer-goods companies working to raise recycling rates and automate compliance reporting. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web, product, and content surface.

companies.name: KITRO
companies.description: KITRO is a Swiss company founded in 2017 in Zurich that helps professional kitchens measure and reduce food waste through AI-powered automation. Its KITRO TARE device pairs an IoT scale with a camera and computer vision to automatically identify, weigh and categorize discarded food with no change to kitchen workflow, feeding a cloud analytics dashboard that surfaces waste trends by time, item and station, compares performance across properties, and exports reports for sustainability and EU food-waste compliance reporting. KITRO serves hotel groups and resorts, hospitals and care homes, corporate canteens, universities and schools, and river and ocean cruise operators in 20+ countries, with customers including Marriott, Hyatt, TUI BLUE, Pestana, 25hours Hotels and Sydney Opera Bar. KITRO publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal — the only customer-facing software surface is the authenticated dashboard at my.kitro.ch — but it does publish an llms.txt agent-readable company description at www.kitro.ch/llms.txt.

companies.name: LocateAI
companies.description: LocateAI (Locate) is an AI-integrated commercial real estate brokerage focused on retail site selection for multi-unit and franchise brands. Its platform pairs proprietary AI models with full-service advisory to help brands choose markets, source and score sites, forecast Year-1 revenue and cannibalization risk, right-size franchise territories, and negotiate leases — from the first market through the signed lease. The models analyze 200M+ mobile devices and 1,100+ variables for device-level trade-area, fair-share, and time-weighted revenue analysis. Locate is delivered as a managed service; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company.

companies.name: Marketing Evolution
companies.description: Marketing Evolution is a marketing measurement and analytics company that provides an AI-driven operating system for marketing operations. Its platform unifies audience data, media exposure, third-party signals, and proprietary sources into a single view of marketing performance and customer behavior, connecting strategy, creative, media, and measurement through an AI-powered loop that enables real-time campaign adaptation rather than static launches. Core products include its Data Platform and Decision Engine, delivering unified marketing measurement (UMM) and person-level attribution to enterprise marketers. The company is backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification.

companies.name: National Bank of Canada
companies.description: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada, TSX: NA) is a Schedule I chartered bank headquartered in Montreal, Quebec, founded in 1859. It is the sixth-largest of Canada's Big Six banks and the leading bank in Quebec, serving personal, commercial, wealth-management, and financial-markets clients. On open finance, National Bank is a notable first-mover: it was the first major Canadian bank to launch a secure, consent-based data-sharing API for retail customers, but it does NOT operate a public self-serve first-party developer portal. Programmatic access to customer financial data is delivered through aggregators rather than a downloadable public API — principally Flinks, the Montreal aggregator in which National Bank holds an ~80% stake, via its Open Banking Environment (OBE), and also through Plaid. National Bank and Flinks are founding participants of the FDX Canada working group, aligning their data-sharing on the FDX technical standard, and the bank is positioning ahead of Canada's forthcoming, legislated-but-not-yet-operational Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / FCAC oversight). Today access is voluntary and aggregator-mediated; there is no operational open-banking mandate and no public first-party API surface.

companies.name: ODAIA
companies.description: ODAIA is a commercial intelligence platform for the pharmaceutical industry, using AI to replace manual analysis and static annual segmentation with real-time, predictive insights. Its products (ODAIA Field, Marketing Intelligence, and Opportunity Analysis) help pharma field reps, brand marketers, and commercial operations teams identify the right healthcare professionals (HCPs), prioritize outreach, and surface untapped prescription opportunities. ODAIA integrates with Veeva CRM to deliver insights directly inside existing rep workflows. It is a Toronto-based, enterprise-focused SaaS vendor backed by Threshold Ventures; the product is sold via sales/discovery calls rather than a self-service public API.

companies.name: omniX labs
companies.description: omniX labs is a New York-based AI machine-vision analytics company (owned by EverWash) serving car wash, oil-change/lube, and related quick-service automotive businesses. Its platform ingests real-time video of the physical business, applies computer vision and AI to synthesize customer interactions, and returns operational insights that help operators boost throughput, optimize staffing, prevent loss, predict demand, and grow revenue. omniX labs was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. It operates a customer web portal but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface at this time.

companies.name: Rwazi
companies.description: Rwazi is a hyper-local market intelligence and Decision AI platform whose product, Sena, combines a company's internal business data with real-world consumer signals from 190+ countries — who is buying what, for how much, from where, when, and why — using consumer activity data, computer vision, zero-party data collection, and 250+ third-party integrations to inform marketing, sales, product, strategy, and growth decisions. Rwazi is a Techstars-backed company added to the API Evangelist network. This profile has been enriched from public web sources; at the time of enrichment Rwazi published no self-service developer API, OpenAPI, or public API reference — onboarding is enterprise, demo-driven, and account-based.

companies.name: Solovis
companies.description: Solovis is a multi-asset investment analytics and portfolio management software platform for institutional investors, including endowments, foundations, pension plans, outsourced CIOs (OCIOs), and family offices. It aggregates data across public and private asset classes into a single dashboard for portfolio modeling, performance analysis, risk analytics, and reporting. Core products include Portfolio Analytics, Risk Analytics, Predict (performance and risk prediction for asset allocation), Risk Pro (factor-based risk analytics, formerly Venn Pro), and Analyst Services for outsourced data capture and portfolio data aggregation. Solovis became part of Nasdaq's investment intelligence business following its 2020 acquisition. The platform is delivered as a private, authenticated SaaS accessed through a client login; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, OpenAPI specification, or `/.well-known/` discovery surface. The host api.solovis.com exists but is fully authentication-gated (HTTP 401) with no public specification.

companies.name: Kriptos
companies.description: Kriptos is an AI-driven unstructured data security platform that automatically discovers, classifies, and labels documents across endpoints, servers, and cloud storage, then feeds that business and risk context into the DLP, CASB, SIEM, EDR, and IAM tooling an organization already runs rather than replacing it. The platform spans data discovery and classification, data compliance and risk management, data access governance across Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, insider threat management with UEBA, DSPM, and AI governance covering shadow-AI monitoring for tools such as Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini. Classification results are written back as native Microsoft Purview and Google Drive labels. Founded in Ecuador and backed by Techstars, Kriptos reports more than 1.2 billion documents classified for over 150,000 users, with customers concentrated in banking, insurance, healthcare, and utilities across Latin America. Kriptos is a sales-led product and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation.

companies.name: Sallie Mae Bank
companies.description: Sallie Mae Bank is a Utah state-chartered industrial bank (industrial loan company) founded on November 28, 2005 and headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, operating as the FDIC-insured banking subsidiary (FDIC cert #58177) of SLM Corporation (NASDAQ SLM), the publicly traded, S&P 400 consumer-finance company best known as the largest originator of private student loans in the United States. Beyond student and education lending, the bank offers retail deposit products including high-yield savings accounts, money market accounts, and certificates of deposit through salliemae.com. Sallie Mae Bank does not operate a first-party public developer program - there is no developer.salliemae.com portal, no api.salliemae.com host, and no published OpenAPI/Swagger definitions. Consumer account and transaction data is reachable only on a permissioned basis through third-party data aggregators (historically Plaid), and no first-party FDX data-access API or published CFPB Section 1033 data-rights posture could be confirmed. This is an identity-only, aggregator-access record reflecting the honest reality that this institution exposes no public API surface.

companies.name: Turquoise Health
companies.description: Turquoise Health is a healthcare price transparency company (backed by a16z) that runs a platform aggregating and normalizing hospital and payer machine-readable price transparency files, negotiated contract rates, and out-of-network pricing into searchable, benchmarked rate data and analytics. Its products span rate analysis and benchmarking, contract management, clear rates and data assets, healthcare transactions, out-of-network pricing, patient cost estimates / Good Faith Estimates, and price-transparency compliance tooling, serving providers, payers, life sciences, and employers.

companies.name: Compstak
companies.description: CompStak is a commercial real estate (CRE) data platform, founded in 2012, that crowdsources and verifies lease comps, sale comps, loan data, and property data from a network of tens of thousands of brokers and appraisers across US markets. Its products include CompStak One (an all-in-one CRE data platform), CompStak Exchange, CompStak AI, and a contact-sales Data API offering Market Insights, Property Insights, Space Insights, and Property Standardization. CompStak was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Its developer surface is enterprise/contact-sales only — there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or API reference.

companies.name: Cyral
companies.description: Cyral is a data security and governance platform (founded 2018, Milpitas CA; acquired by Varonis in March 2025) that provides an agentless, stateless data-layer sidecar for monitoring and governing access to data repositories such as Snowflake, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Amazon S3, Kafka, and Oracle. Cyral was built API-first: its Control Plane exposes a REST API secured with OAuth2 client-credentials, fully automatable through the official Cyral Terraform provider (cyralinc/cyral) and supporting Terraform modules for AWS, Azure, and Okta. Following the Varonis acquisition, cyral.com now redirects to Varonis' Database Activity Monitoring product, but the first-party developer tooling remains published on the cyralinc GitHub organization and the Terraform Registry.

companies.name: GoodShip
companies.description: GoodShip is a freight orchestration and procurement platform for shippers, brokers, and asset-based carriers. It unifies TMS tender, contract-award, and location data, enriches it with real-time market rates, and layers AI-assisted bid analysis (via its Laney AI transportation analyst), lane- and carrier-level performance analytics, carrier scorecards, and in-app collaboration on top. Teams run mini-bids and full-network RFPs, benchmark spend against the market, and take corrective action without dedicated developer resources. Plug-and-play with major transportation management systems; backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and serving US and Canadian operations.

companies.name: kWh Analytics
companies.description: kWh Analytics is a Beaverton, Oregon based managing general agent and data-analytics firm that underwrites property and performance insurance for renewable energy assets — solar, wind, and battery storage. Founded in 2012 and acquired by specialist insurer Beazley in 2023, the company operates what it describes as the industry's largest solar performance database, covering roughly 30% of U.S. solar assets across 300,000+ renewable energy assets and $100B+ in loss data. Its HelioStats platform ingests unstructured asset production documents (via AWS S3, Box, Dropbox, email attachment, or API) and applies OCR and machine learning to extract, validate, standardize, benchmark, and enrich operating data for investors, lenders, and asset owners. Commercial products include data-driven Property Insurance, the Solar Revenue Put credit enhancement, the Wind Proxy Hedge, and the SolarScape market intelligence offering. kWh Analytics also publishes the annual Solar Risk Assessment industry report. There is no public developer portal, published API reference, or machine-readable API specification — data delivery and the HelioStats ingest API are arranged through enterprise engagement.

companies.name: Paramark
companies.description: Paramark is a marketing measurement and forecasting platform that helps growth and finance teams understand the true incremental impact of their marketing spend. Founded in 2022 by Pranav Piyush and Pete Belknap and backed by Greylock, Paramark combines incrementality testing, marketing mix modeling (MMM), and scenario planning in one place, augmented by human growth advisors and AI agents. Rather than relying on last-touch attribution, the platform uses statistics and machine learning to quantify each channel's incremental contribution across search, social, TV, and out-of-home, giving marketers defensible ROI numbers to bring to their finance teams. Paramark maintains an open-source Marketing Mix Modeling workbench and forks of the major MMM libraries under its paramark-inc GitHub organization. Paramark does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; API access is offered as a feature of its Advanced commercial tier.

companies.name: CIBC Bank USA
companies.description: CIBC Bank USA is an Illinois state-chartered, FDIC-insured commercial bank (FDIC Cert #33306) headquartered at 120 South LaSalle Street in Chicago, Illinois. Formerly The PrivateBank and Trust Company, it was acquired in 2017 and rebranded, and today operates as a wholly owned US subsidiary of Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) through the intermediate holding company CIBC Bancorp USA Inc. The bank focuses on commercial banking, capital markets, wealth management, trust services, private banking, and cross-border services for clients with North American operations, rather than mass-market retail. As a US regional institution, CIBC Bank USA publishes no first-party public developer portal or open API program; consumer-permissioned account and balance data is reached only through third-party aggregators such as Plaid, and the CIBC group has a data-access agreement with MX. It is not a documented direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participant and has published no explicit CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture, making its honest API surface aggregator-mediated only.

companies.name: Doczen
companies.description: Doczen is an enterprise AI transformation platform that connects business signals to actionable outcomes, helping large organizations adopt AI in days rather than months. The product uses AI agents to interview employees and aggregate signals from communication and productivity tools to surface operational issues, then ranks the resulting opportunities by financial impact, ROI, feasibility, and urgency. It guides implementation through buy-vs-build decisions and vendor recommendations, and runs a continuous monitoring loop that tracks progress and measures business impact. Doczen targets enterprises across financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, energy, technology, and transportation and logistics, and integrates with hundreds of tools. It advertises an enterprise security and compliance posture (ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, EU AI Act) via a Vanta-hosted trust center. Doczen is backed by Seedcamp and was added to the API Evangelist network from the Seedcamp portfolio; it currently exposes no public developer API.

companies.name: Groundspeed
companies.description: Groundspeed is an insurance data and analytics company that pioneered AI-powered extraction and standardization of unstructured commercial property and casualty (P&C) insurance documents — loss runs, schedules of values, ACORD forms, and broker submissions — turning them into structured, analytics-ready data for underwriters, brokers, and carriers. Founded in Ann Arbor, Michigan and backed by Insight Partners, Groundspeed was acquired by Insurance Quantified, where its technology now powers the Intake, Workflow, and Intelligence products of an AI-driven underwriting platform serving commercial P&C carriers and MGAs. Groundspeed does not currently publish a public developer program, API reference, or self-service onboarding surface; this profile tracks its identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Meridian Credit Union
companies.description: Meridian Credit Union is Ontario's largest credit union and one of the largest in Canada — a member-owned financial cooperative headquartered in St. Catharines and Toronto, serving more than 365,000 members with roughly CAD $31 billion in assets under management, over 2,200 employees, and more than 75 years of history. Formed in 2005 through the merger of Niagara Credit Union and HEPCOE Credit Union, Meridian offers personal, business, and wealth banking and owns Meridian OneCap Credit Corp. (commercial equipment leasing and financing); it previously operated the federally chartered digital bank motusbank, which was wound down in 2023. As a provincially regulated Ontario credit union — overseen by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA), with member deposits insured under Ontario's credit-union deposit-insurance scheme — Meridian is a cooperative, not a Schedule I or Schedule II bank. It publishes no first-party public developer API and no downloadable OpenAPI specification. Consumer-permissioned account-data access today is aggregator-mediated rather than first-party: Plaid maintains a Meridian institution connector, and the Central 1 / Flinks Outbound seam provides API-based data sharing for member credit unions. Canada's federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (legislated in 2024 with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada / FCAC as overseer) is not yet operational, so Meridian's open-finance participation remains voluntary and aggregator-based.

companies.name: Popular (Banco Popular)
companies.description: Popular, Inc. (NASDAQ: BPOP), operating as Banco Popular, is a publicly traded financial holding company founded in 1893 and headquartered in Hato Rey, San Juan, Puerto Rico. It is the largest bank in Puerto Rico and operates through two chartered depository segments: Banco Popular de Puerto Rico (BPPR), serving Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Popular Bank (formerly Banco Popular North America), a New York state-chartered commercial bank serving mainland U.S. markets including New York, New Jersey, and Florida. Popular is FDIC-insured and regulated as a U.S. bank holding company. On its open-finance and API posture, Popular does not publish a first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications for its U.S. institutions (popular.com); consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is made available indirectly through third-party data aggregators such as Plaid, Tink, and Finicity rather than a direct bank API. This identity record reflects that honest reality — an aggregator-only access model with no documented first-party API surface, FDX membership, or published CFPB Section 1033 data-access program. (Note: the separate apiportal.popularenlinea.com open-banking portal belongs to Banco Popular Dominicano / Grupo Popular, a distinct Dominican Republic company, not to Popular, Inc.)

companies.name: Prosperity Bank
companies.description: Prosperity Bank is a Texas-chartered commercial bank (member FDIC, NMLS ID 466414) and the banking subsidiary of Prosperity Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: PB), a Houston, Texas based regional financial holding company with roughly $37-43 billion in total assets and 300-plus full-service branches across Texas and central Oklahoma. It offers consumer and commercial banking, treasury management, mortgage, and wealth services, and has grown largely through acquisitions (LegacyTexas, Lone Star State Bancshares, American Bank Holding, Southwest Bancshares, Stellar Bancorp). On open finance, Prosperity Bank operates no first-party public developer portal or documented API: developer. and api. subdomains do not resolve, and no /developers or /api pages exist. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (Finicity/Mastercard Open Banking, Plaid, and similar), not a directly published bank API. No FDX-conformant data-access API or CFPB Section 1033 posture is publicly documented by the bank as of this review.

companies.name: RB2B
companies.description: RB2B is a US-focused B2B website visitor identification platform that resolves anonymous web traffic into person-level leads — names, LinkedIn profiles, hashed and plaintext business emails, mobile ad IDs, and full business profiles — and pushes them to sales, marketing, and ad-tech systems. The product is delivered as a JavaScript pixel plus a knowledge- base and pipeline of 50+ destination integrations (Slack, Microsoft Teams, Salesforce, HubSpot, Clay, Zapier, Apollo, Customer.io, Demandbase, and others), with global company-level identification and US-only person- level resolution. RB2B operates a separate API Partner Program at api.rb2b.com that exposes credit-metered Identification endpoints (IP → HEM, IP → MAID, IP → Company Domain) and Enrichment endpoints (HEM → LinkedIn, HEM → Business Profile, HEM → MAID, LinkedIn → Email, LinkedIn → Phone, Email → LinkedIn, Email → MAID) for SaaS developers, GTM engineers, retailers, and ad-tech platforms that want to embed identity resolution into their own apps and identity graphs. The platform is SOC 2 Type II certified.

companies.name: Santander US
companies.description: Santander Bank, N.A. (santanderbank.com) is the US retail and commercial banking subsidiary of Spain's Banco Santander S.A., headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. It is a nationally chartered bank (National Association, regulated by the OCC) operating a branch network across the Northeast US (Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Delaware), which positions it as a super-regional bank. Unlike UK and Australian institutions bound by mandated open-banking contracts, and unlike US banks such as Capital One or Chase that publish first-party developer portals, Santander Bank N.A. exposes no public, first-party developer API for its US retail franchise: developer.santanderbank.com does not resolve, and the site publishes no developers/API/open-banking pages. Consumer-permissioned data access in the US is available today through aggregators rather than a direct API — Plaid supports "Santander - Personal" (Assets, Auth, Balance and Transactions). Santander's UK developer portal (developer.santander.co.uk) and the group's Corporate & Investment Banking API marketplace (apimarket.santandercib.com) are operated by separate legal entities and are not the US retail bank's surface. This record is an honest identity profile of a super-regional bank whose US open-finance posture is aggregator-mediated, with no documented first-party developer program.

companies.name: Security Service Federal Credit Union
companies.description: Security Service Federal Credit Union (SSFCU), headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative federally chartered and insured by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). It is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, serving members across Texas, Colorado, and Utah with consumer and business banking, deposit accounts, credit cards, auto and mortgage lending, and investment services through branches, online banking, and mobile apps. Its open-finance posture is the norm for a US credit union: there is no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specification, and no public FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API is documented. Consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party aggregators, and any API capability is delivered through its core banking provider rather than a self-serve developer program.

companies.name: SouthState Bank
companies.description: SouthState Bank, National Association is an OCC-chartered national commercial bank headquartered in Winter Haven, Florida, and the principal subsidiary of SouthState Bank Corporation (NASDAQ: SSB). Formed through the 2020 merger of South State Corporation and CenterState Bank and redomiciled to Florida in 2025, it holds roughly $67 billion in assets and operates across the Southeast, Texas, Colorado, and Virginia. Like most US regional banks, SouthState runs no public first-party developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger definitions. Consumer-permissioned data access is delivered through third-party aggregators rather than a direct API: the Open Banking Tracker records SouthState reachable via Plaid only, with no documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) endpoint and no published CFPB Section 1033 data-access surface. Its open-finance posture is therefore aggregator-mediated, not a self-serve developer program.

companies.name: StorSimple
companies.description: StorSimple was a Santa Clara, California hybrid cloud storage company founded in 2009 by Ursheet Parikh and Guru Pangal. Its appliances combined primary storage, tiered cloud archiving, deduplication, compression, and encryption behind iSCSI/SMB interfaces, backed by $31.5M from Index Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Ignition Partners, and Mayfield Fund. Microsoft acquired StorSimple in November 2012 and folded it into Azure as Azure StorSimple (8000 series physical and virtual arrays, plus the StorSimple Data Manager). The product is managed through Azure Resource Manager under the Microsoft.StorSimple resource provider and its REST API. Azure StorSimple reached end-of-life in December 2022 and is out of support; Microsoft directs customers to Azure File Sync and Azure Files.

companies.name: Clickable
companies.description: Clickable is a marketing analytics and digital advertising platform founded in 2006 that serves as an ads and analytics partner for businesses and agencies. The company builds award-winning pay-per-click (PPC) advertising tools for search and social campaigns and delivers customized reporting that cuts through data overload so marketers can focus on the metrics that matter. Clickable also offers VIN retention reporting purpose-built for automotive dealerships to improve customer retention. Backed by Union Square Ventures, the company focuses on relationship-driven managed advertising and analytics services rather than a public developer API.

companies.name: Cube
companies.description: Semantic layer and headless BI platform with a GraphQL API for querying measures, dimensions, and segments across any SQL database or data warehouse.

companies.name: Denta
companies.description: Denta is a San Francisco-based dental practice management and automation platform, founded by Jack Beecher (Jack Beecher LLC, dba Denta) and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch). Positioned as "the dental practice that runs itself," Denta embeds AI into dental organizations to automate back-office operations: it ingests fragmented data from a practice's existing software, provides analytics so dentists can understand their business, and runs in the background to handle administrative work such as insurance payment posting. Its roadmap includes all-in-one native practice management software and an "autonomous dental practice." As of this profile Denta publishes a marketing site, a blog, and login and legal pages, but no public developer portal, API, or OpenAPI surface has been located.

companies.name: Kindor
companies.description: Kindor is a performance-intelligence platform for technology teams that turns engineering, project-management, finance, and HR activity into automated metrics, reports, and smart notifications. It integrates with tools like GitHub, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Notion, Google Calendar, and Google Meet to track DORA delivery metrics, resource allocation across initiatives, AI-tool adoption and ROI, and productivity anomalies, giving technology leaders real-time visibility and AI-generated summaries so they can align tech investments with business goals without manual reporting. Kindor claims outcomes such as lower tech operating costs, faster delivery, and less time spent on reporting. It is a 500 Global portfolio company; the public website is a Wix site that exposes a live Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint for agentic access, but Kindor publishes no first-party product API or developer portal.

companies.name: PenFed Credit Union
companies.description: PenFed Credit Union (Pentagon Federal Credit Union), founded in 1935 and headquartered in McLean, Virginia, is a federally chartered credit union regulated by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) and one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly 2.9 million members and tens of billions of dollars in assets. It is a not-for-profit, member-owned financial cooperative that originally served the U.S. military and defense community and now offers open membership, providing mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, personal loans, and deposit accounts. On the open-finance front, PenFed runs an internal API-management practice — MuleSoft/Anypoint is the backbone of its digital-banking platform and an Apigee-backed developer portal host exists at developer.penfed.org (with an api.penfed.org gateway) — but neither surface is publicly documented or openly reachable: there is no public developer program, no published OpenAPI, and consumer account data is made available to members through permissioned third-party aggregators such as Plaid rather than a directly documented FDX or CFPB Section 1033 data-access API.

companies.name: Tamr
companies.description: An enterprise data management company that uses machine learning to automate the mastering, enrichment, and classification of messy data across disparate sources. Helps large organizations unify customer, supplier, and product data to power analytics and AI initiatives.

companies.name: Velvet
companies.description: Velvet is a multimodal AI model R&D company (the "multimodal data lab") based in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch. It partners with frontier AI labs and enterprises to build state-of-the-art video datasets and evaluation frameworks that improve models' spatial reasoning and interactive, low-latency capabilities. Velvet operates an invite-only platform for sourcing and contributing multimodal training data, with contributor payouts via Stripe and Wise. It was founded by Lucas Mantovani (CEO, formerly video data at Meta FAIR) and Lucas Tucker (CTO, formerly Adobe). As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK.

companies.name: Brilliant
companies.description: Brilliant is a consumer-first interactive STEM learning platform that delivers bite-sized, problem-solving-driven courses in math, computer science, data science, and science to over 10 million learners on web, iOS, and Android. Brilliant for Educators offers free Premium access to K-12 teachers and students, with Google Classroom roster sync, COPPA/FERPA/GDPR compliance, and a teacher portal for class management. Brilliant does not publish a public developer API or partner SDK — the product is consumer- and classroom-facing, and integration with school ecosystems is limited to Google Classroom roster sync.

companies.name: Brilliant
companies.description: Brilliant is an online learning platform for interactive STEM education, covering mathematics, computer science, data, and science. Headquartered in San Francisco and used by over ten million learners worldwide, Brilliant pairs guided, problem-first lessons with adaptive practice that blends classic intelligent tutoring systems, machine-learning recommender systems, and natural-language conversations. The platform is delivered through brilliant.org and native iOS and Android apps, with a freemium model and a Brilliant Premium subscription that unlocks the full course catalog, including expanding AI-powered features such as personalized tutoring conversations and on-the-fly generation of interactive content. Brilliant operates as a direct-to-consumer subscription business with an educator program for classroom access; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration program, and the `github.com/brilliant` org on GitHub is an unrelated namespace of personal projects rather than an official Brilliant presence.

companies.name: Crosschq
companies.description: Crosschq is a hiring intelligence platform that helps talent acquisition and people-analytics teams improve quality of hire. Its cloud product suite spans AI-powered interview agents, automated reference checks, candidate assessment and screening, identity and interview-fraud detection, and quality-of-hire analytics that tie hiring decisions back to on-the-job outcomes. Crosschq connects to major applicant tracking and HCM systems (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Greenhouse, iCIMS, Oracle, Lever, Ashby, Bullhorn, and others) through pre-built integrations rather than a public self-service API. Founded in Danville, California, the company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and GGV Capital.

companies.name: Hub
companies.description: Hub (Hub.xyz) is a distributed physical-AI data infrastructure company that creates, annotates, and curates custom real-world datasets — egocentric first-person video, image, video, and audio — used to train AI and robotics models. Data is sourced through a global network of 500,000+ retail contributors and verified small and medium businesses across 150+ countries and 100+ languages. Hub offers both off-the-shelf labeled datasets and bespoke, custom-scoped data collection projects quoted within hours, delivered through a fully managed pipeline that couples automation with human-in-the-loop validation for frontier AI labs and Fortune 500 companies.

companies.name: Sankun
companies.description: Sankun (산군) is a South Korean construction-industry big data platform based in Seoul that aggregates and sells access to eight integrated construction databases covering roughly 280,000 construction companies, some 820,000 project sites, government e-procurement bids, contract awards, professional reputation reviews, and construction news. Alongside its web application and a construction sales CRM (Sankun Sales), the company markets a Sankun API (data.sankun.com) for programmatic access to its construction data, though public developer documentation is gated behind sales and login. Sankun is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

companies.name: Startup Ranking
companies.description: Startup Ranking is a platform that tracks, ranks, and indexes startups worldwide based on web presence, social metrics, and growth signals. It provides startup discovery, competitive benchmarking, and market intelligence for investors, entrepreneurs, and researchers.

companies.name: Envelop Risk
companies.description: Envelop Risk is a technology-led reinsurance underwriting and analytics firm specializing in cyber and other complex, emerging risks. The company combines actuarial science, machine learning, and cyber threat intelligence to model, price, and underwrite cyber (re)insurance for insurers, MGAs, and capital-market partners. Its platforms include CyberTooth (cyber risk modeling and augmented underwriting), Cyber Threat Intelligence, Envelop Capital Markets, and Envelop Risk Solutions (product development, analytics, modeling support). Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Envelop Risk surpassed a $1bn gross-written-premium milestone. This API Evangelist profile was created as a portfolio-company lead; the company does not publish a public developer portal, API, or SDKs at this time.

companies.name: Ohalo
companies.description: Ohalo is a data governance company whose Data X-Ray platform discovers, classifies, redacts, and governs unstructured data across enterprise file systems, databases, and cloud stores at petabyte scale. Using generative AI for content categorization and extraction, it helps organizations inventory sensitive data, audit access entitlements, automate redaction, and prepare their data estates for AI adoption while meeting regulatory frameworks such as GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI DSS. Ohalo is backed by 500 Global, Anthemis, and Craft Ventures.

companies.name: RethinkDB
companies.description: RethinkDB is an open source, distributed document-oriented NoSQL database designed for real-time applications, with push-based change feeds, native JSON storage, and an expressive query language called ReQL. Applications interact with RethinkDB through official client drivers (JavaScript, Python, Java, Ruby) that speak the native JSON driver protocol over TCP, rather than through an HTTP REST API. ReQL also includes an r.http command that lets queries pull data from external HTTP APIs directly.

companies.name: 8base
companies.description: 8base is a comprehensive Backend-as-a-Service platform that transforms the entire software development lifecycle by providing AI-assisted design, auto-generated serverless GraphQL infrastructure powered by AWS, and low-code full-stack App Builder tools. The platform enables developers and digital agencies to build scalable, production-grade cloud applications with SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance options without managing DevOps complexity.

companies.name: Appwrite GraphQL
companies.description: Appwrite GraphQL is a powerful API layer that exposes the full Appwrite backend-as-a-service platform through a GraphQL interface, allowing developers to query and mutate any resource type including databases, storage, users, and functions. It mirrors the complete Appwrite REST API (except OAuth) with GraphQL advantages such as selection sets and query batching, enabling precise data fetching and multiple operations in a single request.

companies.name: EdSights
companies.description: EdSights is a student voice and engagement platform for higher education. It pairs an AI-powered SMS chatbot with real-time analytics to collect continuous feedback from students, surface persistence and well-being risk, and flag individuals who need staff intervention. Its Student Voice Score (SVS) benchmarks student satisfaction the way NPS benchmarks customers, and institutional dashboards help retention, advising, and student-success teams act on that feedback throughout the academic journey. EdSights serves 290+ colleges and universities and connects to campus systems — Banner SIS, Slate, Salesforce, Starfish, EAB Navigate360, and Pharos — via SFTP data feeds. The company is Techstars-backed. As of this profile EdSights exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhooks; integration is data-file (SFTP) based, so most API-artifact enrichment is not applicable.

companies.name: Udacity
companies.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

companies.name: Alpharank
companies.description: Alpharank is a no-code sales guidance and digital-origination analytics platform for banks and credit unions. It analyzes funded loan and deposit applications to reveal which marketing tactics, channels, and campaigns actually drive funded dollars, then guides institutions to optimize their online branch, curb funnel abandonment, and turn ad spend into higher-quality leads. Its products include Optimizer, AdSync, and CRMSync, and it serves roughly 200 financial institutions nationwide. Originally recognized for turning payment transaction data into customer influence graphs, Alpharank is a 500 Startups / 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Alpharank publishes a marketing and client-login presence but no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface.

companies.name: Artemis Health
companies.description: Artemis Health (now Artemis by Nomi Health) is a healthcare data analytics platform that helps employers, benefits advisors, and health plans see every healthcare dollar clearly, cut waste, and improve care for their members. The platform unifies medical, pharmacy, and other benefits data to deliver cost analysis, program evaluation, automated reporting, custom analytics, and social-determinants-of-health insights for self-insured organizations. Artemis was acquired by Nomi Health in 2022. The product is a login-gated B2B SaaS application; no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface is published. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and enriched with the verifiable public identity, link, and domain-security signals available.

companies.name: Azara Healthcare
companies.description: Azara Healthcare provides population health management, data analytics, and quality reporting solutions for community health centers, safety-net providers, and physician practices. Its flagship platform, Azara DRVS (Data Reporting and Visualization System), aggregates clinical, claims, and social determinants of health (SDOH) data into unified dashboards, quality measures, eCQM and UDS (Uniform Data System) reporting, patient registries, and care-gap analytics. Related products include Azara Cost & Utilization, Azara Patient Outreach, Azara Care Connect, and value-based care reporting. Azara is backed by Insight Partners and serves the safety-net and federally qualified health center (FQHC) market. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead; the provider publishes no public developer portal or API at this time.

companies.name: Certivity
companies.description: Certivity is a Munich-based RegTech company, founded in 2021, that operates an AI-native regulatory intelligence platform for regulated industries such as automotive, aerospace, and connected vehicles. Its product, Certivity Core, turns complex regulations, standards, and internal documents into structured, machine-readable, engineering-ready requirements with full traceability and real-time monitoring of legal changes across 50+ jurisdictions. The platform digitizes and structures regulatory content from publishers such as ISO, IEC, CEN, CENELEC, ASTM, UL, and SAE using a proprietary ingestion pipeline and a regulatory knowledge graph, and integrates directly into engineering workflows (including Jama Connect) via an official API. Backed by Earlybird, High-Tech Gruenderfonds, UVC Partners, and Almaz Capital, Certivity added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and enrichment lead.

companies.name: SchoolsFirst FCU
companies.description: SchoolsFirst Federal Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned credit union headquartered in Tustin, California, serving educators and their families. Founded in 1934 as Orange County Teachers Credit Union, it is the largest credit union in California and one of the largest in the United States, with roughly $31.9 billion in assets, over 1.4 million members, and about 70 branches. It offers savings, checking, loans, mortgages, credit cards, and investment services. Like most US credit unions, SchoolsFirst runs no first-party public developer program: probes of developer.schoolsfirstfcu.org fail to resolve and /developers returns 404, and its api.schoolsfirstfcu.org host is the member online-banking login backend, not a documented API. Consumer-permissioned data access is available only through open-finance aggregators (Plaid, Finicity, MX, Akoya) rather than a direct API. No public FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented at this time.

companies.name: Verana Health
companies.description: Verana Health is a healthcare real-world data (RWD) and analytics company that transforms de-identified electronic health records from more than 90 million patients across 50+ EHR systems into curated, disease-specific datasets for life sciences and clinical research. Its VeraQ population health data engine harmonizes, tokenizes, and links structured and unstructured EHR data, claims, and medical images using clinician-directed curation, natural language processing, and machine learning, delivering Qdata modules across ophthalmology, urology, and neurology. Verana partners with medical specialty societies (including the AAO IRIS Registry) to power trial design, site and patient identification, real-world evidence studies, and quality-measure reporting. The company is HIPAA-compliant and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV. No public developer API or developer portal is published as of this profile.

companies.name: BlueOcean
companies.description: BlueOcean is a Context AI platform purpose-built for marketing teams. Its agentic AI framework, Spark, combines brand, market, product, and customer context to help marketers unlock creativity, accelerate go-to-market, and deliver measurable impact — automating work from strategy through content creation, competitive intelligence, brand performance analytics, and reporting. The platform surfaces evidence-grounded recommendations across brand, product marketing, and content, and is used by enterprise marketing teams at companies such as SAP, AWS, and Cisco. BlueOcean is backed by Insight Partners.

companies.name: Clay
companies.description: Clay is a go-to-market platform that combines people and company data enrichment from 150+ premium providers, AI research agents (Claygents), intent signals, and workflow automation for sales, marketing, and revenue operations teams. Clay exposes inbound HTTP API endpoints and webhooks so external systems can push records into Clay tables, trigger enrichments, and receive enriched data for CRM sync, lead scoring, and outbound workflows.

companies.name: IBM Db2
companies.description: IBM Db2 is a family of data management products from IBM that includes relational and hybrid database servers running on cloud, distributed, and z/OS platforms, supporting transactional, analytical, and AI workloads. Db2 exposes RESTful services that let applications create, discover, execute, and manage user-defined services natively against the database, and IBM Db2 as a Service on IBM Cloud provides a managed REST API for administering and querying cloud-hosted Db2 databases. Authentication is performed via HTTP basic auth, client certificates, or IBM Cloud IAM Bearer tokens depending on the deployment.

companies.name: Mobileum
companies.description: Mobileum is a telecom analytics and intelligence software vendor whose Active Intelligence Platform delivers AI-powered decisioning, risk management, and network insight for mobile network operators.
