GreenQ was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (also backed by URBAN-X) and added to the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: InsightEra
companies.description: InsightEra Co., Ltd. is a Bangkok-based marketing technology and data intelligence company that builds ready-to-use online marketing tools from social network data. Its platform spans social research (social listening and competitor analytics), social management (omni-channel management and chatbots), social data and analytics (Customer Data Platform and CRM), and social campaigns (campaign targeting and analytics), alongside a Thai NLP service and a generative enterprise AI platform. InsightEra positions its "Intelligence Model" as an ecosystem that connects external intelligence (market, customers, competitors, society) with internal organizational data so brands can turn insight into interaction and action. The company was surfaced as a portfolio lead of lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, documentation, or specification surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public identity only.

companies.name: Ruedata
companies.description: Ruedata (RueData AI) is an AI predictive tire-management software platform for commercial fleet operators. It combines a smart digital inspection app, the TLGX precision tire-measurement device (tread depth to +/-1/32nd and pressure to +/-0.25 percent), and a centralized web platform to help fleets prevent tire blowouts, cut maintenance costs, extend tire lifecycle, and improve road safety. Its business-intelligence layer applies predictive analytics for tire wear and route optimization, and it integrates with major telematics providers such as Samsara, Geotab, Netfleet, and Traffilog plus ERP systems via direct API connections. Ruedata is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer API, API reference, SDKs, or developer portal.

companies.name: Springboard
companies.description: Springboard is an online education company offering mentor-led, career-focused bootcamps and courses in software engineering, data science, data analytics, UX/UI design, cybersecurity, and machine learning. Programs pair a structured, self-paced curriculum with 1:1 industry mentorship, career coaching, and a job guarantee on eligible tracks. Springboard was surfaced from a 500 Global portfolio list and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it operates as a consumer/B2B learning platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, so this profile carries identity and security-posture signals rather than API artifacts.

companies.name: Duetto
companies.description: Duetto is a San Francisco–headquartered hospitality technology company providing a cloud-based Revenue and Profit Operating System (RP-OS) for hotels, casinos, resorts, and independent properties. Duetto's platform combines dynamic pricing, demand forecasting, group business optimization, benchmarking, and reporting to help hospitality operators optimize room rates, profitability, and total revenue performance. Core products include GameChanger (real-time dynamic pricing engine), ScoreBoard (forecasting and reporting dashboard), BlockBuster (group business optimization), Advance (AI-powered demand forecasting), HotStats (profitability benchmarking), and GameTime (select-service hotel revenue management). Duetto serves over 7,500 properties in more than 100 countries, with customers including Meliá, Sonesta, Virgin Hotels, and Sandman Hotel Group. Duetto integrates with major property management systems (PMS), central reservation systems (CRS), booking engines, and channel managers including Cloudbeds, Oracle OPERA / OHIP, Mews, Sabre, Amadeus, SiteMinder, and Infor. Duetto exposes an Open API for technical integration partners but does not publish a public, self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI specification — API access is partner-only and gated through a structured onboarding process with a self-testing toolkit. Revenue is generated through SaaS subscriptions to its revenue management products.

companies.name: Filmgrail
companies.description: Filmgrail is an Oslo, Norway based software company offering an AI-powered digital platform for cinema operators. Its product suite bundles a cinema content management system (CMS), native iOS and Android mobile apps, branded cinema websites, and marketing and analytics tooling into a single managed offering, with a loyalty system, festival platform, push notifications, and a planning tool layered on top. Filmgrail markets these capabilities as a way to automate cinema operations and grow digital ticket sales and moviegoer engagement, and describes API-based integration between its platform and cinema point-of-sale systems, websites, and mobile apps. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from Oslo, Norway and Delaware, USA. Filmgrail does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

companies.name: Motif Analytics
companies.description: Motif Analytics was a startup (founded 2021 by Mikhail Panko and Theron Ji, with Sean Taylor as chief scientist) building interactive sequence analytics for growth and operations teams. Its product let analysts explore event sequences — user journeys, funnels, order-management flows — with a purpose-built Sequence Operations Language (SOL) and in-browser WebAssembly so data never had to leave the browser, backed by a $5.7M seed round led by Amplify Partners and Felicis (2024). As of this enrichment pass the product site and the docs.motifanalytics.com subdomain no longer resolve and motifanalytics.com serves a MarkMonitor brand-protection holding page, indicating the company has wound down. No public REST/GraphQL API, SDK, OpenAPI, CLI, or developer surface was ever published; the sole public GitHub repo is a 2023 bug reproduction.

companies.name: Operand
companies.description: Operand is an AI-enabled pricing and commercial strategy platform for consumer retail, founded in 2024 and backed by Felicis, Y Combinator, SV Angel, and Soma Capital. It applies proprietary AI systems — an autonomous "agent swarm" — to set pricing and promotion strategy for mid-market and enterprise brands and retailers managing thousands of SKUs, volatile demand, and thin margins, running simulations to benchmark margin, revenue, and inventory-turn objectives before automating price changes. Operand is delivered as a managed platform with expert support and request-a-quote pricing rather than a public developer API; it currently publishes no OpenAPI, developer portal, or self-serve SDKs. An earlier Operand product at operand.ai offered an embeddings / semantic-search API with Python, Go, and TypeScript SDKs, now discontinued.

companies.name: Reniac
companies.description: rENIAC Inc. is a Santa Clara-based data acceleration company whose flagship product, the rENIAC Data Engine (rDE), is a drop-in accelerator for open source and NoSQL databases such as Apache Cassandra. Combining FPGAs with proprietary software, rDE speeds storage, network, and compute operations and can be deployed as a hardware-optimized cache, a transparent data-acceleration proxy, or a scalable storage engine on-prem, hybrid, or in the cloud (including early availability on AWS). rENIAC targets ultra-low-latency, real-time workloads — AI/ML, fraud prevention, payment processing, electronic trading, and recommendation engines — claiming up to 10x throughput, 13x lower latency, and significant TCO and CPU reductions. rENIAC ships an infrastructure/hardware acceleration product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe.

companies.name: Alliant Credit Union
companies.description: Alliant Credit Union is a federally chartered, member-owned credit union headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, regulated by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). Founded in 1935 as the United Airlines Employees' Credit Union and rebranded Alliant in 2003, it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with more than 800,000 members and over $19 billion in assets. Alliant operates as a digital-first, branchless institution offering consumer and commercial deposit accounts, high-yield savings and checking, credit cards, auto and home loans, and business banking. Like nearly all U.S. credit unions, Alliant publishes no public first-party developer API or developer portal; consumer-permissioned data access is available to members only through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a directly documented open-finance API.

companies.name: Canadian Western Bank
companies.description: Canadian Western Bank (CWB) is a Schedule I domestic chartered bank founded in 1988 (through the merger of the Bank of Alberta and Western & Pacific Bank) and headquartered in Edmonton, Alberta at Canadian Western Bank Place. Historically the largest publicly traded Schedule I bank headquartered in Western Canada and listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: CWB), it held roughly CA$43 billion in assets and focused on full-service business and commercial banking, personal banking, equipment financing and leasing, trust services, and wealth management across a network of affiliated entities. In June 2024 National Bank of Canada agreed to acquire CWB in an all-share deal valued at roughly CA$5 billion, and the acquisition closed in early 2025; CWB now operates as a subsidiary of National Bank of Canada and its branches and brand are being wound down and rebranded under National Bank. Consistent with Canada's voluntary and still fragmented open-finance landscape — the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework was legislated in 2024 (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement, overseen by the FCAC) but is not yet operational — CWB publishes no first-party public developer portal and no documented public API. Its developer and API hostnames do not resolve, and the entire cwbank.com domain now 301-redirects to National Bank of Canada (nbc.ca). Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reached only indirectly through third-party data aggregators (Plaid is confirmed via aggregator coverage directories). No first-party FDX-conformant data-access API was found. This is an honest identity-only, aggregator-only record for an institution now absorbed into National Bank of Canada.

companies.name: Data.ai
companies.description: Data.ai (founded as App Annie in 2010, rebranded to data.ai in 2022) was a mobile app market-data and analytics provider, offering estimates of app downloads, revenue, usage, and competitive market intelligence across the iOS App Store and Google Play for publishers, brands, and investors. The company historically exposed a market-data API (api.data.ai) for programmatic access to app performance and store intelligence. Data.ai was acquired by Sensor Tower in 2024 and now operates as a Sensor Tower company; its standalone site is a gated login and the former public API host serves a default page, so its independent API surface has been consolidated into Sensor Tower and effectively retired. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an ivp portfolio company.

companies.name: dezhentech
companies.description: Dezhen Technology (德臻) is a Shanghai-based healthcare information technology company providing informatization solutions for public hospitals and medical institutions across China. Its portfolio spans hospital operations management centers, integrated electronic medical record (EMR) systems, information integration platforms, hospital data centers and big-data analytics, refined operations management dashboards, EMR interoperability testing, and domestic (localized) technology transformation of core hospital systems. Dezhen is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. As of this profile the company publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications.

companies.name: Ecovate
companies.description: Ecovate (Ecovate Energy Indices) is an Israeli energy-data company that operates a platform for the wholesale electricity market price index. It publishes benchmark indices and analytics tracking wholesale electricity market prices, giving energy suppliers, large consumers, traders, and regulators a transparent reference for the cost of electricity in the wholesale market. Ecovate was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. The company's public presence is a marketing/product site (Hebrew and English editions) and it does not currently publish a developer program, public API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

companies.name: First West Credit Union
companies.description: First West Credit Union — rebranded Tru Cooperative Bank in 2026 — is a member-owned Canadian cooperative financial institution headquartered in Langley, British Columbia. Formed in 2010 by the merger of Envision Credit Union and Valley First, and later joined by Island Savings and Enderby & District Financial, it operates those four regional brands over a shared branch network with roughly 291,000 members, about $20.8 billion in total assets, 45 branches, and around 1,300 employees. After members voted in 2021 for federal continuance, it received a federal charter under Canada's Bank Act and became a federal credit union / cooperative bank (CDIC-insured) as of April 1, 2026. On the open-finance front First West / Tru runs no first-party public developer portal and publishes no downloadable OpenAPI or partner API; both developer.firstwestcu.ca and developer.trucooperativebank.ca resolve to nothing (NXDOMAIN). Third-party access to member account data today is aggregator-based (screen-scraping via providers such as Plaid and Flinks), the fragmented and voluntary Canadian norm while the federal Consumer-Driven Banking framework (Budget 2024 / Fall Economic Statement 2024, overseen by the FCAC) remains legislated but not yet operational.

companies.name: Golden 1 Credit Union
companies.description: Golden 1 Credit Union is a state-chartered, member-owned not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Sacramento, California, and is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, serving roughly 1.1 million members across California with approximately 20 billion dollars in assets. Founded in 1933 and open to all Californians, it offers consumer checking, savings, credit cards, auto and home loans, and digital banking, and holds the naming rights to Golden 1 Center in Sacramento. Like most US credit unions, Golden 1 publishes NO public developer portal and NO first-party public API; its digital banking runs on a core-provider platform, and consumer-permissioned account data is reachable only indirectly through third-party data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a documented first-party open-finance API. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and this institution's public API surface is honestly empty as of this record.

companies.name: Healthy Labs
companies.description: Healthy Labs is a healthcare and insurance technology company that powers a portfolio of digital health brands driving membership growth for Medicare and ACA (Affordable Care Act) insurance providers. Its offerings center on consumer lead generation, compliance and operational analytics, and member acquisition and retention optimization for the health-insurance market. The company has since rebranded as MPA (mpa.com), positioning itself as an AI-powered platform for licensed insurance professionals and agencies. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, this profile is enriched from public sources; no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, or API surface was found at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: LeapStack
companies.description: LeapStack (栈略数据 / Stack Strategy Data) is a Shanghai-based insurance technology and data-analytics company operating in China's health-insurance sector, applying big-data and risk-control intelligence to help insurers with claims, underwriting, and healthcare-cost analysis. It is a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and Qiming Venture Partners. Its public web presence (www.leapstack.tech) is a client-rendered marketing site; as of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or other public API surface was found. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

companies.name: Mantis
companies.description: Mantis (Mantis Biotech) builds predictive digital twins of individual people, aggregating personal data streams — wearables, digital activity, and clinical records — into high-fidelity models by combining large language models with physics-based simulation. The company positions itself as a neutral intermediary for personal predictive models — an "OAuth for identity" or "Plaid for banking" layer — letting individuals grant scoped, revocable access to their twin to healthcare providers and third-party builders. Applications include pre-symptomatic infection detection, cognitive baseline monitoring, heart-failure decompensation forecasting, medication-adherence prediction, post-operative recovery trajectories, psychiatric relapse early warning, and running trials on twins. Mantis is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company; as of this profile it publishes a marketing site and manifesto but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Manulife Bank
companies.description: Manulife Bank of Canada is a Schedule I federally chartered bank and a wholly-owned subsidiary of The Manufacturers Life Insurance Company, part of Manulife Financial Corporation. Launched in 1993 as Canada's first branchless (direct) bank — and the first federally regulated bank opened by an insurance company in Canada — it operates entirely through online banking, a mobile app, and telephone banking, with no physical branches. It is best known for the Manulife One all-in-one account, the Advantage Account, GICs, mortgages, and lines of credit that connect everyday banking and borrowing with long-term financial planning. Manulife Bank publishes no first-party public developer portal or downloadable API specifications; no developer.manulifebank.ca host resolves, and the public site is bot-protected. Canada's Consumer-Driven Banking (open-banking) framework — legislated in Budget 2024 and the Fall Economic Statement 2024, with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada (FCAC) as overseer — is legislated but not yet operational, so consumer financial data access today is voluntary and occurs through financial-data aggregators (Plaid, Flinks, MX) rather than a first-party bank API. Interac e-Transfer is offered as a consumer feature but is not exposed as a documented public API.

companies.name: Mountain America Credit Union
companies.description: Mountain America Credit Union (MACU) is a federally chartered, member-owned not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Sandy, Utah, founded in 1936 and regulated and insured by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA). It is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly $21.9 billion in assets, more than 1.4 million members, and over 100 branches serving Utah, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, and Arizona, offering consumer and business checking, savings, mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and wealth services. Like the vast majority of US credit unions, Mountain America exposes no public first-party developer API or developer portal: there is no developer.macu.com or api.macu.com host, and every path under macu.com returns the same client-rendered application shell. Consumer-permissioned data access is intermediated through its core banking provider and data aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a directly published API. US open finance is voluntary and fragmented, and no public FDX participation or CFPB Section 1033 data-access posture is documented for this institution at the time of review.

companies.name: Prime Life Science
companies.description: Prime Life Science (璞睿生命科技) is a Chinese life-science technology company focused on digital and intelligent (数智化) clinical research. Its business spans the full lifecycle from clinical research to commercial decision-making, offering digital innovation solutions built on big data and artificial intelligence. The company positions itself as a "digital intelligent clinical research accelerator" aimed at driving innovative drug and device development, health management, and improved clinical-research decision-making and operational efficiency in China. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the Qiming venture fund and added to the API Evangelist network; the public presence is a WordPress marketing site with no developer or API surface discovered during enrichment.

companies.name: ScoreData
companies.description: ScoreData Corporation is a Palo Alto based predictive-analytics and AI/ML platform company founded in 2014 by Danny Yang, Vas Bhandarkar, Mudit Chandra and Prasanta Behera. Its flagship ScoreFast platform, paired with iMaaS (intelligent Models as a Service), lets cross-functional AI teams develop, deploy, monitor, manage and govern machine-learning models in production across Banking, Insurance and Healthcare. ScoreFast uses patented dynamic machine learning that learns continuously, removing the need to manually regenerate predictive models, and its applications can be deployed across in-store, mobile, web, kiosk, chatbot and cloud contact-center touchpoints. ScoreData is backed by 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company awaiting a public developer/API surface.

companies.name: Suncoast Credit Union
companies.description: Suncoast Credit Union is a state-chartered, federally insured (NCUA), member-owned not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Tampa, Florida. Founded in 1934 as Hillsborough County Teachers Credit Union, it is the largest credit union in Florida and one of the largest in the United States, serving well over a million members across Florida counties with more than $17 billion in assets. It offers consumer and small-business deposit accounts, lending, cards, and digital banking through a web presence (the brand's canonical domain is now suncoast.com, with the legacy suncoastcreditunion.com 301-redirecting to it) and an online/mobile banking platform hosted on banking.suncoastcreditunion.com. As is typical for a U.S. credit union, Suncoast publishes NO first-party public developer API and operates no developer portal: no developer or api subdomain resolves for either suncoastcreditunion.com or suncoast.com. Consumer-permissioned data access is available only through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) and its digital-banking core provider rather than a direct API. There is no publicly documented Financial Data Exchange (FDX) participation and no published CFPB Section 1033 open-banking posture. This is an identity-only API Evangelist record reflecting an honest "no public API, aggregator-only" reality.

companies.name: The Data Guild
companies.description: The Data Guild is a San Francisco-based venture studio, founded in 2013, that builds data-driven companies addressing challenges in healthcare, life sciences, renewable energy, and climate change. Steeped in machine learning, data science, and artificial intelligence, the Guild pioneers a co-creation model that converts LP capital into equity across a portfolio of new ventures while applying its own team's efforts directly rather than simply allocating capital. It brings products to market through spinouts, alongside portfolio-company teams, and with strategic partners. Investors include Bloomberg Beta, David Gutelius, and Silicon Valley Data Capital. The Data Guild operates a marketing/company website and publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or MCP surface; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe.

companies.name: VyStar Credit Union
companies.description: VyStar Credit Union is a member-owned, not-for-profit financial cooperative headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida. Founded in 1952 as Jax Navy Federal Credit Union to serve military members at Naval Air Station Jacksonville and renamed VyStar in 2002, it is one of the largest credit unions in the United States, with roughly $14 billion in assets, more than 950,000 members, and approximately 80 branches across Florida and Georgia. It is state-chartered and federally insured by the NCUA. Like most US credit unions, VyStar publishes no public, first-party developer API program: there is no live developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger definition, and no documented first-party data-access API. Consumer-permissioned account data is shared with third parties through financial-data aggregators rather than a documented open API, and the United States has no single mandated open-banking contract. VyStar's open-finance posture is therefore aggregator-mediated, with the emerging CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule as the relevant regulatory horizon.

companies.name: Istra Research
companies.description: Istra Research (Istra LLC) is a quantitative proprietary trading firm that develops data-centric algorithms and low-latency technology to participate in global financial markets. The firm employs researchers and engineers who build automated trading strategies grounded in advanced mathematics, statistics, and large-scale data analysis, spanning quantitative research, algorithm development, and custom hardware/VLSI and software engineering. Istra is a proprietary trading operation rather than an API-first technology vendor: it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or developer documentation, and its technology is used internally. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.

companies.name: Poth Labs
companies.description: Poth Labs is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an AI-native customer research platform that positions itself as "the customer brain for your company." It aggregates scattered customer feedback from sources such as Fireflies, Slack, support tickets, CRM notes, surveys, in-app chat, docs, and product analytics into a unified, searchable system, then extracts patterns, runs thematic and root-cause analysis, generates hypotheses about user issues like churn or checkout abandonment, and validates them through adaptive user interviews and targeted follow-up surveys. Founded by Matthew Wong (CEO, ex-Palantir, Stanford) and Mojmir Horvath (CTO, ex-Tietoevry) and based between San Francisco and New York, the company targets product, growth, customer research, and analytics teams. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass Poth Labs publishes a marketing site but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Poultry sync
companies.description: PoultrySync is an AI-powered data management platform for the poultry value chain, helping producers increase productivity and reduce errors across broilers, breeders, hatchery, layers, slaughterhouse, feedmill, grandparents, lab, and quality management. The platform automates data collection, provides real-time dashboards, detects anomalies, forecasts production, and supports compliance reporting and audits, integrating with existing ERP systems in days. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation is published as of this profile.

companies.name: Quest Software Inc.
companies.description: Quest Software Inc. is a privately held IT management and cybersecurity software company headquartered in Aliso Viejo, California. Its portfolio spans database management and development (Toad), database and infrastructure performance monitoring (Foglight, Spotlight), unified endpoint management (KACE), Microsoft platform management and security (On Demand, Change Auditor, Recovery Manager, Migration Manager), data protection and backup (NetVault, QoreStor, Rapid Recovery), data replication (SharePlex), and data governance and modeling (erwin). Its products are distributed and supported through the Quest Support portal. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; no public, first-party developer API portal or OpenAPI surface was discoverable at enrichment time.

companies.name: ScaleArc (IgniteTech)
companies.description: ScaleArc is database load balancing software that delivers continuous availability and high performance for SQL Server and MySQL databases. It sits transparently between applications and databases to automate failover, split and balance read/write traffic, pool connections, and cache queries with no application code changes, supporting on-premise, cloud, and database-as-a-service deployments such as Amazon RDS and Azure SQL. Originally an independent product, ScaleArc is now owned and supported by IgniteTech (part of ESW Capital Group) and offered through its enterprise software library. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures. There is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or downloadable spec surface for ScaleArc today; access, licensing, and support are handled directly through IgniteTech.

companies.name: SwiftStack
companies.description: SwiftStack was a software-defined object and cloud storage company whose data platform managed unstructured data at scale across private data centers and public clouds using a distributed, shared-nothing architecture built on OpenStack Swift, targeting AI, deep learning, and large-dataset workloads. NVIDIA acquired SwiftStack in 2020; the data platform is no longer available for sale and only existing-customer support and portal resources remain. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Mayfield and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed there is no active public API, developer portal, or SDK surface for the discontinued product.

companies.name: Bluetalon
companies.description: BlueTalon was a data-centric security company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, that provided centralized data access control, dynamic data masking, and policy enforcement across big-data and hybrid data environments (Hadoop, Spark, relational databases, and cloud data stores). Its platform let enterprises define and enforce fine-grained authorization, auditing, and data- protection policies from a single control point. BlueTalon was backed by DCVC (Data Collective) among other investors, and was acquired by Microsoft in 2019, with its technology folded into Microsoft's Azure data-governance and security portfolio. The company no longer operates independently: bluetalon.com is no longer resolvable and the GitHub organization retains only archived, deprecated repositories. This profile is retained as a network record of an acquired provider; there is no live public API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Cleargraph
companies.description: Cleargraph was a Palo Alto, California startup building natural-language and graph-based search over data, operating under the tagline "Data Accessible through Search." It was backed by Version One Ventures and appears in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company is inactive - its primary domain cleargraph.com now 301-redirects off-site, its cleargraph.io website no longer resolves (connection refused), and its GitHub organization (github.com/cleargraph) was archived in April 2026 and holds only forked libraries with no first-party API, SDK, or specification. No live API, developer portal, documentation, or first-party package surface could be verified during enrichment, so no API artifacts were generated.

companies.name: ClippPR
companies.description: ClippPR (later rebranded Primeloop) was a startup that helped brands and PR agencies clip and track their press coverage, measure the value of earned media, and re-engage audiences by turning clicks on shared links into targeted relationships. Founded around 2011 in Las Vegas and part of 500 Startups' eighth (first San Francisco) accelerator batch, the company has since shut down. Its primeloop.com domain is parked/for-sale, primeloop.co no longer resolves, and clipppr.com has been taken over by an unrelated blog. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI was ever published; the only surviving first-party surface is the company's GitHub organization.

companies.name: Dashbase
companies.description: Dashbase, Inc. was a San Jose, California based developer of a next-generation log analytics and search platform, positioned as a lighter, real-time alternative to heavier log-management and observability stacks for DevOps and engineering teams. The company was a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (dashbase.io) no longer resolves / times out and its GitHub organization retains only a single archived fork, so the company appears to be defunct or to have been acquired and wound down; no live developer surface, API, SDK, OpenAPI, or documentation could be located. This profile is retained as a network record with only verifiable facts.

companies.name: Datanyze *
companies.description: Datanyze is a sales intelligence and technographic data provider owned by ZoomInfo. It offers a free browser (Chrome) extension that surfaces business contact information — work email addresses, direct-dial and mobile phone numbers, and company firmographics — for prospects on LinkedIn profiles and company websites. Datanyze pioneered "technographics," the practice of tracking the web technologies and software a company uses to power targeted B2B sales and marketing outreach. ZoomInfo acquired Datanyze in 2018 to deliver real-time technographic data to its customers. No public developer API is currently documented; this profile captures the company's discoverable web and security surface.

companies.name: Datos Io
companies.description: Datos IO was a Silicon Valley data-management startup, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, that built RecoverX — an "application-centric" backup, recovery and data-mobility platform for cloud-native and distributed databases. RecoverX targeted NoSQL and cloud data stores including Apache Cassandra, DataStax, MongoDB, Couchbase and Amazon DynamoDB, alongside relational sources such as Microsoft SQL Server, and used parallel data streaming, semantic deduplication and a distributed metadata catalog to back up in native formats and recover across private, hybrid and public cloud. Datos IO was acquired by Rubrik in 2018 and operated for a period as "Rubrik Datos IO" before the brand was retired. The company has no independent presence today: the datos.io domain has lapsed and is listed for sale through a domain broker, and no live developer portal, documentation or API surface remains. This profile is retained as an archival lineage record within the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Echo AI (fka Pathlight)
companies.description: Echo AI (formerly Pathlight) was an AI-driven customer conversation intelligence platform used by customer-experience and support teams to analyze support conversations, surface hidden insights, and coach agents. It was a portfolio company of Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no discoverable public developer surface — no API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP server — and its marketing domains are offline (pathlight.com no longer resolves and echoai.com returns a removed Framer site). The only verified live public asset is the company's GitHub organization, whose public repositories are forks of third-party libraries and Singer.io data-ingestion taps used internally rather than any first-party client library. This profile is retained as an identity record; no fabricated API artifacts were added.

companies.name: Latent Space
companies.description: Latent Space is an artificial intelligence company building generative models for businesses and creatives, described by General Catalyst as creating "AI technology for predictive analytics and data-driven insights." The company raised a Series A from Greylock and General Catalyst and is listed in the General Catalyst portfolio under the Artificial Intelligence industry in North America. As of a July 2026 probe, Latent Space publishes no developer surface: the company domain latentspace.co returns an HTTP 302 redirect to its X/Twitter profile for every path probed, no docs/api/developer/app/status subdomains resolve in DNS, there are no /.well-known/ discovery documents, no llms.txt, and no public repositories under its GitHub organization. This profile therefore records verified company identity and domain posture only — no API, SDK, or documentation artifacts exist to harvest.

companies.name: McGraw Hill Financial
companies.description: McGraw Hill Financial was a financial information and analytics company providing credit ratings, benchmarks, and analytics to global capital and commodity markets. The company was renamed S&P Global in 2016. No public developer APIs are currently documented under the McGraw Hill Financial brand.

companies.name: McKinsey & Company
companies.description: McKinsey & Company is a global management consulting firm advising leading businesses, governments, non-profit organizations, and institutions on strategy, operations, technology, and transformation. The firm operates in more than 65 countries and runs QuantumBlack, its AI and analytics arm. No public developer portal or external APIs have been identified for McKinsey & Company; its proprietary platforms (e.g., platform.mckinsey.com) are gated to client engagements and authenticated users only.

companies.name: MorphL
companies.description: MorphL was an AI and machine learning platform for e-commerce and digital publishing personalization, offering a suite of API-based, fully-automated models that predicted user behaviors (shopping stage, churn, search intent) to power click-through, conversion, and personalization KPIs across the customer journey. Founded circa 2017 and funded through the Google Digital News Initiative, the European Data Incubator, and the Techstars Montreal AI accelerator, MorphL also shipped an open-source MorphL Community Edition (big-data + Spark/Cassandra ML pipeline). MorphL was acquired by Algolia in January 2021 to power Algolia's AI-driven predictive experiences and personalization. The company's product APIs and hosted developer surface are no longer operated as a standalone service; the morphl.ai and morphl.io domains no longer resolve. The archived open-source code remains public under the Morphl-AI GitHub organization.

companies.name: OtterTune
companies.description: OtterTune was a database optimization ("on autopilot") start-up spun out of Carnegie Mellon University's database research group, operating from roughly 2020 to 2024. It applied machine learning to automatically tune the configuration knobs of PostgreSQL and MySQL databases (including managed instances such as Amazon RDS and Aurora) to improve performance and reduce cost. The company shut down in 2024 and its homepage now states the company is defunct. Its public GitHub organization remains available with infrastructure and agent tooling (ot-agent, Helm chart, CloudFormation/Terraform templates). This API Evangelist profile was added as a portfolio-company lead of Accel and captures the residual public footprint of a now-inactive company rather than a live API surface.

companies.name: Ponder
companies.description: Ponder was a data-science software company founded by UC Berkeley RISELab researchers (Doris Lee, Devin Petersohn, and Prof. Aditya Parameswaran) to commercialize the popular open-source Python libraries Modin (a drop-in pandas replacement that scales dataframe workflows with a single line of code) and Lux (automated visualization and intelligent data discovery inside notebooks). Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, 8VC, Intel Capital, and The House Fund via a $7M seed in March 2022, Ponder was acquired by Snowflake in October 2023. The ponder.io domain is now parked and no longer serves a live product, developer portal, or API; the open-source libraries remain the durable public surface.

companies.name: Tabular
companies.description: Tabular was an independent, managed cloud data platform and storage engine built on Apache Iceberg, founded in 2021 by Ryan Blue, Daniel Weeks, and Jason Reid — two of the original creators of Apache Iceberg and a former head of Data Engineering at Netflix. Its central product was a managed Iceberg catalog exposed over the open Apache Iceberg REST Catalog protocol (an OpenAPI-defined common API), giving any compute engine vendor-neutral access to a single copy of data. Databricks agreed to acquire Tabular in June 2024 and closed the deal that month; the founders joined Databricks and the standalone product was wound down. As of this enrichment pass the tabular.io domain no longer resolves and the tabular-io GitHub organization has no public repositories, so there is no live first-party API surface to harvest. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: ThinkUp
companies.description: ThinkUp was a social media analytics application, co-founded by Gina Trapani and Anil Dash, that gave individuals insights into their own activity across Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, and other social networks. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, it ran as both a hosted subscription service and an open-source project (ThinkUpLLC/ThinkUp on GitHub, 3.2k+ stars) before its hosted service was shut down in 2016. The thinkup.com domain is no longer operated by the company (it now resolves to an unrelated coupon-code site), and no public developer API surface is available for enrichment.

companies.name: Timetric
companies.description: Timetric was a London-based data platform founded in 2008 for publishing, analysing, and performing calculations on large quantities of time-varying statistical data, later providing online market data, analysis, and advisory services to the insurance, construction, and infrastructure sectors. The Timetric Platform exposed an API with OAuth and API-token authentication for creating and updating time series. Timetric was acquired by GlobalData in March 2018 and timetric.com now redirects to globaldata.com; the company no longer operates independently.

companies.name: Twirl
companies.description: Twirl is a data platform and orchestrator that lets teams build data products faster by combining BigQuery, dbt, Python, and Google Cloud services (GCS, Dataflow) in a single git-backed project. Backed by Creandum. As of July 2026 the twirldata.com website and docs.twirldata.com both return 404 (GitHub Pages) and no public API surface is available; the remaining public artifacts are the twirldata GitHub org (twirl-examples) and a placeholder PyPI package (twirldata 0.0.0, "Client SDK for the Twirl data platform").

companies.name: Tydo
companies.description: Tydo delivers autonomous audits for Shopify stores inside Claude. A single integration runs hundreds of audits - retention, shipping, email and SMS, and more - scoring a store against similar brands in its network, re-running on a cadence in the background, and routing every finding to a next step: fix it yourself, turn on an agent, or get matched to a vetted partner via dtcmvp. A Greylock portfolio company, currently waitlist-only with no public developer portal, API documentation, or published MCP endpoint.

companies.name: uberVU
companies.description: uberVU was a social media analytics and monitoring company, backed by Seedcamp, that offered brand-insight dashboards and a metrics API before being acquired by Hootsuite in 2014. The company no longer operates independently - ubervu.com now 301-redirects to blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-analytics/, its former metrics API is retired, and its GitHub organization is dormant. This profile is kept as a historical record of a VC-portfolio company with no current public API surface.

companies.name: Urban Engines
companies.description: Urban Engines was a Silicon Valley urban-mobility analytics startup founded by Shiva Shivakumar and Balaji Prabhakar that built a Space/Time Engine for analyzing how people and objects move through cities, powering commuter routing and congestion insights for cities including Washington D.C., Sao Paulo, and Singapore. Backed by a16z and GV, the company was acquired by Google in September 2016 and is now defunct; it published no public API, developer portal, or client packages, and its former website is parked on Google infrastructure.

companies.name: Ursa Computing
companies.description: Ursa Computing was a startup founded in 2020 by Wes McKinney (creator of pandas, co-creator of Apache Arrow) to accelerate Apache Arrow and open source data science tooling, backed by GV. In late 2021 Ursa Computing and Ursa Labs joined forces with other teams to form Voltron Data, and the company no longer operates independently: ursacomputing.com no longer resolves, and its remaining public footprint is the ursacomputing GitHub organization, whose crossbow repository still runs extra CI for Apache Arrow. No public API surface was ever published under the Ursa Computing name.

companies.name: Voltron Data
companies.description: Voltron Data is a Mountain View-based data infrastructure company (founded 2021) behind Theseus, a GPU-accelerated, composable distributed SQL query engine for petabyte-scale analytics and AI pipelines, distributed embedded through partners rather than as a self-serve public API. The company is a major steward of the open-source composable data stack — Apache Arrow, Ibis, Substrait, Arrow Flight SQL, and ADBC — acquired Claypot AI in January 2024, and is backed by Battery Ventures, GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Walden Catalyst, with an Accenture investment in 2025. As of 2026-07-21 the company website (voltrondata.com) is unreachable — the domain is registered but its DNS zone is lame-delegated — leaving the GitHub organization as the live public surface; no public API, SDK packages, or developer portal are published.

companies.name: GazeHawk
companies.description: GazeHawk was a webcam-based eye-tracking startup founded in December 2009 by Brian Krausz and Joe Gershenson, offering affordable eye-tracking usability and ad-testing services that ran on ordinary consumer webcams instead of expensive dedicated hardware. Backed by Y Combinator (S10) and 500 Startups, the company was acqui-hired by Facebook in March 2012 — Facebook hired the engineering team but explicitly did not acquire the product or technology, and the founders moved on to unrelated backend and product engineering. GazeHawk operated no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; the domain today serves only a legacy static marketing and blog site for the defunct product.

companies.name: Noteable
companies.description: Noteable was a collaborative, cloud-based data notebook platform that combined code (SQL, Python, and R), natural language, and interactive no-code visualizations so data teams could explore, visualize, and act on data together in a single browser-based workspace. It offered real-time collaboration and commenting down to individual data points, scheduled/automated notebook runs, and connectors to databases and warehouses including Trino, Snowflake, CockroachDB, PostgreSQL, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, and Databricks. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Wing Venture Capital. Noteable was acquired by Confluent on December 1, 2023, and the platform, operations, and services were terminated effective immediately, with users given until January 5, 2024 to export their data. As of this enrichment pass the noteable.io domain no longer serves the product and redirects to an Afternic domain-for-sale parking page; app.noteable.io, docs.noteable.io, and api.noteable.io are offline. There is no live public API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Rumarocket
companies.description: Rumarocket is an AI-powered talent management and HR analytics platform whose tagline is "Hire Talent, Not Employees." It integrates with existing HR systems to synthesize workforce data from hiring through employment, applying machine learning to predict employee attrition and performance, evaluate talent fit for specific roles, and deliver predictive insights for retention and workforce wellness. Backed by 500 Global, the platform exposes user-facing recruitment-algorithm and predictive-insights dashboards but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Signify Group
companies.description: Signify Group is a London, United Kingdom-based ethical data science firm founded in 2017 by co-founder and CEO Jonathan Hirshler, applying machine learning, natural language understanding, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) to social and digital media data. Its flagship service, Threat Matrix, is widely regarded as the leading platform for detecting, analysing, evidencing, and actioning online abuse and fixated threats directed at athletes, clubs, leagues, player unions, federations, brands, and other public figures. Threat Matrix scans incoming public messages across X (Twitter), Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok in 39+ languages, uses "augmented intelligence" (AI speed combined with trained human analyst nuance) to triage racist, sexist, homophobic, anti-semitic, islamophobic, gambling-driven, and personally targeted abuse, and produces evidence-grade reports with network mapping that can be used by platforms, police, sponsors, and protection teams. Customers and partners include the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA), Kick It Out, the International Tennis Federation (ITF) and WTA Tour covering c.8,300 players, the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS) protecting 1,000+ athletes and officials, the Badminton World Federation (BWF), the NCAA, and Japan's 2026 World Baseball Classic squad. Signify also operates ShareScore (media coverage and social buzz analytics), Sports Insights (fan engagement and athlete insight analytics), and Online Forensics (brand reputation, OSINT investigations, and risk assurance). Signify is a private services firm with no public developer API, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub organization; engagement is via direct sales and managed service contracts with rights-holders, leagues, federations, and enterprise clients.

companies.name: 6thSense
companies.description: 6thSense is a physical-AI hardware company building the touch layer for dexterous robots. It designs and manufactures wearable tactile-sensing data gloves that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and 3D hand pose — alongside custom tactile skin molded to robot hands. Its capture stack synchronizes eight aligned modalities (tactile and pressure proxies, egocentric video, depth/RGB-D, hand pose, motion and IMU dynamics, wrist and scene cameras, dense labels and commentary, and success/failure outcomes) into model-ready demonstration datasets used to train the next generation of dexterous, manipulation-capable robots. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (S26).

companies.name: acorn systems
companies.description: Acorn is a Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing (TD-ABC) and profitability-management platform for multi-dimensional cost-to-serve analysis, precisely attributing direct and indirect costs against products, customers, regions, business units and facilities. It offers what-if scenario modeling, shared-services optimization, custom business-process modeling, and OLAP/analytics for pricing, supplier negotiation and supply-chain decisions. Originally Acorn Systems, the product is now owned and operated by IgniteTech (an ESW Capital enterprise-software company); the acornsys.com domain 301-redirects into IgniteTech's software library. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification is published for the product.

companies.name: Actuate
companies.description: Actuate Corporation was an enterprise business intelligence and reporting software company founded in 1993 and backed by Accel (partner Arthur Patterson). It was the original developer of BIRT (Business Intelligence and Reporting Tools), building a developer community measured in millions of downloads, and traded on NASDAQ under the ticker BIRT. OpenText acquired Actuate in January 2015 and folded its analytics and reporting technology into OpenText Analytics Cloud. The standalone actuate.com site is no longer an active product presence (all paths return HTTP 404) and the company publishes no independent, live API or developer portal today. A separately named company at actuate.ai (AI video/threat detection) is unrelated to this Accel-portfolio entity and likewise exposes no public API.

companies.name: Adku
companies.description: Adku was a big-data e-commerce personalization startup founded around 2010 by former Googlers (CEO Ajit Varma with co-founders Carlos Whitt and Jesse Shieh), and an AngelPad alumnus. It built machine-learning technology to personalize the online shopping experience for visitors to e-commerce sites such as eBay, Amazon, and Zappos. Backed by Battery Ventures, Greylock Partners, and True Ventures (roughly $1.49M raised), Adku was acquired by Groupon in February 2012 and is no longer an operating, independent company. It has no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface; this record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead for historical/enrichment tracking only.

companies.name: Ahana
companies.description: Ahana was a venture-backed SaaS company founded in 2020 and headquartered in San Mateo, California, that provided a managed, cloud-native offering of PrestoDB — the open source distributed SQL query engine originally created at Facebook — positioned as the query and analytics layer of the open data lakehouse. Ahana raised roughly $32M in seed and Series A funding from investors including GV (Google Ventures), Lux Capital, Third Point Ventures, Leslie Ventures, and Liberty Global Ventures, and was a leading contributor and steward of the Presto Foundation. In April 2023 Ahana was acquired by IBM, which joined the Presto Foundation and folded Ahana's SaaS Presto capabilities into IBM watsonx.data. The independent Ahana product and developer surface no longer exist: the ahana.io domain now 301-redirects to https://www.ibm.com/products/watsonx-data. This profile is retained as a historical network record for the acquired company; there is no live first-party API to enrich.

companies.name: Aiden.ai
companies.description: Aiden.ai was a London-based marketing-analytics startup, founded in 2016 by Marie Outtier and Pierre-Jean Camillieri, that built what it billed as the first AI-powered marketing analyst: a machine-reading assistant that ingested large volumes of paid-advertising data to surface actionable insights, detect anomalies, predict campaign performance, and proactively act to improve ROI. It raised a $1.6M seed round led by Partech in 2018 and was acquired by Twitter (now X) on 2019-11-21. The company no longer operates as an independent business, ships no public product or developer API, and the aiden.ai domain is now parked and listed for sale (Afternic). This profile is retained as a Partech portfolio lead but is defunct: there is no live developer surface to enrich.

companies.name: Ailumia
companies.description: Ailumia is an AI-driven retail operations platform that helps brands and sellers grow on the world's most valuable marketplaces, with a focus on Amazon. The platform applies artificial intelligence across the retail workflow to manage marketplace sales, inventory, supply chain, and finances, giving operators data-driven guidance and automation to navigate the challenges of modern e-commerce. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Taipei, Taiwan, Ailumia is backed by 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio; enrichment probing found a Cloudflare-fronted WordPress marketing presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

companies.name: Airware
companies.description: Airware was an enterprise commercial-drone (UAV) software and aerial-data-analytics company founded in 2011 by Jonathan Downey and headquartered in San Francisco. It began by building an operating system and autopilot for commercial drones, then pivoted to a cloud-based "Aerial Information Platform" that captured, processed, and analyzed drone imagery for enterprise verticals such as mining, quarrying, insurance, and construction. Airware acquired French drone-analytics firm Redbird in 2016 and raised roughly $118M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Kleiner Perkins, GV (Google Ventures), Intel Capital, and Next World Capital. The company ceased operations in September 2018. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no live developer surface, API, or public specification is currently discoverable (the airware.com domain no longer resolves), so this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record.

companies.name: Altruist (iConnectiva)
companies.description: iConnectiva (Connectiva Analytics and Insights Ltd), part of Altruist Technologies Pvt. Ltd., is a telecom analytics product and services company focused on subscriber-data monetization. Its RAFMS platform delivers Revenue Assurance and Fraud Management to telecom, media and utility operators, alongside Big Data analytics to lower churn, boost ARPU and reduce revenue leakage. iConnectiva reports managing 350+ million subscribers for Revenue Assurance and Fraud Management, handling 500+ million customers, processing 15+ billion CDR/day, a repository of 400+ KPIs across RA and FMS, and 1000+ adaptors, delivered through advisory, tool-based and managed services. No public API, developer portal, or SDK surface is published.

companies.name: Amiato
companies.description: Amiato was a Palo Alto, California big-data startup founded in 2011 by Nathan Binkert and Mehul A. Shah, originally incubated at Y Combinator in 2012 under the name Nou Data. Amiato built a real-time analytics pipeline around its Schema-lift technology, which extracted records from NoSQL data stores such as MongoDB and Couchbase, automatically inferred and transformed them into a relational schema, and loaded them continuously into Amazon Redshift so that unstructured operational data could be queried by conventional business-intelligence tools. The company raised roughly $2M from investors including Y Combinator, Andreessen Horowitz, Ignition Partners, Data Collective (DCVC) and angel Bobby Yazdani. Amazon Web Services quietly acquired Amiato in May 2014 (reported publicly in April 2015) in what was widely characterized as a talent acquisition; most of the team joined Amazon's database and Redshift product groups and Amiato ceased independent operations. The company is defunct: the amiato.com domain no longer resolves and there is no surviving public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface to enrich.

companies.name: Applimation
companies.description: Applimation was a provider of application Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) and enterprise data archiving software for packaged applications including SAP (ERP, HR, CRM, SRM, SCM, APO) and Oracle environments, helping customers manage the full data lifecycle from test-data management through archiving of inactive data to lower storage and database costs and improve application performance. Informatica acquired Applimation for approximately $40 million in an agreement announced in February 2009, folding its ILM and database-archiving technology into Informatica's data management portfolio. Applimation no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer surface, API, or documentation.

companies.name: Apropose
companies.description: Apropose, Inc. was a Mountain View, California startup spun out of the Stanford University Computer Science Department in 2013 to bring data-driven software to web design. Founded by Ranjitha Kumar, Jerry Talton, Maxine Lim, and Arvind Satyanarayan, the company built tools for large-scale visual page search and web design analytics — letting teams track design trends, compare a site's design against demographics, and surface prevalent design patterns to inject concrete data into the design process. It raised a roughly $1.875M seed round in 2014 led by New Enterprise Associates (NEA) and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), with angels including Pat Hanrahan and Nick McKeown. The company has since ceased operations and is permanently closed; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation, and its primary domain (apropose.com) is now parked and listed for sale. This profile is retained as an a16z portfolio-lead record.

companies.name: Apsalar
companies.description: Apsalar was a mobile marketing analytics and attribution company (founded 2010, headquartered in San Francisco, backed by Battery Ventures and 500 Startups/500 Global) that provided a mobile measurement platform (MMP) for app install attribution, campaign analytics, and marketing data unification. In 2017 Apsalar merged into Singular (singular.net); the Apsalar brand and its developer/API surface were retired as part of that acquisition. The apsalar.com apex domain no longer resolves to a live site and www.apsalar.com now redirects to Singular, so there is no active first-party API, OpenAPI, or developer portal to enrich. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead pointing to its successor, Singular.

companies.name: ArbiLex
companies.description: ArbiLex is a legal-fintech startup founded at the Harvard Innovation Labs in 2018 by Isabel Yang that brings AI and predictive analytics to high-stakes international arbitration and litigation finance. Its Bayesian machine learning and NLP models — trained on a dataset of over nine million cases — produce empirical, explainable case ratings that help counsel quantify uncertainty, reduce errors, and value claims. ArbiLex also operates the ArbiLex Funding Exchange (AFX), a data-driven marketplace pairing AI-rated cases with litigation-finance capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; no public developer API surface was found at time of enrichment.

companies.name: Arbor Software
companies.description: Arbor Software Corporation was an enterprise business-intelligence and OLAP software company founded in 1991 in Sunnyvale, California by Bob Earle and Jim Dorian. It created Essbase, the pioneering multidimensional online-analytical-processing (OLAP) server first released in 1992, and went public on NASDAQ under the ticker ARSW in 1995. Arbor merged with Hyperion Software in 1998 to form Hyperion Solutions Corporation, which Oracle Corporation acquired in 2007; the Essbase technology lives on inside Oracle. Arbor Software no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface, so there is nothing to enrich.

companies.name: Arimo
companies.description: Arimo (formerly Adatao) was a Palo Alto, California AI and big-data startup building a distributed deep-learning and "Behavioral AI" analytics platform on top of Apache Spark, backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Bloomberg Beta. The company was acquired by Panasonic in 2017 and folded into Panasonic's AI/innovation efforts, and it no longer operates as an independent provider. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead for the API Evangelist network, this profile has no surviving developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich - the arimo.com and arimo.ai domains no longer resolve.

companies.name: Ark.com
companies.description: Ark.com was a people search engine founded in San Francisco in March 2012 by Patrick Riley and Yiming Liu, and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2012 batch. Ark indexed over a billion public social network profiles — aggregating "ghost profiles" from Facebook, LinkedIn, AngelList and other networks — and let users search across them with filters such as hometown, current city, high school, college, employer and interests, to reconnect with classmates and acquaintances or find new business contacts. The company raised a $4.2M seed round in April 2012 from Andreessen Horowitz, Greylock Partners and SV Angel, and reached the finals of TechCrunch Disrupt NYC 2012. Ark is no longer operating: Y Combinator lists the company as Inactive and PitchBook lists it as Out of Business. As of a July 2026 probe the ark.com domain no longer serves the company — it redirects to www.ark-invest.com, the unrelated ARK Investment Management site — and no api., developer. or docs. subdomain resolves. Ark never published a public API, developer portal or SDKs, so there is no API surface to catalog. Retained as a historical a16z portfolio record only.

companies.name: Backtype
companies.description: BackType was a San Francisco social-media analytics startup (backed by 500 Startups/500 Global) whose BackTweets product helped publishers measure the reach and conversion of their Tweets and content for clients including The New York Times, HubSpot, bitly, and SlideShare. The BackType team also built Storm, the distributed real-time stream-processing system later open-sourced as Apache Storm. Twitter acquired BackType on July 5, 2011 and folded the team into its platform group; the standalone product and public API were discontinued after the acquisition. The company is defunct and backtype.com is now a parked domain, so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Baker Technologies
companies.description: Baker Technologies (Baker) was a Denver, Colorado based customer relationship management (CRM) and marketing platform built for the cannabis industry, founded in 2014 by David Champion, Joel Milton, and Roger Obando. A graduate of the 500 Startups accelerator, Baker helped licensed dispensaries grow revenue and build customer relationships through online ordering, loyalty programs, SMS/text messaging, and analytics, and launched an expanded integrations program with a developer API connecting dispensaries to 20+ ancillary cannabis services. The company raised approximately $11.75M (including an $8M Series A) before being acquired by TILT Holdings in 2018. The trybaker.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, indicating the product has been discontinued; no live developer portal, API documentation, or specifications are publicly available.

companies.name: Beckon
companies.description: Beckon was a marketing analytics and marketing performance measurement SaaS platform, founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Mateo, California. Its product automated the ingestion, harmonization, and normalization of marketing data from across paid, owned, and earned channels into a single unified set of metrics and dashboards, giving marketing teams a "total marketing intelligence" view of spend, performance, and ROI. Beckon was venture-backed by Canaan Partners and Storm Ventures, and was subsequently acquired into the IgniteTech (ESW Capital / Trilogy) portfolio. The independent beckon.com domain now redirects to its acquirer, IgniteTech, and the company no longer operates a public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal of its own.

companies.name: Bit.io
companies.description: Bit.io was a serverless, shareable PostgreSQL database platform that let developers spin up cloud Postgres databases in seconds, load and query data, and share them via a link, with programmatic access over the standard Postgres wire protocol. Founded by Adam Fletcher and Jonathan Mortensen and backed by Battery Ventures, bit.io was acquired by Databricks in May 2023; the standalone product was sunset on June 29, 2023 (database exports available through July 29, 2023) and the team moved to Databricks. This profile is retained as a defunct/acquired network record — there is no live API, developer portal, documentation, or discovery surface to enrich.

companies.name: BitYota
companies.description: BitYota was a Data-Warehouse-as-a-Service (DWaaS) startup founded around 2011 in Santa Clara, California, offering a SaaS analytics data warehouse that ran on top of Amazon Web Services and Rackspace infrastructure and natively queried semi-structured JSON data. The company's team of data-processing engineers was acqui-hired by LifeLock in August 2015 for approximately $12.8 million, and the standalone BitYota product and company were subsequently wound down. The primary domain bityota.com no longer resolves (no DNS records), no public API, developer portal, documentation, source repositories, or client SDKs survive, and there is no active API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest. This profile is retained for historical/network completeness and is flagged defunct.

companies.name: Blue Flame Data
companies.description: Blue Flame Data was an early-2000s consumer-preference analytics company (founded around 2000 in New York City) that built web-based software for real-time measurement of consumer market preferences, marketed as TrueChoice Preference Technology for quantifying the preference structures of individual consumers and employees. The company appears to be defunct: its domain (blueflamedata.com) resolves to a parked/unresponsive IP and does not serve a live site. It was surfaced to the API Evangelist network via Battery Ventures portfolio mining. During enrichment no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, packages, MCP server, or other machine-readable artifacts could be located, so no API artifacts were produced.

companies.name: Bluedata Software Inc
companies.description: BlueData Software Inc was a big-data infrastructure company whose EPIC platform ran Hadoop, Spark, and other analytics workloads in Docker containers on-premises and in the cloud. It was a dcvc (Data Collective) portfolio company and was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) in 2018; its technology now lives on as the HPE Ezmeral Container Platform. The original www.bluedata.com domain 301-redirects to HPE's container-platform page, and the company no longer operates an independent developer, API, or documentation surface, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest without fabrication. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead.

companies.name: Bluefin Labs
companies.description: Bluefin Labs was a social TV analytics company founded in 2008 in Cambridge, Massachusetts by Deb Roy and Michael Fleischman, spun out of research at the MIT Media Lab. Its platform semantically interpreted public social media commentary from Twitter, Facebook and blogs and automatically linked those comments to the television shows and advertisements people were watching, producing audience engagement measurement for networks, agencies and brands. Its product, Bluefin Signals, gave media buyers a tool for accessing and analyzing social TV response data. The company raised a Series A led by Redpoint Ventures in 2010 and a $12M Series B led by Time Warner Investments in January 2012, with SoftBank Capital and Lerer Ventures participating. Twitter acquired Bluefin Labs on February 6, 2013 for a reported ~$100 million and absorbed the team and technology into its TV advertising and analytics products. The company is DEFUNCT: it operates no independent product, developer program or API, and the bluefinlabs.com domain no longer belongs to the company — it now redirects to an unrelated news site. This profile is retained as a historical / portfolio-graph record only.

companies.name: BlueTalon Data Systems
companies.description: BlueTalon Data Systems was a data-centric security company that built dynamic, policy-based access control, data masking, filtering, and auditing for enterprise data platforms such as Hadoop, relational databases, and big-data stores. It let organizations enforce fine-grained authorization and privacy controls at the point of data access. Founded around 2013 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, BlueTalon was acquired by Microsoft in July 2019, after which its team and technology were absorbed into Microsoft's data-governance and security efforts (Azure). BlueTalon no longer operates as an independent company; the bluetalon.com domain is parked on Azure DNS with no active web, developer, or API surface, so this network profile carries identity only and has no live artifacts to enrich.

companies.name: Braid Social
companies.description: Braid (Braid Social) was a creator-economy startup building a direct-to-fan engagement platform for the creator economy. Founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro, Braid let creators build customizable landing pages that consolidated their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts, and commerce links), collect fan phone numbers, and reach followers directly through SMS text messages, push notifications, and mailing lists, with link tracking and cross-platform analytics. Positioned as a creator-friendly, direct-to-audience alternative to algorithm-driven social platforms, Braid raised a $6.8M seed round in August 2023 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Initialized Capital. The company appears to be defunct as of this profile — its primary domain (braid.ai) now redirects to a domain-for-sale listing and no developer, documentation, or API surface could be found. Added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead; no public API artifacts exist to enrich.

companies.name: BrightBytes
companies.description: BrightBytes was a San Francisco-based K-12 education data and analytics company founded in 2012 by Rob Mancabelli, best known for Clarity, a decision-support and analytics platform used by schools and districts to connect technology spending and classroom use to student learning outcomes, and for DataSense, a data-integration platform that captured, cleaned, and synced student data between disparate school systems. The company sold DataSense and its team to Microsoft in February 2019 and was itself acquired by Google in 2022. BrightBytes no longer operates independently: as of July 2026 www.brightbytes.net returns an expired-site placeholder and no developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, or status surface remains. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface to catalog.

companies.name: BrightFunnel
companies.description: BrightFunnel was a San Francisco-based B2B marketing analytics company founded in 2012 that built a revenue attribution and forecasting platform. Its Revenue Intelligence Suite gave B2B marketers multi-touch attribution, revenue-funnel analysis, account-based measurement, web analytics, and predictive forecasting so they could quantify marketing's impact on pipeline and revenue and align plans with business priorities. BrightFunnel was acquired by account-based marketing vendor Terminus in January 2018, and its multi-channel analytics were folded into the Terminus platform. It no longer operates as a standalone product: the brightfunnel.com domain now serves only a redirect, and there is no live developer portal, public API, documentation, SDK, or discovery surface (.well-known, llms.txt) to enrich. This profile remains a historical company stub, originally surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.

companies.name: Canopy Labs
companies.description: Canopy Labs was a customer analytics and predictive marketing SaaS company founded in 2012 in the Toronto, Ontario area (Thornhill) by Wojciech Gryc and Jorge Escobedo, with an additional office in San Francisco. A Y Combinator alumnus, it built machine-learning software that helped businesses model and predict customer behavior, optimize purchase funnels, and personalize marketing across the customer journey. The company raised seed funding from investors including BDC Venture Capital's IT Fund and Valar Ventures. In 2018 Canopy Labs was acquired by Drop Technologies (the customer-loyalty app Drop), after which the independent product, website (canopylabs.com), and any developer/API surface were wound down. This profile is retained as a historical company record; the entity no longer operates independently and publishes no live API.

companies.name: Cargon Tech B.V.
companies.description: Cargon Tech B.V. is a supply-chain and logistics technology company backed by 500 Global. Its public presence at cargon.com positions Cargon as a fast, innovative supply-chain platform with powerful analytical tools for shippers and carriers, while the related Cargon TMS product (cargon.tech) offers a cloud transport-management system for small carriers and freight forwarders covering dispatch, fleet management, invoicing and Timocom integration. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment (the cargon.com site is a client-rendered single-page app that returns its index shell for unknown paths), so this profile currently carries identity and domain-security signal only.

companies.name: Cascade
companies.description: Cascade (www.cascade.io) was a no-code data analysis platform founded in 2019 by Jake Fuentes and Jon Brelig that let non-technical business teams import large datasets, transform and combine them with no-code tools, then visualize and present findings as interactive data apps (positioned as a cloud-native, collaborative alternative to Alteryx). The company wound down in 2023 after failing to reach breakout growth; www.cascade.io now serves a retrospective "What Cascade Did" page. As of the 2026-07-18 enrichment probe there is no public API, developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or documentation surface to enrich, so this profile carries identity only.

companies.name: Cashforce
companies.description: Cashforce is a fintech platform focused on cash flow forecasting and working-capital analytics for corporate treasury and finance teams, connecting ERP systems, bank accounts, and financial data to give companies real-time visibility into cash positions, liquidity, and forecasting scenarios. Originally a Techstars-backed portfolio company, Cashforce was acquired by Billtrust and its standalone product surface is no longer independently operated; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public footprint. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API definitions are currently reachable at the cashforce.com origin (the site returns HTTP 522), so this record carries identity and domain-security signals only.

companies.name: Caspida
