companies.description: Caspida was a cybersecurity company specializing in user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA), applying unsupervised machine learning to network, endpoint, and identity data to detect insider threats and advanced attacks without predefined rules. Splunk acquired Caspida in July 2015 and folded its technology into Splunk User Behavior Analytics (Splunk UBA). Caspida no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no standalone developer program, API, or documentation surface; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record.

companies.name: Cazena
companies.description: Cazena was a Waltham, Massachusetts-based enterprise software company, founded in 2014, that delivered a fully-managed SaaS data platform — a "Big Data as a Service" cloud data lake that let enterprises run analytics, machine learning, and data-lake workloads on managed cloud infrastructure without operating the underlying stack themselves. The company was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), North Bridge Venture Partners, and Formation 8. Cloudera agreed to acquire Cazena (alongside Datacoral) in June 2021, folding Cazena's managed SaaS data-lake technology into the Cloudera platform. Cazena no longer operates as an independent provider; its domain cazena.com now redirects to cloudera.com, and it exposes no independent public API, developer portal, or documentation.

companies.name: Celequest
companies.description: Celequest was a business intelligence software company that built an appliance-based platform for real-time operational BI — streaming dashboards and continuous analytics over live transactional data rather than batch data-warehouse reporting. The company was acquired by Cognos in 2007, and its technology was folded into the Cognos Now! operational BI appliance; Cognos itself was acquired by IBM in 2008. Celequest no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer surface. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment probe, celequest.com and www.celequest.com resolve to IBM redirect infrastructure (redirect.www.ibm.com) and issue a blanket HTTP 301 to the IBM Cognos Now! product page for every path, including /.well-known/* and /llms.txt. There is no portal, no documentation, no API, and no artifacts to harvest. This record is retained as a historical/acquired-company entry in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Clearstory Data
companies.description: Clearstory Data was a big-data analytics startup (Menlo Park / Mountain View, CA) that built a cloud service for blending and visualizing enterprise and third-party data, backed by a16z, GV (Google Ventures), Kleiner Perkins and Khosla Ventures. It was acquired by Alteryx in 2016 and is no longer an independent company. Its former domain (clearstorydata.com) has lapsed and now 301-redirects to unrelated parked/spam sites, so it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/defunct portfolio record; no live artifacts are producible.

companies.name: CloudPhysics
companies.description: CloudPhysics is a SaaS-based big-data analytics platform for virtualized IT infrastructure, founded in 2011 and acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise in 2021. Deployed as the CloudPhysics Observer virtual appliance against VMware vSphere / vCenter, it collects IT metadata and delivers data-driven insights for capacity planning, cost optimization, migration assessment, and infrastructure health. It is now part of HPE; cloudphysics.com redirects to HPE storage. CloudPhysics exposes no public developer API of its own — the product consumes the VMware vCenter API to gather metadata rather than publishing a developer-facing API, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

companies.name: Convertro, Inc.
companies.description: Convertro, Inc. was a marketing analytics company based in Santa Monica, California, providing a multi-touch attribution platform that measured the ROI of marketing touchpoints across online and offline media using algorithmic attribution models. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Convertro was acquired by AOL in 2014 and folded into the AOL/Verizon (now Yahoo) advertising stack. It no longer operates an independent public developer surface: convertro.com redirects to yahooinc.com, and no developer portal, documentation, API, or reachable API host was found during enrichment. This profile is retained as a network record; there is no live provider API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Coremetrics
companies.description: Coremetrics was a web analytics software company founded in 1999 and headquartered in San Mateo, California. It delivered a cloud-based (SaaS) digital marketing analytics platform used by more than 2,100 online brands to capture and analyze visitor and shopper behavior across web, social, and mobile channels for marketing optimization, attribution, and personalization. Backed by Accel and other venture investors, Coremetrics was acquired by IBM in 2010 and folded into IBM Digital Analytics and the IBM Watson Marketing / Enterprise Marketing Management suite. The standalone coremetrics.com developer surface is no longer operational, and no live public API, documentation, or SDK could be found during enrichment.

companies.name: Cross Access
companies.description: Cross Access was a data-integration software company backed by Battery Ventures that was acquired by IBM on 2003-10-17 and folded into IBM's information-integration portfolio. It is defunct and has no independent web presence, developer portal, API, or documentation surface today; DNS for candidate domains (crossaccess.com, cross-access.com, crossaccess.io) does not resolve. This profile is retained as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio record, not an active API provider, and there are no live artifacts to enrich.

companies.name: CrowdAnalytix
companies.description: CrowdAnalytix (CAX) is a crowdsourced data science and predictive analytics platform that connects enterprises with a global community of data scientists to build, test, and compare machine learning models through hosted modeling competitions. The company runs prediction and classification contests across industries such as consumer packaged goods, retail, banking, insurance, and healthcare, and has extended into AI/ML model development, data annotation and labeling, and packaged AI solutions. Headquartered in Frisco, Texas with operations in Bangalore, India, CrowdAnalytix is backed by Accel.

companies.name: Cullinet Software
companies.description: Cullinet Software (formerly Cullinane Database Systems) was a database and application software company based in Westwood, Massachusetts, best known for the IDMS/IDMS-DB mainframe database management system, the IDD data dictionary, and the ADS/Online application development environment for IBM mainframes. Backed by Battery Ventures, Greylock, and Morgenthaler Ventures, it was one of the first software companies to go public (1978) and was acquired by Computer Associates (CA) on June 30, 1989. The company is defunct and publishes no developer portal, API, or documentation surface today; this record is retained as a historical portfolio-graph node with no enrichable API artifacts.

companies.name: Customer Database
companies.description: Customer Database is the topic dedicated to APIs, schemas, vocabularies, and reference designs for the systems of record that store customer identity, profile, contact, preference, consent, and account data. A customer database underpins CRM, marketing automation, customer data platforms (CDPs), customer service, billing, and analytics use cases, and is increasingly expected to support API-first access, schema-on-write data quality, real-time eventing, GDPR/CCPA consent and erasure workflows, and identity resolution across web, mobile, and offline channels. This repository tracks the vendors, standards, and patterns that make customer data accessible, governed, and portable.

companies.name: cVidya Networks
companies.description: cVidya Networks was a provider of big-data analytics software for communications and digital service providers, best known for its MoneyMap product suite covering revenue assurance, fraud management, marketing analytics, and data monetization for telecom operators. Founded in 2000 by Alon Aginsky as an Israeli/US company, cVidya grew to roughly 300 employees and about $65M in revenue with deployments across Europe, LATAM, APAC, North America, and Africa. In January 2016 the company was acquired by Amdocs (reported at ~$30M) and absorbed into the Amdocs Revenue Guard and Business Assurance offering; cVidya no longer operates as an independent company and its cvidya.com domain no longer resolves. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record; there is no live developer portal or public API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Dapper
companies.description: Dapper was an advertising-technology and web-data company founded in 2006 by Jonathan Aizen and Eran Shir, seed-funded by Accel. It ran two surfaces: Dapper Ads, an intent-driven dynamic-ad product that pulled live product and inventory data from an advertiser's own site into targeted creative without IT integration; and open.dapper.net (the "Dapp Factory" / Dapper: The Data Mapper), a hosted tool that turned any web page into structured feeds, web services and widgets — XML, RSS, JSON, YAML, CSV, iCalendar, Google Gadgets, Netvibes modules and image loops — effectively letting anyone "create an API for any site" before providers published their own. Dapper was acquired by Yahoo! in 2010 and both surfaces were shut down; dapper.net now resolves to Yahoo nameservers with no host, and open.dapper.net no longer resolves. There is no live API, developer portal, or documentation to enrich.

companies.name: DappRadar
companies.description: DappRadar is a blockchain application discovery and analytics platform, widely described as "the world's dapp store." It tracks decentralized applications (dapps), NFT collections, tokens, and DeFi activity across many blockchains, providing rankings, portfolio tracking, and on-chain market intelligence to consumers, builders, and investors. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Vilnius, Lithuania, DappRadar is a Prosus Ventures portfolio company. This profile was seeded from that portfolio and is being enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

companies.name: Dasera
companies.description: Dasera is a data security company in the data security posture management (DSPM) and data governance space, founded by Ani Chaudhuri and backed by Sierra Ventures. Its platform was built to continuously discover, classify, and monitor sensitive data across cloud and on-premises data stores (databases, warehouses, data lakes) and to surface data security, privacy, and compliance risk across the data lifecycle. As of this enrichment pass the standalone dasera.com origin is unreachable (a Cloudflare 1001 origin error with a failed TLS handshake), so no live developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface could be harvested; this profile records the domain-security posture that could still be probed via DNS/TLS and remains a stub awaiting a live API surface.

companies.name: Data Elite Services
companies.description: Data Elite Services, Inc. was a San Francisco company associated with Data Elite, a venture lab and early-stage accelerator for big-data startups and data scientists founded in 2013 at 135 Main Street, San Francisco, California. The entity was registered in California on 2013-08-27 as a foreign stock corporation and its filing status is recorded as forfeited by the Franchise Tax Board, indicating the business is no longer active. Enrichment probes in July 2026 found no live company website, no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface of any kind. The dataelite.com domain resolves but redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale parking lander rather than a company site, and no other candidate domain resolved. This record is retained as an inactive historical entry in the API Evangelist network with no API artifacts to enrich; it should not be treated as an active API provider.

companies.name: Datacurve
companies.description: Datacurve is a San Francisco-based AI infrastructure company that positions itself as "the data engine for frontier AI," building high-quality, expert-annotated datasets, reinforcement-learning environments, long-horizon agent tasks, benchmarks, and supervised fine-tuning demonstrations used to train and evaluate frontier AI models. Its offerings include off-the-shelf and custom datasets, agent-trajectory capture (tool calls, pivots, recovery attempts), and domain-sensitive evaluations across software engineering, data science, cybersecurity, machine learning, and research. Datacurve is backed by Homebrew and publishes research such as the DeepSWE long-horizon coding benchmark. The company sells through direct engagement (contact@datacurve.ai) and currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

companies.name: Datafleets
companies.description: DataFleets was a privacy-preserving data science and federated computation platform that let organizations run analytics and machine learning across distributed, siloed, or regulated datasets without centralizing or exposing the underlying raw data, using techniques such as federated learning and differential privacy to keep data in place while still enabling cross-silo insight. Founded as a venture-backed startup and backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, DataFleets was acquired by LiveRamp in early 2021. Its former datafleets.com domain now redirects to liveramp.com, and the company operates no independent public developer portal, API, or documentation, so there is no live API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

companies.name: DataFox
companies.description: DataFox was a San Francisco company-intelligence and sales-prospecting startup, backed by GV among others, that used machine learning to collect and score signals about private and public companies (funding rounds, hiring, news, growth signals) and delivered them to sales and marketing teams through a web application, CRM integrations, and a company-data API. Oracle acquired DataFox and folded its company-and-signals data into the Oracle Cloud CX / Oracle Fusion Marketing stack. The independent product has been fully retired: as of this profile the datafox.com apex and www hosts are served from Oracle infrastructure and every path under www.datafox.com issues a blanket HTTP 301 to Oracle marketing pages, while api.datafox.com and app.datafox.com resolve to a parked Oracle address that accepts no connections. There is no surviving DataFox developer portal, documentation, API reference, or specification to harvest, so this profile is retained as a historical/acquired company record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: DataGravity
companies.description: DataGravity was a data management and security software company founded in April 2012 in Nashua, New Hampshire by Paula Long (co-founder of EqualLogic) and John Joseph. It pioneered the "data-aware storage" category, shipping hybrid storage arrays that indexed, classified, and audited data in place so that security, governance, and search became properties of the storage tier rather than bolt-on tooling. The company raised venture funding from Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, CRV and others, won Best of Show at VMworld 2014, and began shipping in October 2014. In February 2016 it pivoted from appliances to a software-only behavioral data-security product. DataGravity ceased operations in June 2017 and its assets were assigned to a liquidator; HyTrust acquired the technology and roughly twenty employees, folding the product into HyTrust CloudAdvisor (HyTrust was itself acquired by Entrust in 2021). The datagravity.com domain no longer belongs to the company and now 301-redirects to an unrelated business (anomalo.com). No public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable specification survives, so there is no API surface for this profile to describe.

companies.name: Datalogix
companies.description: Datalogix was a consumer-purchase and marketing data company that connected offline buying behavior to digital advertising audiences, enabling measurement and targeting for brands and ad platforms. Backed by General Catalyst and IVP, it was acquired by Oracle in 2014 and folded into the Oracle Data Cloud. The datalogix.com domain now 301-redirects to Oracle's acquisitions page, and no standalone Datalogix developer portal, API, or documentation remains publicly available.

companies.name: Datorama
companies.description: Datorama was a cloud-based marketing intelligence and analytics platform founded in 2012 in Tel Aviv and New York. It unified marketing, advertising, and sales data from thousands of disparate sources into a single AI-powered reporting and dashboarding layer, using its "Genius" machine-learning engine to automate data harmonization across ad, social, web, and CRM APIs. Salesforce acquired Datorama in August 2018 for a reported ~$800 million and rebranded it as Salesforce Marketing Cloud Intelligence (Marketing Intelligence). The standalone datorama.com domain now 301-redirects to the Salesforce Marketing Intelligence product page, and the former standalone developer/API surface has been folded into Salesforce documentation. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a lightspeed-venture-partners portfolio lead.

companies.name: DecisionPoint Software
companies.description: DecisionPoint Software was a San Mateo, California-based enterprise software company that provided packaged financial performance management (FPM) and financial data warehousing software, built primarily around the Oracle ERP stack. Its systems captured and moved continuously changing data from financial source systems into a data warehouse, automatically configuring the analytic environment as the source systems changed, and shipped as far as Release 11 with operations in both the United States and the United Kingdom. The company was named one of the 50 fastest-growing private companies in Silicon Valley in 2004 and raised a $5M Series B round from Battery Ventures that same year. It was acquired in December 2005 by NCR's Teradata data warehousing division, which folded the FPM and data warehousing technology into the Teradata enterprise data warehouse offering. DecisionPoint Software has not operated as an independent company for roughly two decades: it publishes no website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface, and this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: Dverse
companies.description: Dverse is the API Evangelist network profile for Symmetry Dimensions Inc. (株式会社SYMMETRY), a Tokyo-based technology company whose "DVERSE" digital-twin lineage evolved into a portfolio of DX solution services, infrastructure operations and maintenance support (インフラ維持管理支援), and SDTC data services. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the network as an enrichment lead. The branded domain symmetry-dimensions.com now redirects to the company's live site at symmetry-inc.co.jp. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate/marketing site (a Nuxt single-page app on Google Cloud) but no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, CLI, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface — so no machine-readable API artifacts could be harvested. This record therefore carries company identity plus a probed domain-security profile only, and remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

companies.name: E8 Storage Systems
companies.description: E8 Storage Systems was an Israeli enterprise storage startup that built rack-scale NVMe flash arrays, separating high-performance shared flash from compute so that data-intensive workloads could reach local-NVMe latency over the network. The company was backed by Accel and was acquired by Amazon; the acquisition was reported on 2019-07-31. E8 no longer operates as an independent vendor and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API. Its historical domain, e8storage.com, is retained defensively but does not resolve: there are no address or mail records, and DMARC aggregate reports are directed to dmarc.amazon.com. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical big-data and storage-infrastructure record with no active API surface to enrich.

companies.name: eBureau
companies.description: eBureau was a predictive analytics and big-data scoring company founded in 2004 and headquartered in St. Cloud, Minnesota, providing real-time predictive scores, identity verification, and fraud-prevention products (eScore, eIDverifier, eIDcompare) to lenders, insurers, and marketers. eBureau was acquired by TransUnion in December 2015 and its capabilities were absorbed into TransUnion's fraud and identity solutions; the ebureau.com domain remains live (behind Cloudflare) but exposes no independent public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Redpoint Ventures and enriched with a live domain-security probe.

companies.name: EdgeSpring
companies.description: EdgeSpring is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of kleiner-perkins, lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Edia
companies.description: Edia is an AI platform for K-12 school districts focused on improving student outcomes. Its products span AI math tutoring (reported 8-23% score improvements), attendance intervention to reduce chronic absenteeism (up to 30% reduction), and District Intelligence analytics that consolidate data from student information systems (SIS), learning management systems (LMS), behavior, and wellness sources into a single view for educators and administrators. Edia reports serving 200+ districts and 500K+ students. The company is backed by Felicis and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced company profile. Edia does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or API specification, so this profile carries only verifiable company identity and probed domain-security posture.

companies.name: EduPristine
companies.description: EduPristine is a Mumbai-based finance, accounting, and analytics training institute founded in 2008, offering classroom and online certification-prep and professional up-skilling programs. Its catalog spans financial modeling, CFA, FRM, ACCA, US CPA and US CMA, business analytics and data science, digital marketing, financial accounting (Big 4 aligned), and healthcare/medical coding. EduPristine runs training centers across India alongside self-paced and instructor-led online courses, and is part of Adtalem Global Education. Sector: edtech. No public developer API or documented API surface was found during enrichment; the corporate website sits behind a WAF that blocks automated discovery of a well-known or developer surface.

companies.name: ENGIE Insight Services
companies.description: ENGIE Insight Services (formerly Ecova, now operating as ENGIE Impact) is a sustainability and resource-management company that helps corporations, cities, and governments reduce their environmental footprint and operating costs. It provides energy, water, and waste expense management, utility bill auditing and payment, data management, sustainability consulting, and decarbonization strategy across a large portfolio of client sites. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, this profile has been enriched with domain-security and discovery probes; the company publishes no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

companies.name: Enhanced Radar
companies.description: Enhanced Radar is a San Francisco-based applied AI company building intelligent systems for aviation, the world's most complex transportation domain. Its work centers on pilot-controller communications, where the company owns the full pipeline from data collection through in-house labeling and quality assurance to produce high-quality aviation AI training datasets. Products include Pattern, an aviation operational intelligence platform; ATC.com, a live air traffic control radio service; and Y4, an aviation understanding model announced in February 2026. Enhanced Radar has demonstrated real-time detection of runway incursion risks and raised $7 million in May 2026. It is backed by DCVC and Initialized Capital. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: eVestment Alliance
companies.description: eVestment Alliance is an institutional investment data, analytics, and market-intelligence platform founded in 2000 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. Institutional asset managers report performance, holdings, and firm data into the platform, while investment consultants, asset owners, and allocators use it to research, screen, and compare managers, funds, and strategies across traditional and alternative asset classes. eVestment was acquired by Nasdaq in 2017 and is now delivered as part of Nasdaq's investment-intelligence solutions; its primary website redirects to nasdaq.com/solutions/evestment/. Originally backed by Insight Partners, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface is currently published.

companies.name: Farmeron
companies.description: Farmeron was a dairy herd-management and farm-analytics SaaS founded in 2011 in Osijek, Croatia, that helped dairy producers track animals, feed, milk production, and farm operations through a web platform and data integrations. The company went through the 500 Startups accelerator and was acquired by the machine-vision agriculture firm Cainthus in 2016, after which the standalone Farmeron product was wound down. This network profile is retained as a historical/portfolio lead; the farmeron.com domain is registered but no longer serves a live website or API, so there is no public developer surface to enrich.

companies.name: FireVisor
companies.description: FireVisor is an AI-based manufacturing analytics platform that helps manufacturers leverage their production data beyond traditional defect detection and process control methods. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Singapore (with a secondary office in Toronto, Canada), FireVisor works toward "self-aware factories powered by artificial intelligence," applying machine learning to manufacturing and industrial-automation data. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this profile the public firevisor.com site returns a 404 from its load balancer and exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

companies.name: FirstFuel Software
companies.description: FirstFuel Software was a business-focused energy analytics SaaS company that used utility meter and building data to profile commercial and industrial customers, helping utilities target energy-efficiency and customer-engagement programs. The company was acquired by Uplight, and the firstfuel.com domain now redirects to uplight.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. The enrichment pipeline found no active first-party developer surface (no developer, api, or docs subdomains resolve, and no OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP artifacts are published), so this profile remains an identity-only record for a company that no longer operates a standalone API program.

companies.name: Fliptop
companies.description: Fliptop was a San Francisco-based predictive marketing and customer intelligence startup that applied data science and machine learning to CRM and marketing-automation data to score leads, predict conversion, and prioritize sales pipelines. Founded around 2009, it was acquired by LinkedIn in August 2015 and folded into LinkedIn's Sales Solutions (Sales Navigator) product. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its former domain fliptop.com now 301-redirects to business.linkedin.com/sales-solutions. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio-company record.

companies.name: Fortunes
companies.description: ForTunes was a Vienna-based mobile music data analytics application for self-publishing and DIY artists, managers, and small labels. The app collected and visualized performance data across Spotify, Apple Music, SoundCloud, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and other platforms into a single intelligent feed, with notifications for playlist adds and follower growth, a Spotify playlist recommendation engine, public artist profiles, and team collaboration. Backed by Speedinvest (2018), the company was acquired by Utopia Music in 2023. As of this profile the primary web domain (fortunes.io) no longer resolves and no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; the product surface is the consumer iOS and Android apps.

companies.name: Framed *
companies.description: Framed (framed.io), formerly Framed Data, was a GV-backed predictive-analytics / customer churn-prediction machine-learning startup. As of 2026 the framed.io domain no longer hosts a product or developer surface: it serves a static Squarespace landing page titled "Framed + Square" that points visitors to Square Capital (squareup.com/capital), indicating the team/product moved to Square. No API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable artifact surface survives, so there is nothing to enrich against; this record is retained as a dormant/acquired lead.

companies.name: Freshplum
companies.description: Freshplum was a San Francisco data-science startup (founded 2010) that built cloud-based predictive analytics for e-commerce, gauging online shopper behavior in real time to surface personalized promotional offers and discounts to visitors who might otherwise abandon a purchase. During its private alpha it was already processing over 10M requests a day. Freshplum raised roughly $1.7M from investors including DCVC and GV (Google Ventures) before being acquired by ad-targeting company TellApart in July 2014 (TellApart was in turn acquired by Twitter in 2015). The company is defunct: it ships no live product, developer portal, documentation, or public API, and the freshplum.com domain is now a parked listing offered for sale via Afternic. This profile is retained as a historical/portfolio record; there is no API surface to enrich.

companies.name: GAGO Group
companies.description: GAGO Group (Beijing Jiage Tianyu Technology Co., Ltd.) is a China-based frontier-technology company focused on agricultural and rural big data applications. Its homepage positions the business around agricultural and rural big data, applying remote-sensing and data-analytics techniques to agriculture. GAGO Group is backed by DCM Ventures and was added to the API Evangelist network from that portfolio. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate website at gagogroup.cn but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification could be verified, so no spec-derived API artifacts were produced.

companies.name: Gnip
companies.description: Gnip was a social media data aggregation company founded in 2008 in Boulder, Colorado by Eric Marcoullier and Jud Valeski. It became the first authorized reseller of the Twitter "firehose" and delivered enterprise-grade access to real-time and historical social data from Twitter, Tumblr, WordPress, Disqus, StockTwits and many other sources through products such as PowerTrack, Historical PowerTrack, the Search API, the Audience API and the Engagement API. Twitter acquired Gnip in April 2014 and folded its technology into Twitter's enterprise data platform; the Gnip brand and standalone APIs were retired and gnip.com now 301-redirects to the Twitter/X enterprise developer documentation. This profile is preserved for historical/network completeness — Gnip is no longer an independent provider.

companies.name: HiCustomer
companies.description: HiCustomer (ハイカスタマー) was a Japanese Customer Success Management (CSM) SaaS built specifically for SaaS companies. Its platform aggregated customer data scattered across BI tools, CRMs, and chat tools to visualize product usage, communication history, revenue, and contract information in one place. Teams used configurable health-score rules to monitor account health across the customer lifecycle, and custom alerts to surface churn and upsell signals at the right moment, with time-series analysis to make customer-success outreach repeatable. The company also offered customer-success consulting. As of this enrichment pass the hicustomer.jp domain no longer resolves to a live site (its authoritative AWS Route 53 zone is empty) and the product appears discontinued; the last archived homepage (Oct 2024) shows only a minimal "About the company" page. No public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal was ever published.

companies.name: Hitwise
companies.description: Hitwise was an online competitive-intelligence and audience-measurement company that tracked website traffic, clickstream behavior, and search-term data to help marketers benchmark share of visits, referral sources, and competitor performance across industry verticals. Originally an Australian firm, it was later owned by Experian and then Connexity. The Hitwise brand has since been retired -- as of this enrichment pass the hitwise.com domain no longer serves a live product (it returns a lapsed-host "Site is not available" page with a mismatched TLS certificate) and exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead of insight-partners; enrichment found no active API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Hyper 4
companies.description: Hyper (heyhyper.ai) is a Y Combinator-backed startup building "the self-driving company brain" — a knowledge-management platform that assembles a centralized, self-maintaining knowledge graph from a team's emails, Slack, GitHub, calendars, and other work sources, then feeds that context back into AI agents and tools so they act with accurate company memory and require fewer repeated corrections. Founded in 2026 by Shalin Shah and Kanyes Thaker and based in San Francisco, the company was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this profile Hyper is very early-stage, publishing only a marketing landing page at heyhyper.ai with no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface yet available; this record captures verified company identity and will be re-enriched as a developer platform is published.

companies.name: Id Analytics
companies.description: ID Analytics was a San Diego-based identity risk and fraud analytics company founded in 2002. It operated the ID Network, a cross-industry consortium of consumer identity behavior, and productized it as ID Score and related fraud-detection, credit-risk, and identity-verification analytics used by financial services, telecommunications, and government. The company was acquired by LifeLock in 2012, passed to Symantec when it bought LifeLock in 2017, and was sold to LexisNexis Risk Solutions in 2020, where its capabilities are now delivered. It no longer operates an independent developer portal or public API; idanalytics.com now redirects to LexisNexis Risk Solutions.

companies.name: IHS
companies.description: IHS was a global information and analytics company providing critical insight to customers across industries including aerospace, defense, automotive, chemicals, energy, and financial services. IHS merged with Markit in 2016 to form IHS Markit, which was subsequently acquired by S&P Global in 2022. The legacy ihs.com domain now redirects to S&P Global. No public IHS-branded APIs are tracked here; current API offerings live within S&P Global product lines.

companies.name: Illustra
companies.description: Illustra Information Technologies was an object-relational database company founded in 1992 by Michael Stonebraker, Gary Morgenthaler and several of Stonebraker's students to commercialize the Postgres research project. Its DataBlade extensibility modules let structured and unstructured multimedia data (text, geospatial, web content) be stored and indexed as true objects. NASA selected it in 1995 to store millions of satellite images. Informix Corporation acquired the company in 1996 and folded the object-relational engine and DataBlades into what became Informix Universal Server; that lineage passed to IBM and is now maintained by HCL Technologies. Illustra no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no standalone website, developer portal, or API. This record was surfaced from a historical Trinity Ventures portfolio list; enrichment found no live API surface.

companies.name: Instante
companies.description: Instante (also listed as Istante Software) is a data-warehousing software company that received a seed investment from Canaan Partners, with John Balen listed as the sponsoring partner on Canaan's portfolio page. The company is profiled as an application software provider building tools for data warehousing. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist VC-portfolio pipeline as a Canaan Partners portfolio lead. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no public developer surface. No reachable company website, API, developer documentation, SDKs, OpenAPI, or event/webhook surface could be verified. The candidate domains instante.com (a parked domain listed for sale) and instante.io (an unrelated Brazilian consumer photo-gallery app) are not this company.

companies.name: Invidica
companies.description: Invidica is an Oakland-based B2B wholesale ecommerce marketplace (founded 2019) that upgrades the wholesaler-retailer relationship for the reseller economy. It pairs a marketplace where resellers order wholesale products directly from brands with AI-driven analytics that combine Amazon sales data to predict an item's profitability, sales velocity, and competition, helping small sellers find the most profitable products to resell. Founded by CEO Sean Bovell and backed by 500 Global and 1517 Fund (pre-seed, 2021). The company appears to be pivoting under the Reroute Retail brand (rerouteretail.com, "launching soon"); its original invidica.com domain no longer resolves. No public API or developer surface is currently published.

companies.name: Isidor
companies.description: Isidor is a frontier enterprise-AI company, founded in 2025 and headquartered in San Francisco with a London presence, building secure, vertically-integrated data pipelines that transform unstructured proprietary enterprise data into training- and evaluation-ready material for foundation models. Its platform spans five capabilities it describes as evaluation (industry-specific and agentic benchmarks), verifiers for generative-AI outputs in critical workflows, reasoning-trace data capture, foundation-model post-training (fine-tuning and alignment on proprietary data), and enterprise-grade security and privacy. Isidor raised an oversubscribed $3.6M pre-seed led by Gradient Ventures, futurepresent, and Seedcamp, with angels from Google DeepMind, Perplexity, and others. The company has no public API or developer surface yet; this profile tracks it as an enrichment lead in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Itemfield
companies.description: Itemfield was an enterprise data-integration software company known for its Complex Data Exchange (CDE) and B2B data-transformation technology, which parsed, mapped, and transformed complex, unstructured, and industry-standard message formats into structured data. Itemfield was acquired by Informatica in 2006, and its technology was absorbed into Informatica's B2B Data Transformation product line. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no surviving independent Itemfield developer surface: the itemfield.com domain now resolves under Informatica-managed DNS and serves no HTTP content, so there is no live API, documentation, portal, or specification to harvest.

companies.name: Jask Labs
companies.description: Jask Labs (JASK) was a cybersecurity company that built an Autonomous Security Operations Center (ASOC) platform — applying machine learning and analytics on top of network and security telemetry to triage and prioritize security alerts and reduce SOC analyst workload. Backed by Battery Ventures among other investors, JASK was acquired by Sumo Logic in 2019 and folded into Sumo Logic's cloud SIEM / Cloud SOC offering. Jask Labs no longer operates as an independent company: its domains (jask.ai and jask.com) now permanently redirect (HTTP 301) to sumologic.com, and there is no standalone Jask Labs developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or live product surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a portfolio-lead stub with the acquisition recorded.

companies.name: Katch
companies.description: Katch is a Speedinvest-backed agricultural technology and embedded-finance platform serving agribusiness supply chains. It offers essential digital services for its partners, including e-commerce, grain procurement, and business intelligence, and layers embedded financial solutions such as factoring and credit directly within transactions. This lets agricultural partners manage cash flow, access working capital, and streamline supply-chain operations from a single platform. Katch was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; an enrichment pass found no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI, or machine-readable API surface for the company at this time.

companies.name: Kimono Labs
companies.description: Kimono Labs was a developer-tools startup that let users turn any website into a structured API without writing code, using a visual point-and-click tool to define data selectors that Kimono would crawl on a schedule and expose as JSON/CSV endpoints and RSS feeds. Founded in 2014 by Pratap Ranade and Ryan Rowe and backed by Cowboy Ventures, the company was acquired by Palantir Technologies in February 2016, after which the hosted cloud service at kimonolabs.com was shut down on 29 February 2016; a downloadable Kimono Desktop application was released as a farewell so existing scrapers could continue running locally. The company is defunct and operates no live API today; this profile is retained for historical and network completeness.

companies.name: Kyndoo
companies.description: Kyndoo Inc. was a San Francisco based influencer-marketing software platform that let brands find, connect to and work with social-media influencers. Its differentiator was audience authenticity: Kyndoo built a database of vetted influencers and published the "Kyndex" score, described as a credit score for influencers, which measured whether a following was made of real people with buying intent rather than purchased bot accounts. Around that database it sold campaign management, attribution and brand-safety tooling to brands, taking a service fee on the influencer deals brands negotiated through the platform. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Kyndoo was acquired by CIPIO (cipio.ai) and its web property is now offline - kyndoo.com has not served a page since early 2022. Kyndoo never published a public API, developer portal or SDK, so this profile is an identity and lifecycle record rather than an API profile.

companies.name: L2
companies.description: L2 Inc was a subscription research and business intelligence firm founded in New York City in 2010 by NYU Stern marketing professor Scott Galloway and co-founder Maureen Mullen. L2 benchmarked the digital competence of consumer brands, publishing more than 25 Digital IQ Index reports each year covering over 2,200 brands across fashion, luxury, retail, beauty, financial services, hospitality and consumer packaged goods. Its research scored brands on site experience, e-commerce, digital marketing, social media and mobile execution, and was sold as a subscription to CMOs and senior marketing leaders. The firm raised roughly $16.5 million in venture funding, including backing from General Catalyst (Larry Bohn and Paul Sagan) from 2014. Gartner acquired L2 in March 2017, when it had about 150 employees across New York and London, and folded the Digital IQ research into Gartner for Marketers. L2 never operated a public developer program or API: its research was delivered through a subscriber web platform and published reports. The l2inc.com domain is registered but no longer resolves, and no L2-branded developer, documentation or API surface remains online. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record with no API artifacts.

companies.name: LearnSprout
companies.description: LearnSprout was a San Francisco edtech company founded in 2012 by Franklyn Chien, Anthony Wu and Joe Woo out of the Imagine K12 accelerator. It built LearnSprout Connect, an API layer that unlocked K-12 student data held in student information systems (SIS) through direct database integration rather than the SIS application layer, giving edtech developers a single "once and done" integration plus a change-log endpoint for incremental syncs. It also sold a district-facing analytics product covering attendance, grades and college readiness, reaching over 2,500 schools across 42 states on roughly $4.7M raised from Andreessen Horowitz, Formation 8 and Samsung Ventures. Apple acquired the company in January 2016 and the public API was retired; learnsprout.com no longer resolves and is parked on Apple nameservers.

companies.name: Linkett
companies.description: Linkett is a digital out-of-home (DOOH) analytics platform for digital signage and retail displays. Its proprietary technology passively gathers audience data at the screen and reports real-time campaign performance metrics such as impressions, dwell time, and engagement, giving advertising agencies detailed client reporting and giving advertisers measurement they can tie back to return on ad spend. Linkett is headquartered in Canada with offices in Toronto and California, and was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Linkett publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification, and its website is served behind a bot/CAPTCHA challenge that blocks automated retrieval.

companies.name: MAGNiTT
companies.description: MAGNiTT is a venture data platform covering startups, investors, and funding activity across emerging venture markets, with a focus on the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) and adjacent emerging ecosystems. It aggregates data on startup companies, venture capital and corporate investors, funding rounds, and exits, and publishes market research and analytics reports used by founders, investors, and enterprises to track venture activity. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass MAGNiTT publishes no discoverable public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery surface; the platform is a subscription-based data product served behind login and bot protection.

companies.name: MapReduce
companies.description: MapReduce is a programming model and processing technique for computing large data sets in parallel across a distributed cluster. Originally developed by Google and popularized by Apache Hadoop, it splits data processing into map and reduce phases to enable scalable big data analytics.

companies.name: Markov
companies.description: Markov (Markov Studios) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building data and environments for training computer-use AI. The company captures how people actually use computers - screen recordings with synchronized mouse and keyboard inputs, annotations, and open datasets across real workflows in tools like Salesforce, Blender, and Photoshop, plus gaming data from Valorant, Minecraft, and GTA. Markov sources high-quality tasks and data to train the next generation of computer-use and reinforcement-learning models, releasing much of its work in public on Hugging Face (150k+ dataset downloads). Founded in 2026 by Dev Mandal (CEO) and Harish Ashok, Markov distributes its datasets through Hugging Face rather than a first-party API; this profile currently tracks no public API surface.

companies.name: Massive Dynamic
companies.description: Massive Dynamic is an AI-powered advertising platform that bills itself as "The Advertising Copilot" and "the human-AI interface for massive scale." It helps media and advertising teams coordinate large-scale digital ad campaigns by pairing an AI Analysis Copilot (automating daily analytics checks, quarterly business reviews, and Media Mix Modeling) with Execution Delegation, where an AI agent handles operational campaign setup so strategists can focus on decisions. The tool works inside existing Slack and email workflows as a conduit between strategy and activation teams, and emphasizes enterprise-grade data governance with ring-fenced customer data and an explicit commitment not to use customer data to train or improve models. The company was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: Merkle
companies.description: Merkle Data is a risk-management and analytics platform for crypto institutions, founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York. The platform aggregates proprietary market data (its Pulse dataset), public blockchain data, and third-party feeds to give funds, trading desks, and other digital-asset institutions actionable analytics across portfolio risk, liquidity risk, and counterparty risk, delivered through both interactive dashboards and programmatic APIs. Merkle Data is backed by Pantera Capital. As of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API reference, or SDK is discoverable and merkledata.io resolves to a login-gated institutional dashboard, so this record captures identity only.

companies.name: Merklebase, Inc.
companies.description: Merklebase provides data-driven infrastructure for institutional digital-asset finance, spanning enterprise data management, a core portfolio management system, reporting and accounting, risk management, a trade capture system, and a digital-asset loan management system. It advertises connectivity to 220+ custodians, trading venues, and data providers, and is used by hedge funds, asset managers, and financial institutions to streamline front-to-back operations across fiat, crypto, derivatives, and stablecoins. A developer API and connectivity layer is referenced by customers, but the public developer surface (docs.merklebase.io on Theneo) is currently unpublished and the API (api.merklebase.io, AWS API Gateway) is gated, so no public OpenAPI/SDK artifacts are harvestable yet.

companies.name: Metaphor
companies.description: Metaphor was an active-metadata / data-catalog platform (metaphor.io) that combined a social, agent-assisted data governance experience with a large library of open-source Python "connectors" that extracted metadata (schemas, lineage, usage, ownership, documentation, data quality) from warehouses, BI tools, and data pipelines to populate the Metaphor app. Founded by ex-LinkedIn DataHub engineers and backed by Amplify Partners, Metaphor's technology platform was acquired by KPMG; the metaphor.io site now redirects to the KPMG acquisition announcement and the standalone developer surface (docs.metaphor.io, api.metaphor.io, the MetaphorData GitHub org) has been decommissioned. The first-party open-source metadata packages (metaphor-connectors, metaphor-models) still resolve on PyPI.

companies.name: miim
companies.description: mi|im (pronounced "mime", for Movement Imaging | Intelligence Matters) develops proprietary machine-learning and computer-vision technology that turns movement into intelligence for retail. Its movement-imaging platform analyzes and optimizes how people flow through physical space, helping retailers improve customer experience, drive operational efficiency, and detect and respond to events. Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital; no public API, developer portal, or documentation was found during enrichment (the miim.ai domain currently returns a parked WordPress error page).

companies.name: Minit
companies.description: Minit was a process-mining software company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Bratislava, Slovakia. Its platform ingested event-log data from systems of record (ERP, CRM, service desks) to reconstruct, visualize, and analyze how business processes actually run, surfacing bottlenecks, rework, compliance gaps, and automation opportunities. Backed by Earlybird Venture Capital (among other investors), Minit was acquired by Microsoft in March 2022, and its process-mining technology was folded into Microsoft Power Automate Process Mining (process advisor). The standalone Minit product, developer surface, and minit.io site have been retired; the domain now resolves through Microsoft-controlled Azure DNS and no longer serves a public site or API. This profile is retained as a network record of an acquired company; there is no independent Minit API to enrich.

companies.name: MLnetworks
companies.description: MLNetworks is an AI-powered telecommunications network optimization company, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The company positions itself around helping telcos "unlock the full potential of your telco network," delivering AI-driven insights, an advertised ~30% reduction in CAPEX/OPEX, and faster network problem resolution. As of this enrichment pass the public surface at mlnetworks.io is a marketing site only (a Next.js/Vercel single-page app) with no published developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery documents — all probed endpoints returned 404 and no docs/api/developer subdomains resolve. Go-to-market is a Calendly discovery-call booking rather than a self-serve developer signup.

companies.name: Moat
companies.description: Moat was an advertising measurement and analytics company, backed by Insight Venture Partners and Mayfield, that measured ad viewability, attention, and brand safety across digital and video advertising. Oracle acquired Moat in 2017 and folded it into Oracle Advertising (Oracle Moat / Oracle Data Cloud). The independent moat.com brand no longer operates a standalone developer program: www.moat.com now 301-redirects to oracle.com/advertising, and the bare moat.com host no longer negotiates TLS. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/absorbed company lead with no independent public API surface.

companies.name: Narrative Science
companies.description: Narrative Science was a Chicago-based artificial-intelligence company known for its Quill natural-language-generation (NLG) platform, which automatically turned structured data into written narratives and data stories. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Sapphire Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company no longer operates independently: Salesforce acquired Narrative Science in December 2021 and folded its technology into Tableau. The former corporate domain (www.narrativescience.com) now 301-redirects to Tableau's AI/augmented-analytics pages, and no developer, api, or docs subdomains resolve. There is no independent public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface remaining to enrich; this profile is retained as a historical/acquisition record.

companies.name: Natero
companies.description: Natero was a customer-success and predictive-analytics platform (an Andreessen Horowitz portfolio company) that helped SaaS teams reduce churn, monitor account health, and drive expansion using machine learning. It was acquired by Freshworks in 2019 and folded into the Freshsuccess product line. As of this enrichment pass the standalone company is defunct - the natero.com domain no longer resolves to a website, and there is no live developer portal, API reference, or public API surface to catalog.

companies.name: Natural Intelligence Systems
companies.description: Natural Intelligence Semiconductor (Natural Intelligence Systems) is a fabless semiconductor startup founded in 2016 and headquartered in Boise, Idaho, led by founder and CEO Paul Dlugosch. The company is developing the Natural Neural Processor (NNP), a novel processor architecture inspired by the human neocortex to deliver disruptive performance for artificial intelligence and big-data analytics workloads. Its roadmap spans the chips, system boards, and a software tool chain of compilers, drivers, and low-level APIs needed to bring the NNP into customer systems. It exposes no public web API today; the developer surface is chip- and driver-level tooling. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead.

companies.name: Next Big Sound
companies.description: Next Big Sound was a music-industry analytics company founded in 2009 out of Techstars Boulder that tracked artists' social, streaming, and airplay signals (plays, fans, engagement across Spotify, YouTube, SoundCloud, radio and social platforms) and exposed them through a REST developer API used by labels, managers and media. It was backed by Foundry Group, Uncork Capital (SoftTech VC), Alsop Louie and IA Ventures, and was acquired by Pandora in August 2015. Its analytics became Pandora's artist tools and were folded into the Pandora / SiriusXM Artist Marketing Platform (AMP). The standalone developer API and portal (developer.nextbigsound.com) have been deprecated; nextbigsound.com now resolves to Pandora infrastructure and HTTP redirects to amp.pandora.com. This profile is retained as a network identity record for a defunct/acquired provider — no independent live API surface remains to harvest.

companies.name: Node.io
companies.description: Node (Node.io, legally Node Inc.) was an artificial-intelligence startup founded in 2014 by former Google executive Falon Fatemi. Node marketed an "artificial intuition" platform that combined a customer's CRM data with a large external graph of people and companies to score and predict which prospects, partners, employees, or investors a business should engage next. The company raised roughly $16M from investors including 500 Global, Mark Cuban, Avalon Ventures, Canaan Partners, and Bee Partners. On 2020-08-24 Node Inc. was acquired by SugarCRM, which folded the technology into its sales and CX products rather than continuing to sell it as a standalone product. Node.io no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation, or public API; the node.io domain is now a parked GoDaddy/Afternic "for sale" listing. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record with no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Normalyze
companies.description: Normalyze was a data security posture management (DSPM) company that helped organizations discover, classify, and protect sensitive data across SaaS, PaaS, multi-cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments, mapping data access paths and prioritizing risk. Backed by Battery Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners, Normalyze was acquired by Proofpoint in 2024 and its capabilities are now delivered as part of the Proofpoint Data Security Posture Management product line; the normalyze.ai domain redirects to Proofpoint. Normalyze never published a standalone public developer portal, API reference, or SDK, so this profile has no independent API surface to enrich.

companies.name: NS8
companies.description: NS8 was an e-commerce fraud-prevention and behavioral-analytics vendor (Protect / Score / TrueStats) surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the company appears defunct with no reachable web or API surface — ns8.com carries only AWS Route53 nameservers and a Google recovery-domain-verification TXT record but resolves to no A record (apex, www, api, and developer subdomains all fail to resolve), it is not present in the APIs.io catalog, and no OpenAPI, developer portal, SDK, or other API artifact could be discovered.

companies.name: Observo Ai
companies.description: Observo AI was an AI-powered data pipeline platform for observability and security telemetry. Its product reduced log and event volume (filtering low-value data by up to ~80%), normalized diverse telemetry formats into standardized schemas such as OCSF, and enriched data at ingest before it reached a SIEM or observability backend. Founded to tame the roughly 35% annual growth of security and observability data, the company was backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and was subsequently acquired by SentinelOne, where the technology now ships as Singularity AI Data Pipelines. The former observo.ai domain now 301-redirects to SentinelOne and the company no longer operates an independent public developer or API surface.

companies.name: OGSystems
companies.description: OGSystems was a geospatial intelligence, data analytics, and advanced technology company based in Chantilly, Virginia, serving the United States intelligence community and Department of Defense with threat analytics, machine learning, and geospatial exploitation solutions. The company was acquired by Parsons Corporation in 2019 and folded into Parsons' national security and intelligence portfolio. Its former domain (ogsystems.com) now redirects to parsons.com, and it maintains no independent public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an identity/lead record surfaced from VC-portfolio data; there are no API artifacts to enrich.

companies.name: Okera
companies.description: Okera was a data access governance and data security platform providing fine-grained, attribute-based access control, data discovery and classification, dynamic masking, and audit for analytics and machine-learning workloads across data lakes and warehouses. Founded around 2016, Okera was acquired by Databricks in May 2023 and folded into the Databricks governance stack (Unity Catalog). Okera no longer operates as an independent product: the okera.com domain now 301-redirects to databricks.com, and there is no standalone Okera developer portal, documentation, or public API surface remaining. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record.

companies.name: Omniture
companies.description: Omniture was a web analytics company founded in 1996 in Orem, Utah and backed by Battery Ventures. It went public in 2006 and was acquired by Adobe Systems in 2009 for approximately 1.8 billion dollars. Its flagship SiteCatalyst product became Adobe Analytics within the Adobe Experience Cloud, and the DataWarehouse and reporting interfaces were folded into Adobe's Analytics APIs. The omniture.com domain now redirects to adobe.com and no independent Omniture API surface exists. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead in the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: OnFarm
companies.description: OnFarm Systems, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Fresno, California, was an agriculture IoT data-integration company that offered a customizable dashboard aggregating in-field sensor and remotely gathered data (weather, soil, irrigation) into a single view for farming operations across the US, Europe, and Asia. OnFarm was acquired by SWIIM System in July 2018, at which point CEO Lance Donny became SWIIM's COO. The onfarm.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, and no live public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface remains. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; enrichment found no active API surface to harvest.

companies.name: Optiant
companies.description: Optiant, Inc. was a Boston-area supply chain optimization software company founded in 2000 on multi-echelon inventory optimization technology developed by researchers at MIT. Its flagship PowerChain suite (Network Design, Inventory, and Planner) let global manufacturers and distributors model multidimensional supply chains and free up working capital trapped across multi-echelon networks. Optiant was acquired by Logility, Inc. in 2010 (~$3.3M) and its technology was folded into Logility's Voyager Solutions suite as Voyager Inventory Optimization. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API surface; the optiant.com domain no longer resolves. This profile was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and enriched as a historical/defunct lead.

companies.name: Orchard
companies.description: Orchard (Orchard Platform Markets) was a New York City online-lending technology company founded in 2013 that provided data, analytics, reporting, and an order-management system connecting institutional investors with marketplace-lending originators. Backed by Canaan Partners and Spark Capital, Orchard was acquired by Kabbage in April 2018 (substantially all assets); its team joined Kabbage's data-science org and the standalone product and its developer surface were wound down. The orchardplatform.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live API, documentation, or developer portal to enrich.

companies.name: Orgspace
companies.description: Orgspace, Inc. was a B2B people-operations software company offering org design, staffing, and workforce analytics tools that integrated alongside existing HR/HRIS systems. Its product let teams create team configurations, propose org charts, visualize cost projections, and build headcount plans framed around assigning people into roles rather than tracking open positions. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As of this enrichment pass the orgspace.io domain no longer resolves (no DNS records) and the company appears defunct; no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface could be found.

companies.name: Origami Logic
companies.description: Origami Logic was a marketing-intelligence / big-data analytics company (backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners) surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network. As of the 2026-07-20 enrichment pass the origamilogic.com web surface is defunct: DNS resolves only Google Workspace mail (MX + SPF/DMARC) with no A record on the apex or www host, so there is no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. Domain-security posture was probed and recorded; no other public API artifacts exist. Retained as a historical company profile.

companies.name: OutlookSoft
companies.description: OutlookSoft was a corporate performance management (CPM) software company providing budgeting, planning, consolidation, forecasting, and financial reporting software. Originally surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub, enrichment confirmed OutlookSoft was acquired by SAP in 2007 and folded into SAP Business Planning and Consolidation (SAP BPC). The outlooksoft.com domain is now controlled by SAP (SAP nameservers) and serves no live site, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical company record; there is no independent API to enrich.

companies.name: Parstream
companies.description: ParStream was a big-data analytics database company founded in 2011 in Cologne, Germany by Michael Hummel, Joerg Bienert and Norbert Heuber. Its columnar, GPU-accelerated OLAP database was built for Internet-of-Things environments, filtering and analyzing billions of records in sub-second time at the edge of the network, with query access via SQL and a JSON query format plus a C++ API for user-defined query nodes. Cisco acquired ParStream on October 26, 2015 and folded the team into its Data and Analytics Group; the standalone product was declared obsolete and retired in 2018. The former parstream.com domain now redirects to a Cisco end-of-life product page, and no independent developer portal, API, SDK, or discovery surface remains to enrich.

companies.name: Periscope Data
companies.description: Periscope Data was a cloud business-intelligence and analytics platform (SQL-based dashboards, data exploration, and reporting for data teams), backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, SuSa Ventures and Threshold Ventures. It was acquired by Sisense in 2019; the product is now Sisense for Data Teams and the periscopedata.com domain 301-redirects to sisense.com. No standalone Periscope Data developer portal, documentation, or public API surface remains as of this enrichment pass.

companies.name: Petrarch
companies.description: Petrarch is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) data-marketplace company based in San Francisco that unlocks enterprise data for the AI economy. Petrarch sources proprietary, enterprise-facing datasets from distressed businesses and legacy industries such as construction, manufacturing, and logistics, clears and anonymizes them, and brokers them to AI companies and research labs building for the physical world. Notable data types transacted include construction plans, autonomous-driving recordings, and codebases. The company was founded by Harvard graduates Ian Lee, Samuel Hahn, and Sudhish Swain, with prior experience at organizations including Scale AI. As of this profile Petrarch operates a public marketing website but does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

companies.name: Phood Solutions
companies.description: Phood Solutions is a New York City-based food-waste technology company founded in 2015 by Luc Dang and Nick Kruczek. Its computer-vision platform, PhoodX, pairs a countertop scale and camera system with a waste-analytics dashboard to automatically identify, weigh, and categorize discarded food in commercial kitchens, grocery prepared-foods operations, and food-service venues. The platform reports product-level margins, recommends demand-based production volumes, and helps operators cut food waste by up to 50 percent, reduce kitchen labor, and lower food-inventory costs. Phood also offers Phood Lab, custom digital solutions built by its food technologists. The company is backed by Techstars. Phood publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

companies.name: Placemeter
companies.description: Placemeter was a New York City computer-vision analytics startup (a Techstars company) that turned live video feeds into real-time measurements of pedestrian and vehicle activity in physical places, offering a data API for foot-traffic and movement counts. The standalone product and developer API are no longer operational: placemeter.com no longer serves a website (the apex domain has no address record, carries no mail exchanger, and is defensively parked under Netgear's corporate registrar, CSC Corporate Domains), so there is no live API surface, documentation, SDK, or event stream to enrich.

companies.name: Platfora
companies.description: Platfora was a big-data analytics company founded in 2011 by Ben Werther that provided in-memory business intelligence and data visualization directly on top of Apache Hadoop, letting analysts run interactive queries, build "lenses," and share dashboards without ETL into a separate warehouse. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Battery Ventures, In-Q-Tel and others, it raised roughly $65M before Workday acquired the company in July 2016 and folded the technology into Workday's analytics stack. The standalone Platfora product and platfora.com developer surface were subsequently discontinued; the domain no longer resolves and no public API or developer program remains.

companies.name: Primary Data
companies.description: Primary Data was a software-defined storage and data-virtualization startup best known for its DataSphere platform, a metadata engine that abstracted files across heterogeneous storage tiers (flash, disk, cloud) behind a single global namespace and moved data automatically by policy. Backed by Battery Ventures among other investors, the company ceased operations in 2017, with much of its team and technology continuing at Hammerspace. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass the company is defunct and primarydata.com is a parked domain (GoDaddy lander), so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to harvest.

companies.name: Privitar
companies.description: Privitar was a UK-founded data privacy and data provisioning company known for its Data Privacy Platform, which applied de-identification, anonymization, tokenization and policy-based data access controls to sensitive data at scale for enterprises in financial services, healthcare and government. Privitar was acquired by Informatica in 2023 and folded into Informatica's data governance and privacy portfolio. As of this enrichment pass the privitar.com domain (and docs.privitar.com) permanently redirects (HTTP 301) to informatica.com, and no independent Privitar developer portal, API documentation, or API surface remains online. This profile is retained as a network lead record for the former company; live API artifacts now belong to Informatica.

companies.name: QuBit
companies.description: QuBit was a London-based ecommerce personalization and product-discovery platform — customer-experience optimization, recommendations, A/B testing, and behavioral big-data analytics — backed by Accel, Balderton Capital, and Sapphire Ventures. QuBit was acquired by Coveo in 2021 and fully absorbed into the Coveo Merchandising Hub. The qubit.com domain, its developer docs (docs.qubit.com), and every API and /.well-known/ endpoint now redirect to coveo.com and docs.coveo.com, so QuBit no longer operates an independent public API surface.

companies.name: Recommind
companies.description: Recommind was an enterprise information analytics and eDiscovery software company founded in 2000, best known for its CORE predictive-analytics platform and its Axcelerate eDiscovery and information-governance products used by legal and enterprise customers. OpenText acquired Recommind in 2016, and the Recommind brand and its technology are now folded into OpenText's Discovery and information-management portfolio. The standalone recommind.com domain now redirects to the OpenText brand page, and no independent Recommind developer portal, API reference, or API surface remains.

companies.name: reetian
companies.description: reetian (Chinese brand 瑞天数智, Reetian Digital Intelligence) is a China-based digital-intelligence company surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. Its public presence is a JavaScript single-page marketing site at reetian.com fronted by Cloudflare; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or source repositories that could be discovered and harvested. This profile remains a company-level lead pending a public API surface.

companies.name: Rentlytics
companies.description: Rentlytics was a multifamily real estate data analytics company founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, CA (with offices in Sacramento and Denver). Its platform consolidated operational and financial data scattered across multifamily assets into a unified business-intelligence layer, and it shipped products such as Open Data Services and Renovation Manager for per-unit and per-property yield visibility. Rentlytics was acquired by RealPage in 2018 for roughly $57 million and folded into RealPage's real-estate platform. As of this enrichment pass the standalone rentlytics.com domain is parked (it redirects to a generic lander) and the company operates no independent public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.

companies.name: RiskPulse
companies.description: RiskPulse was a supply chain risk and weather-intelligence company (also known by its Stormpulse brand) that scored and forecast weather, transit, and logistics disruption risk across supply chain networks. It was acquired by Everstream Analytics; the riskpulse.com and stormpulse.com domains now 301-redirect to everstream.ai, where the capability lives on as Everstream's Weather Intelligence and Analytics product. As of this enrichment pass there is no standalone RiskPulse public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or discovery surface, and Everstream exposes no public API either. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company lead.

companies.name: Riverpool
companies.description: Riverpool (riverpool.ai) is an early-stage, pre-launch startup building what it describes as the "post-modern analytics data stack" — a continuously circulating, self-refreshing approach to analytics data rather than a stagnant warehouse. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the public site is a "coming soon" landing page hosted on GitHub Pages with no launched product, developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or other API surface to catalog yet. This profile captures verified company identity and domain-security posture; API artifacts will be added when the product and its developer surface go live.

companies.name: RJMetrics
companies.description: RJMetrics was a Philadelphia-based business intelligence and analytics company (founded 2008, backed by Trinity Ventures, SoftTech VC and others) that helped online businesses centralize, model and visualize data from databases and SaaS tools. In 2016 the company was acquired by Magento; its analytics product became Magento Business Intelligence and now lives inside Adobe Commerce, while the data-pipeline team spun out the standalone product Stitch (later acquired by Talend). The RJMetrics brand no longer operates independently: rjmetrics.com issues a 301 redirect to the Adobe/Magento Business Intelligence product page, and there is no surviving RJMetrics developer portal, public API, SDK or documentation surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record rather than an active API provider.

companies.name: Rocana
companies.description: Rocana (formerly ScalingData) was an IT operations analytics company founded in 2014 in San Francisco and backed by GV.
