Its product captured and analyzed all machine data from all sources across data-center infrastructure, keeping it online and queryable for years so operations teams could perform root-cause analysis and surface emerging IT problems before they caused outages. The company raised roughly $19.4M before being acquired by Splunk in 2017, after which the independent Rocana product and brand were wound down. It was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment on 2026-07-21 confirmed there is no live public website (rocana.com no longer resolves), no developer portal, no API, and no client packages — the company no longer operates independently.

companies.name: Seculert
companies.description: Seculert was an Israeli cybersecurity company that provided cloud-based automated threat and attack detection, analytics, and breach-detection services, correlating outbound traffic and threat intelligence to identify compromised devices. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, it was acquired by Radware in January 2017 and folded into Radware's cloud security portfolio; the independent seculert.com brand is now defunct. This enrichment pass found no live independent API surface: the apex domain no longer serves TLS, www.seculert.com redirects to a dead HubSpot landing page, and no /.well-known, llms.txt, or developer/API documentation is published. Retained as a network profile of an acquired, now-inactive provider; DNS records (DMARC ruf to dmarc@radware.com) corroborate the Radware ownership.

companies.name: SeeCommerce
companies.description: SeeCommerce was a supply-chain performance management software company that provided analytics and management software focused on supply-chain visibility and problems. It raised roughly $47-58M across multiple venture rounds from investors including Insight Partners and Integral Capital Partners, and was acquired in February 2006. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct/acquired with no live website, developer portal, or public API surface (seecommerce.com no longer resolves to the company and other candidate domains do not resolve), so there are no API artifacts to harvest.

companies.name: Seek AI
companies.description: Seek AI was a New York City generative-AI enterprise data analytics company, backed by Battery Ventures, that built a conversational analytics agent letting business users query enterprise data in natural language and receive trustworthy answers (translating plain-language questions into SQL and narrative results over a company's own databases and warehouses). In 2025 Seek AI was acquired by IBM and folded into IBM watsonx AI Labs, a developer-first agentic-AI innovation hub in New York City; the company no longer operates an independent product, developer program, or public API. Its former developer subdomain (developers.seek.ai) now redirects to IBM's watsonx AI Labs, and the standalone seek.ai marketing site is no longer served. This API Evangelist profile records Seek AI as an acquired portfolio company and carries no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Shoppr
companies.description: Shoppr was a Malaysia-based consumer fashion-discovery mobile app (launched May 2015, often described as the "Tinder of fashion") that let shoppers swipe through personalized clothing recommendations. The founding team, led by Kendrick Wong, subsequently pivoted the business into Omnilytics, a B2B fashion retail market-intelligence and analytics platform serving brands and retailers. As of this enrichment pass the associated domain omnilytics.co is a parked domain (nameservers lander.d.parity.domains) and neither Shoppr nor Omnilytics exposes any public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal. This entry originated as a 500 Global portfolio lead and is retained for record; it has no API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Silver Tail
companies.description: Silver Tail Systems was a website fraud and abuse detection company founded in 2008 in Menlo Park, California by Mike Eynon and Laura Mather, both formerly on the anti-fraud team at eBay/PayPal. Its product collected and analyzed real-time web traffic to deliver web session intelligence and predictive analytics that detected fraud, account takeover, and abuse on banking and commerce websites. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) among others, the company raised roughly $20M across three rounds before being acquired by RSA, the security division of EMC, in 2012 and rebranded as RSA Web Threat Detection. It no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no live developer or API surface.

companies.name: Simply Measured
companies.description: Simply Measured was a Seattle-based social media analytics and reporting platform, founded in 2010 and backed by Trinity Ventures, that measured brand performance across Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and other social channels. It was acquired by Sprout Social in December 2017 and its product, brand, and developer surface were sunset and folded into Sprout Social. The simplymeasured.com domain now 301-redirects to sproutsocial.com and no independent Simply Measured API, developer portal, or documentation remains online. This record is retained as a defunct/acquired portfolio-lead marker; there is no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: Sisu Data
companies.description: Sisu Data was an a16z-backed augmented-analytics / decision-intelligence startup that automatically surfaced key drivers and anomalies in structured business data. It was acquired by Snowflake in October 2023 and the standalone product and developer surface were subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass the sisudata.com domain no longer hosts a product, developer portal, API, or documentation — it 301-redirects to the LinkedIn "Sisu is joining forces with Snowflake" announcement, and its TLS certificate expired in November 2024. No public API surface exists to enrich; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio record only.

companies.name: Skyboximaging
companies.description: Skybox Imaging was a satellite imaging and geospatial-analytics company (founded 2009, Mountain View, CA) that built a constellation of small high-resolution Earth-observation satellites (SkySat) and the analytics to turn frequent imagery into commercial insight. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Bessemer, Khosla Ventures and others, it was acquired by Google in 2014 (~$500M), renamed Terra Bella, and its satellite business was sold to Planet Labs in 2017. The skyboximaging.com domain is no longer a live product surface; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph and historical reference.

companies.name: SLP InfoWare
companies.description: SLP InfoWare was a French software company founded in 1989 by graduates of Telecom ParisTech and based in Paris, France, providing customer profiling, churn prediction, fraud detection, and retention analytics to the telecommunications, banking, and insurance industries. Its flagship products included CHURN MINER and a Churn/CPS application that analyzed customer billing data to predict and prevent subscriber attrition. The company raised venture funding and was acquired by Gemplus International SA in October 2000 (Gemplus later became part of Gemalto, now Thales). No independent SLP InfoWare website, developer portal, or public API surface exists today; this record is retained as a historical / portfolio-lineage entry in the API Evangelist network and carries no live API artifacts.

companies.name: StableBrowse
companies.description: StableBrowse is a San Francisco startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building browser infrastructure and real-world data pipelines for AI agents and AI labs. Its platform transforms dynamic websites into structured knowledge and execution graphs so agents can reliably complete web-based tasks — form filling, data extraction, authentication flows, and website change detection — without relearning workflows on every run, and it sources, labels, and enriches hard-to-find long-tail, gated, and ephemeral web data until it is worth training on. StableBrowse markets performance gains including large reductions in token usage, faster workflow execution, and high task success rates across use cases such as price monitoring, loan applications, CRM updates, travel booking, and navigation of legacy enterprise systems. The company was founded by Jay Mehta, Deepit Shah, and Somansh Shah (all formerly of Amazon). As of this profile the public site is a marketing landing page with no published API, developer documentation, or developer portal.

companies.name: Star Analytics
companies.description: Star Analytics is a business-intelligence software company described as a market leader in process automation and application integration across hybrid computing environments, with products built to address the automation and integration requirements of business intelligence software. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no public developer platform, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; the primary domain (staranalytics.com) resolves to a parking IP and does not serve HTTPS, consistent with a legacy company that is no longer independently operating.

companies.name: Statwing
companies.description: Statwing was a self-serve statistical-analysis SaaS tool that let non-statisticians run and interpret analyses on survey and spreadsheet data through a point-and-click interface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment (2026-07-21) found no live company or developer surface. Statwing was acquired by Qualtrics in 2015 and the product discontinued, and the statwing.com domain now serves an unrelated Thai-language lifestyle site. No API, documentation, SDKs, or developer resources exist.

companies.name: StyleSage
companies.description: StyleSage was a fashion and retail market-intelligence startup (Techstars-backed) that applied computer vision and data science to track apparel pricing, assortment, discounting, and trend signals across e-commerce retailers. The stylesage.co domain now redirects to Centric Software, which acquired the product and folded it into its Centric Market Intelligence platform for fashion, footwear, home, and beauty brands. As of this enrichment pass no standalone public developer API, documentation, SDK, or well-known surface is published for StyleSage.

companies.name: SumAll
companies.description: SumAll was a New York-based social media and business analytics startup, surfaced as a portfolio company of battery-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct - its primary domain sumall.com no longer resolves to a live product and is parked/listed for sale on Afternic. There is no live developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface to harvest, so no provider artifacts were produced.

companies.name: Survata
companies.description: Survata was a San Francisco market-research and brand-measurement company, backed by Bloomberg Beta, that ran online surveys and brand-lift studies to measure advertising effectiveness across digital channels. Survata was acquired by Upwave in 2019 and the brand has since been fully absorbed — survata.com now 301-redirects to upwave.com, the enterprise brand-measurement platform. No public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or well-known discovery surface is published for Survata or its Upwave successor; this profile is retained as a network lead with no live API surface.

companies.name: The Rainmaker Group Ventures (letitrain.com)
companies.description: letitrain.com was the corporate domain of The Rainmaker Group Ventures, LLC, an Atlanta-based hospitality revenue and profit optimization software vendor serving hotels, resorts and casinos. Rainmaker sold an "intelligent profit platform" built around three products: guestrev for transient pricing and science-based revenue management, grouprev for group pricing and evaluation, and revintel for business intelligence and reporting, with a demand forecast marketed to operators including Caesars Entertainment, Atlantis Casino Resort Spa and Two Roads Hospitality. The company was backed by Norwest Venture Partners and ran offices in Atlanta, Las Vegas, Singapore and Dubai. The brand is retired: letitrain.com now serves a blanket redirect to Cendyn, the acquiring company, its TLS certificate expired in December 2022, and no Rainmaker developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification was ever published or archived. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct-provider record with no active API surface.

companies.name: Tidemark
companies.description: Tidemark is enterprise financial and operational planning software for continuous, extended, and driver-based planning. It provides scenario ("what-if") modeling, workflow and approvals, and real-time data integration across 140+ ERP and EPM systems for budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning. Founded as a venture-backed cloud analytics and enterprise performance management (EPM) company and counted among the Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) portfolio, Tidemark was later acquired and is now offered as a product within the insightsoftware family. It has no publicly documented API, SDK, or developer portal; integration is delivered through pre-built ERP/EPM connectors rather than a public developer program.

companies.name: Toyota Connected
companies.description: Toyota Connected is Toyota Motor Corporation's global connected mobility technology arm, building the data, telematics, and software platforms that power Toyota and Lexus connected vehicle services worldwide. The group operates as a federation of regional subsidiaries — TOYOTA Connected Corporation (Japan), Toyota Connected North America (TCNA, Plano, Texas), TOYOTA Connected Europe (TCEU, United Kingdom), TOYOTA Connected India (TCIN), TOYOTA Connected Asia Pacific, and Toyota Tsusho Connected Middle East — and runs Toyota's Mobility Service Platform (MSPF) and the Drivelink telematics backbone behind Safety Connect, Service Connect, Remote Connect, Destination Assist, Wi-Fi Connect, and the "Hey Toyota" in-vehicle voice assistant. TCNA reports surpassing five million connected customer calls across Toyota and Lexus and runs Toyota's Big Data Center for connected-vehicle data. KINTO — Toyota's mobility services brand for car subscription, car-sharing, ride-hailing, and carpooling (KINTO One, KINTO Flex, KINTO Share, KINTO Ride, KINTO Join) — sits adjacent in Toyota's mobility portfolio and is powered by KINTO Technologies on AWS. Toyota exposes developer portals at developer.eig.toyota.com (Toyota API Portal covering TMC, TMNA, TEMA, TFS, NAMC, and other entities) and developer.toyotaconnected.eu (Toyota Connected EU API services, including Telematics and Vehicle APIs documented with Swagger/OpenAPI), but access is gated to partners and internal Toyota teams — no public, unauthenticated OpenAPI specifications are published. Third-party access to Toyota vehicle data for individual developers is typically brokered through partners such as Smartcar and High Mobility rather than directly via Toyota's own portals.

companies.name: Trace Data
companies.description: Trace Data (tracedata.io) was a data-security startup founded by James Donelan that built a platform integrating data observability, privacy, and security to track when and where company data is accessed as it moves across APIs, SaaS, and cloud, backed by venture investors including Accel. The company appears defunct: its website has been offline since after April 2021, and the tracedata.io DNS zone is now served by Netskope nameservers. No public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or GitHub surface remains.

companies.name: TrendKite
companies.description: TrendKite was an Austin, Texas PR and media intelligence platform founded in 2013 that used AI and big-data analytics to measure the impact of earned media on brand reputation, website traffic, and business goals. It was acquired by Cision in January 2019 for approximately $225 million and folded into the Cision Communications Cloud. TrendKite no longer operates as an independent company. Its former domain (trendkite.com) now redirects to cision.com, and no independent TrendKite developer portal, public API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface exists. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record; there is no standalone API surface to enrich.

companies.name: TrueLens
companies.description: TrueLens was a marketing-technology startup providing social media analytics and customer intelligence. Its product, Socialgraphics, helped brands target customers using data compiled and analyzed from multiple social networks for marketing campaigns. Google Ventures (GV) led a roughly $1.2M funding round in 2012; the company was small (2-10 employees). TrueLens now appears defunct: its former domain truelens.com 301-redirects to an unrelated retailer (misterspex.de), and no public API, developer portal, or documentation could be found. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a GV portfolio lead; there is no live API surface to enrich.

companies.name: TTAGG
companies.description: TTAGG was a social media analytics startup founded in October 2011 in Fayetteville, Arkansas, and backed by 500 Global. It rebranded as DataRank in 2013, providing brand managers with tools to monitor and rank conversations about their brands and competitors across social media, blogs, forums, and e-commerce sites. DataRank was acquired by Simply Measured in 2015, which was in turn acquired by Sprout Social in 2017. The company no longer operates independently and publishes no public API; datarank.com redirects to sproutsocial.com and ttagg.com is parked.

companies.name: TXN
companies.description: TXN (TXN Solutions, Inc.) was a San Francisco consumer spending analytics company that captured transactions directly from the credit and debit cards of an opt-in research panel, layering demographics and targeted surveys on top to give merchants competitive intelligence and share-of-wallet insight. Founded by Alex Rampell, Pasha Bitz, and Jonathan Wolf and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Bloomberg Beta, General Catalyst, Homebrew, SV Angel, and Slow Ventures, it is listed as exited in the Bloomberg Beta portfolio. As of July 2026 txn.com serves only a parked "Launching Soon" page on an Alibaba Cloud host with a self-signed TLS certificate — no product, developer, or API surface remains.

companies.name: TXN Solutions
companies.description: TXN Solutions (TXN) was a fintech startup founded in 2014 that offered a web application for consumer spending analytics, competitive intelligence, and surveys - capturing spending directly from the credit and debit cards of consumers who joined its research panel to give brands, investors, and researchers insight into consumer spending, merchant performance, and market positioning, including CPG and SKU-level data. It raised seed funding (announced November 2016) from a16z, Homebrew, Bloomberg Beta, and Social Starts. The company appears defunct as of July 2026 - its historical domain txn.com has been relinquished and is parked on the eName domain marketplace - and no public API surface is known.

companies.name: Unamo
companies.description: Unamo was a Warsaw, Poland based SaaS suite offering SEO monitoring, social media monitoring, and conversion rate optimization, formerly known as Positionly, and backed by Point Nine Capital. The company appears defunct as of July 2026, with unamo.com no longer resolving in DNS and the pre-rebrand positionly.com site serving stale 2017-era content whose API, signup, terms, and privacy pages return 404. No public API surface, client packages, or developer documentation remain online.

companies.name: Unifi
companies.description: Unifi Software was a self-service data platform built around an enterprise data catalog, with AI-based recommendations, data discovery, and data preparation tools aimed at business users. A Canaan Partners seed investment (led by Maha Ibrahim), the company was acquired by Dell Boomi, which announced its intent to acquire Unifi Software's data catalog and preparation technology in December 2019; by mid-2020 the Unifi site had been folded into Boomi. Its former domains no longer host the product — unifisoftware.com does not resolve and unifiyourdata.com is parked at Safenames — so no public API surface remains to catalog.

companies.name: Upcode Academy
companies.description: UpCode Academy was a Singapore-based coding school offering short bootcamps and part-time courses (SQL, Python, Web Development with Ruby on Rails, Data Science, Computer Vision, IoT) taught by industry practitioners. Operated by 40 Tasks, a 500 Global portfolio company whose earlier product was the LOCO location-based search app at 40tasks.com. The company appears defunct - upcodeacademy.com serves a Cloudflare 522 dead-origin error (a bare default server page by December 2025) and 40tasks.com no longer resolves in DNS (domain-squatted since about 2023). No public API surface was found.

companies.name: Valor Water Analytics
companies.description: Valor Water Analytics was a San Francisco-based water analytics company that built financial data and dashboard tools for water utilities, including leak and revenue-loss detection. A Y Combinator, Imagine H2O, and 500 Global portfolio company, it was acquired by Xylem Inc. (completed February 2, 2018) and folded into Xylem's digital portfolio, now represented by the Xylem Vue platform. valorwater.com redirects to Xylem Vue, and no independent API surface remains published.

companies.name: Versant
companies.description: Versant Corporation was an American software company that built specialized object and NoSQL data-management systems, notably the Versant Object Database (VOD) and the FastObjects embeddable object database. Its persistence technology was accessed through language-native C++, Java (JDO/JPA-style) and .NET APIs rather than a REST web API, and was deployed across telecommunications, energy, financial services, transportation, manufacturing and defense. Backed by Trinity Ventures, Versant IPO'd on NASDAQ (VSNT) in July 1996 and was acquired by Actian Corporation in December 2012; the product line continues today as the Actian NoSQL Object Database.

companies.name: VisualLogix
companies.description: VisualLogix develops mission-critical CAD, simulation, and analytical software used by engineers who design and validate real-world physical systems. Its tools span computer-aided design, physics and systems simulation, and analytical modeling for engineering teams building and testing products across industrial, mechanical, and infrastructure domains. VisualLogix is backed by Insight Partners. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing website (built with Figma Make) but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable discovery surface.

companies.name: Wildfire Interactive
companies.description: Wildfire Interactive, Inc. was a social media marketing software company founded in 2008 by Victoria Ransom and Alain Chuard in Redwood City, California. Its platform let brands create, optimize, and measure their presence across social networks — running branded promotions, sweepstakes, contests, and coupons plus page management, advertising, messaging, and analytics across Facebook, Twitter, Pinterest, and YouTube. Backed by the Facebook Fund, Summit Partners, Accel Partners, and Founders Fund, Wildfire was acquired by Google in 2012 and folded into Google's advertising products (DoubleClick); the standalone product was wound down by 2014. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of uncork-capital and is retained as a historical record — the company operates no independent public API surface today.

companies.name: Xtract
companies.description: Xtract was a social-intelligence analytics company (xtract.fi / xtract.com) that refined social interaction, behaviour, and demographic data from telecom operators into detailed subscriber profiles through its Social Links platform, powering churn prevention, product marketing, customer acquisition, and demographics prediction. A Creandum portfolio company now listed as exited; its websites are offline and no public API surface exists.

companies.name: ZipDial
companies.description: ZipDial was a Bangalore, India based mobile marketing and analytics startup founded in 2010 that pioneered "missed call" engagement, letting consumers interact with brands and campaigns by giving a toll-free number a missed call rather than paying for a call or SMS. It was acquired by Twitter in January 2015 and its standalone product was subsequently wound down. The company was backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups) among other investors. As of this enrichment pass the original company is defunct and no longer operates a developer program or public API; the zipdial.com domain now resolves to an unrelated general-interest content/news aggregation site with no developer, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record.

companies.name: Comprehend
companies.description: Comprehend Systems, Inc. was a clinical-trials software company that built SaaS analytics for the life-sciences industry. Its flagship product, Comprehend Clinical, let clinical data managers and executives monitor studies and make real-time decisions across multiple source systems without moving the underlying data. The company raised a Lightspeed Venture Partners Series B in 2014 and was acquired by Saama Technologies in 2019, after which the standalone Comprehend product and the comprehend.com domain were retired. This API Evangelist profile is a Lightspeed portfolio lead; the company is defunct as an independent entity and publishes no live developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs.

companies.name: DWL
companies.description: DWL Inc. was an enterprise software company founded in 1996 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, with significant engineering and operations in Toronto, Ontario. DWL built customer data integration (CDI) middleware — its flagship product, DWL Customer, was a real-time master data hub that consolidated fragmented customer records from across banking, insurance, telecommunications, and retail systems into a single authoritative view, and served that view back to operational applications through a transaction-oriented services layer. Backed by Insight Venture Partners, AGF Investments, Nationwide Mutual Capital, Royal Trust, and Stone Point Capital, DWL was acquired by IBM in August 2005 to fill the CDI gap in IBM's information-management stack. DWL Customer was rebranded IBM WebSphere Customer Center and subsequently folded into IBM InfoSphere Master Data Management. DWL has not operated as an independent company for two decades, never published a public developer program or API, and the dwl.com domain now redirects to ibm.com. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

companies.name: HNC
companies.description: HNC Software Inc. was a San Diego-based predictive-software company founded in 1986 that built neural-network and decision-management systems for credit-card and workers-compensation fraud detection, customer analytics, and profitability management across financial services, insurance, telecommunications, and retail. Its flagship Falcon product screened a large share of the world's payment-card transactions for fraud. HNC was an early Battery Ventures investment, went public in 1995, and was acquired by Fair Isaac (FICO) in May 2002; it no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no current developer or API surface.

companies.name: Dimensional Modeling
companies.description: A data modeling technique used in data warehousing that structures data into fact tables containing measurable metrics and dimension tables containing descriptive attributes, optimized for query performance and business intelligence reporting. Organizations use it to track key metrics, identify trends, and optimize business outcomes.

companies.name: Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology
companies.description: The Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology (FCSM) is an interagency committee dedicated to improving the quality of Federal statistics. FCSM is hosted under the federal Statistical Policy Office and does not publish a public developer API.

companies.name: Infinity Platform
companies.description: Infinity Platform is an index for tracking platform offerings branded with the Infinity name across data management, analytics, and integration services. This index is a placeholder for cataloging APIs from vendors that operate Infinity-branded platforms.

companies.name: Nugit
companies.description: Nugit is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Qube Horizon
companies.description: Qube Horizon is a platform described as offering project management, resource allocation, and analytics services. No public website or API documentation could be verified at the time of this entry, so no APIs are listed below.

companies.name: Sentieo
companies.description: Sentieo is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: Streambase
companies.description: Streambase is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: big-data. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

companies.name: SUMIF
companies.description: SUMIF is a company profile entry under research. No confirmed public API or developer documentation has been identified at this time. The name may refer to a data analytics or spreadsheet tooling company.

companies.name: Write Ahead Log
companies.description: A Write-Ahead Log (WAL) is a standard technique in database systems where changes are first recorded to a sequential log file before being applied to the actual data files. It ensures durability and crash recovery by guaranteeing that committed transactions can be reconstructed from the log even if the system fails during a write operation.

companies.name: Apache Spark
companies.description: Open-source unified analytics engine for large-scale data processing with built-in modules for streaming, SQL, machine learning and graph processing.

companies.name: Partitioning
companies.description: Partitioning is a data and systems concept used to divide databases, tables, storage, or workloads into smaller, more manageable pieces for performance, scalability, and operational reasons.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

companies.name: ACID
companies.description: ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) is a set of properties that guarantee database transactions are processed reliably even in the face of errors, power failures, or system crashes. These four properties ensure that data remains accurate and consistent, making ACID compliance a fundamental requirement for relational databases, distributed systems, and financial APIs.

companies.name: Amazon Scraper API
companies.description: REST/JSON API for extracting structured Amazon product, search, and batch data across 20 marketplaces, with key-based authentication, official SDKs, a CLI, and a local MCP server. Operated independently under the ChocoData namespace; not affiliated with Amazon.com, Inc.

companies.name: Apstal
companies.description: AI-first website analytics and visitor tracking platform that replaces traditional dashboards with a natural-language chatbot interface, offering conversational analytics, cookieless tracking, session replays, and heatmaps. Programmatic access is provided through a hosted MCP server exposing analytics tools.

companies.name: Azure Databricks
companies.description: Azure Databricks is an Apache Spark-based analytics platform optimized for Microsoft Azure. It provides a collaborative workspace for data engineers, data scientists, and analysts to work together on big data and machine learning workloads.

companies.name: Boycott Israeli Consumer Goods Dataset
companies.description: The Boycott Israeli Consumer Goods Dataset, maintained by TechForPalestine, is a version-controlled, golden-source repository collating consumer boycott and alternative product data into a single consumable dataset. The project aggregates data from authoritative sources including the Who Profits Research Center, the BDS Movement boycott guide, and the AFSC profiteering company list. Data is stored as YAML and exported in CSV and JSON formats for integration into software products and services.

companies.name: Cloud Storage and Data Acquisition
companies.description: Cloud Storage and Data Acquisition is a topic profile in the API Evangelist Network covering APIs and tooling for ingesting, moving, and persisting bulk and streaming data into cloud-resident storage. It groups object storage services, data-lake foundations, managed ingestion pipelines, change-data-capture connectors, transfer appliances, and data-broker APIs that provide source material for cloud-storage workloads. The topic is intended as an entry point for developers and architects evaluating how data lands in cloud storage from on-premises systems, SaaS APIs, IoT devices, public data sources, and partner exchanges.

companies.name: Data Commons
companies.description: Data Commons is an open knowledge graph initiative led by Google that aggregates and harmonizes the world's public data into a single graph, making global statistical data simple to explore, query, and integrate through REST, Python, BigQuery, web component, and MCP interfaces.

companies.name: Data Modeling
companies.description: Data Modeling is the discipline of designing structured representations of data to organize information, define relationships, and govern how data is stored, accessed, and managed. It spans conceptual, logical, and physical models across relational, dimensional, NoSQL, graph, and data vault paradigms, supported by standards and tools from the OMG, DAMA, Erwin, PowerDesigner, dbt, and modern data modeling platforms.

companies.name: Data Models
companies.description: Data Models are structured representations of entities, attributes, and relationships that define how data is stored, accessed, and exchanged. The landscape spans relational, hierarchical, network, object, document, graph, key-value, columnar, and event-sourced models, plus shared semantic models like Schema.org, FIBO, FHIR, ISO 20022, and W3C RDF/OWL.

companies.name: Data Quality Standards
companies.description: Data Quality Standards is the landscape of frameworks, standards, and tools used to define and measure the accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and timeliness of data. It spans ISO/IEC 25012 and ISO 8000, the DAMA-DMBOK data quality dimensions, EDM Council DCAM, and open source and commercial tooling like Great Expectations, Soda, dbt tests, Monte Carlo, and Anomalo.

companies.name: Data Warehouse Schemas
companies.description: Data Warehouse Schemas is the landscape of analytical schema patterns used to organize fact and dimension data for business intelligence and reporting. It spans star, snowflake, and galaxy schemas, the Kimball dimensional modeling methodology, the Inmon Corporate Information Factory, Data Vault 2.0, and modern lakehouse table formats like Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, and Apache Hudi.

companies.name: Database Schema Design
companies.description: Database Schema Design is the practice of defining the tables, columns, data types, constraints, indexes, and relationships that make up a database. It applies to relational, document, key-value, columnar, and graph stores, and is supported by ER tooling, schema-as-code formats like DBML and Prisma, migration tools like Liquibase and Flyway, and emerging schema registries for streaming and document data.

companies.name: Lakehouse Architecture
companies.description: Lakehouse Architecture is a data architecture paradigm that combines the best features of data lakes and data warehouses, providing ACID transactions, schema enforcement, and governance on low-cost storage with support for both business intelligence and machine learning workloads.

companies.name: Normalization
companies.description: Normalization is a data management concept used in database design and data processing to reduce data redundancy and improve data integrity. In databases, normalization organizes columns and tables to minimize duplication. In data processing, it refers to transforming data into a standard format for consistency and comparability. This index tracks normalization as a concept within the API Evangelist Network rather than a specific vendor or product API.

companies.name: Relational Data Modeling
companies.description: Relational data modeling is a database design approach that organizes data into tables (relations) with rows and columns, establishing relationships between tables through primary and foreign keys to ensure data integrity and minimize redundancy. This index covers leading platforms, tools, and APIs for relational data modeling including ER diagram tools, schema design platforms, DDL generation services, and database design automation.

companies.name: Sketches
companies.description: Sketches are probabilistic data structures used in computing and data engineering to approximate answers to queries over large data streams with controlled error bounds and dramatically reduced memory requirements. Common sketches include Count-Min Sketch (frequency estimation), HyperLogLog (cardinality estimation), Bloom Filter (membership testing), and T-Digest (quantile estimation). APIs in this domain include sketch-native databases like Apache DataSketches, Redis probabilistic data structures, and cloud analytics services that implement sketch algorithms for real-time analytics, approximate query processing, and streaming analytics.

companies.name: Taxi - Describe How Your APIs and Data Relate
companies.description: Taxi is an open-source language (Apache 2.0) for describing APIs, data models, and how data relates across an entire ecosystem. TaxiQL is a declarative query language that lets consumers define the data they want while Taxi handles orchestration across REST APIs, databases, Kafka topics, gRPC services, and S3 buckets. Taxi eliminates manual integration code by using semantic type annotations to automatically discover data paths and adapt to evolving API schemas.

companies.name: Thordata
companies.description: Proxy network and web-data-collection platform offering SERP API, Web Scraper API, Web Unlocker, Scraping Browser, and residential/mobile/ISP/datacenter proxy infrastructure. Provides HTTP APIs with Bearer-key and proxy-gateway authentication plus a documentation-index llms.txt for agent consumption.

companies.name: UN Comtrade
companies.description: United Nations international trade statistics database with a REST API for accessing import/export data, commodity trade flows, and bilateral trade statistics. Covers over 200 reporting countries and territories with data spanning goods and services trade classified by HS, SITC, and other commodity codes.
